Implement LLD 039.6: durable, canonical Brain run admission that distinguishes blocked capacity from provider failures.

## Architecture decision

- The Run Admission Durable Object is the single persisted owner of rate counters and concurrency leases.
- Admission policy requires canonical user, workspace, thread, and run-attempt identities; no client-fingerprint fallback remains.
- The exact run-attempt owns its idempotent lease. `RUN_ADMISSION_BLOCKED` carries typed admission metadata rather than provider semantics.
- Policy, transport, and orchestration are focused runtime collaborators.

## Changed / deleted paths

Changed: controller integration, `RunAdmissionLimiter`, admission policy/client/service collaborators, focused runtime tests, and policy inventory.

Deleted: legacy service-layer admission implementation/tests and fingerprint scope helper/tests.

## Review repair

Added direct Durable Object contract coverage for concurrent different-thread admission, deterministic constrained-workspace blocking, and exact-lease-only release. This closes the prior gap where only mocked policy/client paths were tested.

## Lifecycle-first evidence

### User-visible symptom

Capacity-blocked work could be admitted inconsistently or appear as a provider failure.

### Full affected lifecycle

Chat request -> canonical identity validation -> persisted rate admission -> persisted concurrency lease -> Brain/RunEngine dispatch -> runtime terminal settlement -> exact lease release.

### Canonical owner

The Run Admission Durable Object owns persisted rate counters and leases; Brain runtime helpers only compute policy and transport typed decisions.

### Violated invariant

A blocked run must not acquire partial ownership or use provider-failure semantics; a terminal run attempt must settle only its own lease.

### Architectural root cause

The prior service was a disabled no-op with client-fingerprint fallback, and its limiter contract did not expose run-attempt-owned capacity decisions.

### Duplicate authority or fallback removed

Removed the no-op admission path, old service-layer owner, and client-fingerprint fallback. No legacy path is retained.

### Boundary regression test

Focused Durable Object tests prove two threads can acquire within workspace policy, a constrained sibling is deterministically blocked, and releasing a non-owner does not free the occupying lease.

### Lifecycle/conformance regression test

Brain focused admission tests (8), Brain lint/typecheck, import-boundary, and rebuild-governance gates pass locally. Terminal-event lease-release integration is revalidated after the required 039.3 runtime settlement dependency lands.

## Proof

- Brain focused admission tests: 8 passed
- Brain lint and typecheck passed
- `pnpm check:boundaries` passed
- `pnpm gate:rebuild-governance` passed (24 migration-safety and 13 governance tests)
- `git diff --check` passed

## Merge independence

This PR is otherwise independent of 039.4/039.5 secure API and of Web slices; it does not modify ExecutionService, secure API, or Web.

## Remaining integration

Hard dependency: PR #392 (039.3 runtime interrupt and terminal settlement) must merge first. This PR must then be refreshed against `dev` without rewriting history, and terminal-event lease-release integration revalidated. Do not merge while #392 is open.

## Temporary mechanism deletion criteria

None. No fallback, compatibility lane, or temporary admission mechanism is retained.

## Risks / rollback

Forward-only: missing canonical identities now fail explicitly. Revert the two PR commits only if emergency rollback is required; doing so restores the unsafe no-op/fallback behavior.

## Red-flag evidence

This reduces the admission portion of RF-032: capacity is persisted and typed instead of being mislabelled as a provider failure. It does not close RF-032, RF-008, RF-017, or RF-027; secure-run isolation, control-plane separation, contextual action routing, and broader policy consolidation remain owned by their respective slices.'

Plan 039.4 establishes the secure API workspace/run-attempt sandbox lease boundary. It removes unscoped default sandbox authority and preserves infrastructure outcomes without relabelling them as provider failures.

- One runtime/plugin registry is held per workspace/run-attempt; distinct workspaces never share mutable plugin state.
- Serialized leases share a workspace mutation queue; explicit read-only leases may run concurrently.
- Active entries and cancellation use `(leaseId, taskId)` only.
- `sandbox_unavailable` is a typed execution status. Exit 137 releases the matching lease; the API emits 503 and persists exactly one replacement lease.
- Readiness is awaited before task execution. A 15-minute bounded lease matches Cloudflare Sandbox ephemeral lifecycle guidance; replacements are capped at one generation.

## Changed paths

- `apps/secure-agent-api/src/{ports,adapters,core,api,schemas,conformance}/**`
- No Brain callers or other Plan 039 slices changed.
- Deleted paths: none.

# Checkpoint implementation contracts

Implementation invariants and failure modes. Start with the [domain model](../architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md), [scenarios](../architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md), and [security/privacy overview](../security-and-privacy.md) for architecture and user-facing behavior. This reference holds engineering constraints rather than another domain overview.

Repository paths in code spans are relative to the repository root unless stated otherwise.

### Session Strategy (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/`)

The CLI uses a manual-commit strategy for managing session data and checkpoints. There is no `Strategy` interface: `*ManualCommitStrategy` (`manual_commit.go`, constructed by `NewManualCommitStrategy()`) is the only implementation and callers hold it concretely. `strategy.go` holds the types its methods take and return.

#### Strategy Methods

`*ManualCommitStrategy`'s main entry points:

- `SaveStep()` - Record a turn-end step in session state (files touched, their blob hashes, step count); writes no git objects
- `ListPendingCheckpoints()` - List pending checkpoints (see the note below: there is no restore path)

**There is no restore path.** `Rewind()`, `PreviewRewind()`, `CanRewind()` and
their helpers were removed once the `rewind` commands went and nothing outside
tests still called them. Nothing in the strategy writes checkpoint contents back
over the worktree, and re-adding that is a product decision, not a refactor.

What survives is everything that reads a checkpoint without touching working
files. `PreviewNextCheckpoint()` (the next checkpoint's contents, from session
state) and `ListPendingCheckpoints()` / `ListLogsOnlyPendingCheckpoints()` feed
`checkpoint list --pending`. `RestoreLogsOnly()` writes a checkpoint's session
logs into the agent's session directory — logs only, never worktree files — and
feeds `entire resume` and `entire trail resume`. The type they return is
`PendingCheckpoint`, and it covers both shapes that listing contains: a
subagent task record on session state, not yet condensed onto
`entire/checkpoints/v1`, **or** a logs-only resume point — a commit on the
current branch whose logs *are* already condensed there, listed so the
transcript can be restored. "Pending" names the listing, not a promise that the
work is un-condensed. Either way you can list it and resume from it, but the
CLI cannot restore working files from it. The `--pending` flag, the command
paths, and the `--json` shape are unchanged by that rename. Next-checkpoint
preview elements are additional array elements marked `is_next_checkpoint`;
every other row keeps its key set.

#### How It Works

The manual-commit strategy (`manual_commit*.go`) does not modify the active branch - no commits are created on the working branch. Instead it:

- **Writes no git objects between commits.** At turn end `SaveStep` records the step in session state only: `StepCount`, `FilesTouched`, and `TouchedFileHashes` (path → git blob hex of the file as the agent left it, hashed with `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` so clean filters apply exactly as `git add` would; `""` records a deletion; an absent entry means "unknown, fall back to the path name"). Hashing runs outside the session lock. Symlinks and other non-regular entries are never hashed. Gitignored paths and submodule gitlinks (mode 160000 in HEAD or the index) never enter `FilesTouched` on any route (turn end, task-record completion, per-tool hooks, Codex child files, and the transcript extraction a mid-turn commit falls back to): `strategy.FilterTrackableChanges` runs one `git check-ignore` batch plus pathspec-limited `git diff-index --cached --raw` (index entries that differ from HEAD, so an unchanged ancestor directory costs nothing) / `git ls-tree HEAD` (no `-r`) mode checks (each bounded by `gitrepo.PathClassificationBudget`, answers cached per process so a commit hook asks once per path across sessions), failing open, because a path no commit can carry would keep the session pending forever. Paths beneath a gitlink are dropped too: the gitlink query includes each path's ancestor directories, and a path with a gitlink ancestor is dropped before the ignore check. Edits inside a submodule are not tracked by the superproject's session; they belong to the nested repository, whose own session records them. `git check-ignore` fails a whole batch with exit 128 when it refuses one path (beneath a symlinked directory, or anything else it rejects). `gitrepo.IgnoredPaths` finds paths with a symlinked ancestor in process first (no-follow `Lstat` through the worktree root, once per ancestor) and never sends them to git; if a batch is still refused, it confirms with a probe path that git can answer at all and bisects the batch, so k refused paths among n cost O(k log n) processes. Refused paths are reported and dropped; the rest of the answers stand. If the probe fails too, the batch is an error and every path is kept. Deletions are never ignore-checked: a git-status deletion is of a tracked path, and `git check-ignore` reports a path whose deletion is staged. Transcript-extracted files (a commit before the session's first turn end) cannot be told apart from deletions, so a path HEAD tracks is exempt from the ignore check on that route too (`filterTrackableFiles`, via `gitrepo.PathsInHEAD`); the gitlink drop still applies. The staged listing (`getStagedFiles`, `git diff --cached --raw -z`) skips gitlinks too, so a staged submodule pointer never stamps a trailer. A step path that is neither in the worktree nor a recorded deletion is dropped from `FilesTouched` as a transcript-parsing phantom; an earlier step's missing file is kept (it may be stashed). See `strategy/touched_file_hashes.go`.
- **Linking is by name; carry-forward compares blob hashes** (`strategy/content_overlap.go`): a commit (or the staged index, in prepare-commit-msg) "contains the agent's work" when it carries any path in `FilesTouched` — modified, deleted, or new, whatever its content — except a new file at a path the session recorded as deleted. There is no hunk-level or blob comparison for linking. After a commit, a path stays in `FilesTouched` for carry-forward unless the commit took the recorded content, the commit and worktree agree on a different version (the human replaced it), or the commit deleted the path and the worktree lacks it too (a recorded hash is history, not remaining work). A worktree path that cannot be inspected (for example an unreadable parent directory) always counts in favour of keeping pending work. An unhashed path (a session from an older CLI, or one `MergeUnhashedFilesTouched` cleared) gets the same commit-versus-worktree comparison without the recorded-hash shortcut, and an uncommitted one drops only when it is absent from both the commit and the worktree (a path the commit still has but the worktree lacks is a pending deletion). A recorded deletion stays while it is pending — the commit tree still has the path and the worktree still lacks it, even if the commit modified the path — so the later commit that deletes it links; it drops once a commit removes the path or the file is re-created.
- **One pending-work predicate gates the lifecycle.** `State.HasPendingWork()` (steps, files touched, or task content; it ignores `FullyCondensed`) decides whether condensation, eager/session-end condensation, the orphan sweep (`isOrphanedSessionState`), the zombie sweep, `IsCondensableEndedSession`, and `entire doctor` treat a session as having uncondensed work. The zombie sweep, `IsCondensableEndedSession`, and doctor's ENDED classification also skip `FullyCondensed` sessions explicitly: re-condensing one resets its phase to IDLE while `FullyCondensed` stays set, so PostCommit's FullyCondensed+ENDED skip would stop matching. Do not re-key any of them on a git ref.
- **Supports multiple concurrent sessions** - each session's pending work lives in its own state file, so sessions in one worktree or across worktrees never share storage before condensation
- Condenses session logs to permanent `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on user commits
- Every path that builds a stored transcript sanitizes before redacting; the committed paths also externalize images in between, giving **sanitize → externalize images → redact**. Sanitization is the agent's optional `agent.TranscriptSanitizer` capability, applied via `agent.SanitizeTranscriptForStorage`; it strips non-portable agent state (Codex's encrypted reasoning payloads, the encrypted_content parts of multi-agent `agent_message` items, and compaction blobs, which are bound to the originating session and cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint). The three paths are the Stop write of the local working copy (`lifecycle.go` sanitizes before `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is written; that file is neither externalized nor redacted and never enters a git object as-is), post-commit condensation (`prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go`), and the Stop finalize full-session rewrite (`manual_commit_hooks.go`). Where all three steps run, order is load-bearing at each step: sanitizing first avoids externalizing images out of items about to be discarded (storing an asset whose referencing line disappears) and avoids redacting megabytes of ciphertext only to discard it — base64 is the pathological input for the entropy layer, so a large Codex rollout otherwise costs tens of seconds per Stop *and* per commit; externalizing before redaction is required because redaction would otherwise flag and destroy the high-entropy base64. Sanitization is idempotent, so downstream paths call it without knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is the store's belt-and-braces call). The agent's own transcript is never modified. Coupling to respect: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize` is a growth baseline compared against the size of the stored sanitized transcript (`storedTranscriptSize`, the `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` working copy) in `sessionHasNewContent` once a turn has ended, so it must be measured in the same sanitized (pre-externalization) coordinate — that is `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline`; using the raw size makes the comparison false forever and the session silently stops condensing.
- **Redaction cost and the two mechanisms that contain it.** Redaction dominates the Stop hook on a large session: it is ~99.7% of a transcript blob write (git object writing is milliseconds), and ~82% of that is the betterleaks regex ruleset. Two things keep it bounded, and both rest on redaction being **per-line and stateless** (`redact.redactJSONLLines`) — a rule that looked at neighbouring lines would silently break both:
  - `jsonlContentImpl` shards the line pass into ~1MiB byte-balanced groups across goroutines. Output is byte-identical to the sequential pass. Sharding is gated on an explicit `concurrencySafe` argument describing the **redactor**, not on which entry point was called: `String` is pure and opts in, while collector closures that accumulate into a shared map/slice pass `concurrencyUnsafeRedactor`. Shards are balanced by bytes rather than line count because transcripts mix short lines with occasional multi-MB tool results.
  - Whole-transcript redaction reuses the previous checkpoint's redacted output as a prefix and redacts only appended lines (`checkpoint/redact_cache.go`), turning a per-Stop cost of O(whole transcript) into O(appended). The stored prefix must always end immediately after a `\n`, which is what makes plain byte concatenation reproduce the full result; content with a partial trailing line is therefore never cached. Eligibility is keyed on `paths.TranscriptFileName` (`full.jsonl`), **not** a `.jsonl` suffix — `transcript.jsonl` is regenerated in full each checkpoint and `full.jsonl.001` chunks are not appended, so neither should qualify. Reuse requires the prefix bytes to still hash the same and `redactionFingerprint()` (CLI version + commit + `redact.ConfigFingerprint()`) to match, so a rewritten transcript, changed custom rules or scanner selection, or a CLI upgrade all fall back to a full redaction. Bump `configFingerprintVersion` in `redact/fingerprint.go` whenever the regex layers change behaviour, or stale output can be reused. The cache lives in the git common dir, resolved without caching from the explicit worktree root through `gitrepo.ResolveWorktreeMetadata`, never under `.entire/`, because anything in the metadata directory would be walked into the checkpoint tree and committed. Both whole-transcript paths are covered: condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite hold the transcript in memory and go through `checkpoint.RedactTranscriptCached`, keyed on a synthetic key carrying the session ID (`transcriptCacheKey`, so concurrent sessions never share an entry). The metadata-directory walk (`createRedactedBlobFromFile`) does not use the cache. Entries an older CLI cached under the real tree path are never read and are reclaimed by `entire clean`. The in-memory prefix is stored as a **file** in the cache dir, not a git blob: go-git deflates the whole payload before discovering the object exists (dotgit dedups the rename, not the compression), and above `agent.MaxChunkSize` the whole-transcript blob matches no chunk the store writes, so it would linger unreachable until `git gc` pruned it and silently reverted the cache to full redaction. Each store writes its payload under a new name and the entry last, so the entry's rename publishes the pair: a store that fails or is killed before then leaves the previous entry and its payload intact, and the next successful store deletes the key's other payloads. The entry also records the payload's length, and a payload of any other length (cache writes do not fsync, so a power loss can leave one empty) is not reused. `redactIncrementally` owns the whole-content fallback and takes the redactor as a parameter, so prefix and suffix cannot come from different pipelines; condensation and finalize share that pipeline by both routing through `redactSessionTranscript`. A per-subagent task transcript opts out with a nil repo: it is written once per task rather than appended across checkpoints.
- **Redaction counts ride with the redacted bytes.** `redact.JSONLBytes` returns `RedactedBytes` whose `Counts()` (`redact.Counts`) report placeholders written and matches per layer; `AlreadyRedacted` bytes carry none, which reads as unknown. Counting happens where a value is replaced (`redactRegions`, plus the key-context and credential-key placeholders in `redactLeafValue`), never during detection, so the probe scans `keyContextFindsMore` runs are not counted. On a spliced JSON line the replacements are what `applyJSONReplacements` wrote, since it rewrites every copy of a collected value, including copies in fields the walk skips; layer matches stay what the scanned values held. Each layer in `detectAllLayers` tags its regions with `tagFrom`; a layer added without a tag reports as `unattributed`. A line the structural fallback redacts a second time rolls its tally back first, and shards tally separately, so counts compose like the output: counts(A+B) = counts(A) + counts(B), which the prefix cache relies on. Its entry stores the prefix's counts and a reuse adds the suffix's; an entry without counts is not reused. The counts describe the stored `full.jsonl`, which is the whole session so far, so they accumulate across a session's checkpoints and summing those checkpoints counts earlier turns again. The tree writer stores the session transcript's counts as `Metadata.Redaction` and sums sessions into `CheckpointSummary.Redaction`, which stays nil when any session stored a transcript without counts. The finalize rewrite replaces a session's counts when its transcript changes, and keeps them when identical bytes arrive without counts. OPF passes do not count, and prompts, summaries, and subagent transcripts are not counted.
- Each committed session stores the (sanitized, redacted) transcript (`full.jsonl`, read by CLI resume/explain) plus a best-effort compact transcript (`transcript.jsonl`, generated via `transcript/compact`, which wraps the root `transcript` library's converters). For Claude Code, Cursor and Droid, conversion is a records adapter (`transcript/jsonl_records.go`) followed by the agent-agnostic fold (`transcript.Fold`), which is meant to be shared with the backend for live sessions; its output is byte-identical to the previous two-pass compactor except that an assistant line with empty content is now always skipped, checked against the copy in `transcript/legacy_oracle_test.go`. Like `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` stores the **full compacted session** on every checkpoint (via `compact.FullWithBoundary`), so each checkpoint is self-contained and the session survives a mid-history checkpoint being lost/reverted/rebased. This checkpoint's slice begins at the session metadata's `compact_transcript_start` (a line offset in compact-output coordinates, distinct from `checkpoint_transcript_start` which indexes raw `full.jsonl` lines); a nil/absent marker means a legacy delta-only `transcript.jsonl` (read from line 0). The marker rounds toward inclusion when a streaming message straddles the boundary, so the slice never drops this checkpoint's content but may repeat ≤1 merged line at its head. An agent that declares `compact_transcript` (external agents, `checkpoint/compact_agent.go`) compacts its own format instead: it gets the already-redacted bytes, its output is re-redacted, the marker is how many leading lines its compaction of the raw lines before `checkpoint_transcript_start` shares with the full output (so a line merged across the boundary stays in scope), and errors, a 5 s timeout (it runs inside the checkpoint ref lock), empty output or assets fall back to the built-in compactor; plugin stderr is never logged. Compact generation is best-effort and is skipped when the compacted output exceeds the 50MB blob cap (unlike `full.jsonl`, `transcript.jsonl` is not chunked — `full.jsonl` stays authoritative and the compact is regenerable). Both files are pushed with the v1 branch. The root `metadata.json` `sessions[].transcript` pointer keeps targeting `full.jsonl`; when the compact transcript was generated the session entry also carries a `compact_transcript` path pointing at `transcript.jsonl` (omitted otherwise) so external readers can locate it next to `full.jsonl`.
- **Subagent task records** - subagent work (Claude Code's Task tool) is captured as durable `session.TaskRecord` entries on session state, a pointer mid-turn (declared transcript path + labels; background launches record at launch, completions attach files/tokens/path exactly-once via `strategy.CompleteTaskRecord`, Factory Droid Workers upsert). Condensation materializes each record — declared path first, then (when the declared path is empty or cannot be opened) the agent's verified child-inventory resolution (`resolveInventoryTaskTranscripts` → `agent.ExtractWithSubagentInventory`; for Codex, a rollout whose `session_meta.id` matches the agent ID, so a parent committing mid-turn before its Stop refresh or a rollout archived after its path was recorded still resolves), then the agent-layout fallback, same sanitize → externalize → redact pipeline — into `tasks/<toolUseID>/{agent-<agentID>.jsonl, task.json}` inside the parent session's checkpoint (unavailable transcript → `task.json` with a stable path-free reason; the writer redacts `task.json`'s free-text `task_description` itself, since the record carries it verbatim); live records store transcript-so-far each condensation, completed records are removed after a successful write; a foreground subagent that commits its own work mid-run has no record when that commit condenses, so when files the subagent's transcript names are now in HEAD, its post-task also stores the completed record straight into the newest checkpoint condensed during the run whose `files_touched` include one of them (`strategy.AttachTaskToCheckpoint`, the `Tasks` write), and files it left uncommitted still complete a record in session state for the commit that later carries them; the run's checkpoints are the entries the turn's `TurnCheckpointIDs` gained past the pre-task snapshot, by position, because an amend appends its commit's existing ID again; a failed write waits in `PendingTaskAttachments`, which is not pending work, and each turn end retries it up to `maxTaskAttachmentRetries` times; this path keeps images inline because turn-end replaces the session's assets; a completed record whose usage was computed from its transcript (`TokenUsageFromTranscript`) gets that usage recounted from the raw transcript condensation stores, never lowering its API call count. `State.HasTaskContent()` feeds `State.HasPendingWork()`, so records-only sessions condense. Task-record completion, per-tool hooks, and Codex child-file merges add paths through `strategy.MergeUnhashedFilesTouched`, which drops any recorded hash for those paths so they fall back to name matching. Claude Code's post-todo hook writes nothing and is no longer installed (installs prune it); its subcommand stays registered so configs written by older CLIs keep working.
- Uses the `post-rewrite` Git hook to keep local session linkage aligned after amend/rebase rewrites
- Builds git trees in-memory using go-git plumbing APIs
- **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures log restore (`RestoreLogsOnly`) works after repo relocation or across machines.
- **Token usage scoping** - `SessionState.TokenUsage` is the session-wide total used by `entire status`; `SessionState.CheckpointTokenUsage` is the pending checkpoint delta since the last condensation. Checkpoint token metadata must stay scoped to `SessionState.TokenStart()` (`TokenTranscriptStart`) or the pending checkpoint delta. `TokenTranscriptStart` is set only where tokens are stored or carried over, and moves back only when a condensation or attach records the end of a transcript that got shorter (rewritten or compacted): condensation (`AdvanceCheckpointWindow`, which leaves it alone when the transcript could not be read), attach (`ConsumeAttachTokenWindow`) and adopt (`SetTokenStart`); unlike `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, carry-forward and adopt never move it back and the turn-end advance after a mid-turn commit leaves it behind, so a checkpoint whose displayed window restarts at 0 still counts each token once and a mid-turn commit's post-commit tail lands in the next checkpoint. `session attach` counts from it too and records the transcript end afterwards (`strategy.AttachTokenUsage` / `ConsumeAttachTokenWindow`); adopt carries the source's offset, pending delta and subagent baseline because the retired source never condenses again. Attach sets `SessionState.TokenUsage` to the whole-transcript total for an idle or ended session, or for a running one whose agent exited (or, when liveness can't be checked, went quiet past `StuckActiveThreshold`); a running session keeps the hooks' total (its turn's Stop adds that turn) plus the cumulative subagent total; if a hook changed token state while attach waited at its prompt, attach leaves token state alone. Cursor tokens come only from stop-hook payloads, while Copilot CLI can also backfill full-session totals from `session.shutdown`. Condensation's full-session backfill recompute runs with `subagentsDir=""` and so drops `SubagentTokens`; `fillMissingSubagentTokensFrom` refills it from the already-rescoped `state.CheckpointTokenUsage`. The checkpoint-scoped recompute (`calculateLiveTranscriptTokenUsage`, counting from `TokenStart()`) reads the still-available subagent transcripts only when no checkpoint-scoped subagent total already exists, the agent supports that extraction, and a real subagent directory exists. It subtracts `SubagentTokensBaseline` for checkpoint metadata and keeps the cumulative snapshot on `state.TokenUsage` so the reset advances the next baseline; an empty delta stays nil. The scan is substantially more expensive for subagent-heavy sessions, so every gate is load-bearing. The store sums those scoped values across a checkpoint's sessions via `types.AddTokenUsage` (the single token-summing primitive — do not hand-roll another; a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place).
- **Child-session tokens** - Subagents that run as sessions of their own (OpenCode child sessions, whose agent implements `agent.ChildSessionSubagents`; Factory AI Droid Workers) never appear in the parent's transcript or its subagent snapshot. Their usage is credited once, in the same session-state mutation that completes the task record, to `SessionState.ChildSessionTokens`, a summed total kept apart from the replace-on-snapshot `TokenUsage.SubagentTokens`. The SessionEnd sweep's completion of a still-running child credits too, with the call's start recorded as unknown (its record start may be the hook's clock), so it counts the child's usage so far and a later stop adds nothing. `CreditedChildCalls` (bounded, survives condensation) keys credits like completion-record keying, an unknown start on either side matching, so a stop repeated after condensation is not credited again. A child's task entry is not recounted at condensation (`taskUsageRecountable`), so it shows the credited figure. Checkpoint metadata adds `PendingChildSessionTokens()` (rebaselined by `RebaselineSubagentTokens`) to its subagent total in `resolveCondensedTokenUsage` and `AttachTokenUsage`; displays use `SessionState.TotalTokenUsage()`.
- Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees). ID-based condensation (`CondenseSessionByID`, used by sweep and doctor) stamps the target state's recorded `Branch`, even if empty or its worktree was removed. Turn end refreshes this value only from the session's recorded home worktree, capturing mid-turn branch switches; absent hooks or unavailable/foreign homes preserve the last recorded value. It resolves current and recorded worktree metadata without Git subprocesses and opens the recorded `WorktreePath` only when its validated registration and Git common directory identify the current repository; a missing, unregistered, replaced, or unreadable home falls back to the caller repository (an unreadable one with a Warn log), and only errors resolving the caller's own worktree are returned. Ordinary post-commit condensation still uses the committing repository's HEAD branch.
- **Commit-to-session linking is identity-first** (`strategy/session_identity.go`): identity comes from `SessionState.Owner`, the `proclive.Identity` that `captureSessionOwner` already records on every turn start (first non-transient ancestor — proclive skips shells, `entire` itself, and the Go toolchain, so a human commit typed in the same terminal never matches). Commit hooks snapshot their own ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and match every candidate against it in memory (`Ancestry.Depth`) — one hostname/boot-id/proc walk per commit, not one per session state — linking the commit to the session whose agent process is an ancestor — in any worktree (nearest ancestor wins, so a nested agent beats the outer agent that spawned it, and only a tie at equal depth falls to the latest interaction; host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse and cross-machine matches; Windows cannot introspect and falls back to worktree matching). The identity match is UNIONED with the worktree-matched set, never a replacement: a commit condenses every session with pending content in its worktree. The exception is a worktree where no session is homed: there the fallback's sessions belong to other worktrees, so once ancestry identifies the committer they are dropped, and a session from elsewhere joins only through its record of this worktree; a commit with no identified committer (Windows, no recorded owner) still links the fallback's sessions. Any session matched outside its home worktree is guest-linked — whether identity-matched or selected by the pre-existing single-worktree fallback — and is condensed and linked without mutating worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`) from the foreign worktree (`isSessionHomeWorktree`). Worktree matching is always computed (it is the sole mechanism for commits with no agent ancestry): imported sessions never link, and multi-worktree ambiguity is filtered to recently-interacting sessions (15 min) before declining. This deliberately turns some former ambiguity declines into a best-candidate link; `recentSessionWindow` is a correctness tradeoff because a session in a long-running build or tool call can age out and leave the other recent worktree to win. **The recency shortcuts trust only the agent's own commit** (`commitProvenance`): the no-TTY / `commit_linking=always` fast path stamps, and PostCommit condenses, ACTIVE and live-task sessions without an overlap check. A session is foreign to a commit when its recorded owner is alive, absent from an ancestry walk that reached init (`Ancestry.Excludes`; a walk cut off by `maxAncestryDepth` or a failed lookup proves nothing), and not named by any agent's caller-session variable; a foreign session skips the fast path, links only on staged-file overlap (task records and transcript growth do not count), and condenses only on committed-file overlap; for an IDLE session a fresh live task whose running subagent wrote a staged or committed file (`liveTaskFilesInCommit`) counts as that overlap. No owner, a dead or unverifiable owner, and Windows keep the shortcuts. The stderr hint naming `entire session adopt` fires only from the commit-linking path, and only when identity matching could not rescue the commit either. **Squashes inherit their trailers**: when SQUASH_MSG exists in the per-worktree git dir, prepare-commit-msg copies its `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers into the message only when a staged path is one a commit Git recorded in that message changed (`inheritSquashedCheckpointTrailers`); a squash committed with `-m` reports `message`, not `squash`, and an abandoned squash's stale message is ignored. Inherited trailers are links: matching still runs and a session with pending work is stamped after them, and PostCommit condenses only into the trailer without a checkpoint (`pickCondensationTarget`, the last such one, since the stamp is appended) among those prepare did not record as inherited (`recordInheritedTrailers` / `takeInheritedTrailers`, a marker in the per-worktree git dir tied to the commit's parent), rechecks that target's existence before writing, and refuses to write into a checkpoint the session did not stamp or is not amending (`stampedByAnotherCommit`). **Redone commits inherit too** (`inheritReplacedCommitsTrailers`, `replacedCommits`): the dropped work is read from HEAD's reflog (per-worktree `logs/HEAD`, tail-bounded), skipping resets that did not move HEAD; dropped commits are those only the old tip reaches (`git rev-list <tip>` excluding HEAD, remotes and every branch not pointing at the tip); a dropped commit is inherited when every staged file it changed matches the old tip byte for byte; commits since the reset keep the redo open only if each redid dropped work; an amend fold (`reset --soft` + `commit --amend`) inherits too, recorded against HEAD's parent. Staged content, mode and deletions come from one rename-free `git diff --cached --raw` of the commit index (`stagedBlobs`, keeping the hook's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`). A redone path is **held** (`redo.paths`) only when the newest dropped commit that changed it carries a checkpoint that is not deleted and exists in this clone's store (`capturedCheckpoints`) and the staged mode matches; inheriting stays permissive. A commit whose every staged path is held gets no fresh trailer; otherwise session matching sees only the redo's other staged paths (`redo.others`, the same rename-free view). Held paths ride in the inherited-trailers marker; a commit that ends up with no stamped trailer (a pure redo, or a partial redo whose other files are no session's work) drops them from the worktree's sessions' `FilesTouched` where the commit holds the recorded content (`reconcileRedoneFiles`), while a stamped trailer is condensed with overlap judged without the redo, so it always resolves. Under `go test`, `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree` refuse to open outside the temp root so non-isolated tests fail loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into a real repo.
- **Reclaiming sessions whose agent vanished** - not every agent fires a session-end hook, and any agent can be killed before its hook runs, so a session can be left un-finalized forever. `SessionState.Owner` — the same fingerprint commit linking matches above — is captured at every turn start by `captureSessionOwner`, and `State.OwnerExited()` reports it gone via `proclive.Check`. `finalizeExitedSessions` sweeps those inside `entire doctor` and `__sweep_sessions`, ending them exactly as a clean stop would. **Not `entire status`**: status is a read-only observer — it reads through `StateStore.ListReadOnly` and reports a dead-owner session as `exited` without finalizing it, because asking what is happening must not change what is happening. Status therefore shows such a session until doctor or the sweeper reaches it. **`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case; only already-finalized sessions are excluded, per the shared `State.IsEnded()` predicate. Liveness is Unknown on Windows and for cross-host state, where behaviour degrades to the `StuckActiveThreshold` timeout. Because the sweep runs inside interactive commands, its eager condensing is capped by `sweepCondenseBudget` across the whole sweep: every candidate is always marked ENDED (a single atomic rename — that is what stops `entire status` reporting it as live), while condensing runs only while the budget lasts, so a multi-day backlog drains over successive invocations instead of stalling one. Skipping a condense is the existing fail-open path — PostCommit retries, and `doctor` reports the session as "ended with uncondensed checkpoint data".
- **Snapshot checkpoints** (`strategy.CreateSnapshotCheckpoint`, hidden `entire checkpoint create`) - for sessions that change no files, which otherwise never get a checkpoint: turn end skips `SaveStep` when nothing changed, so session end finds no steps and `PrepareSessionEndCondensation` marks the session condensed without writing. A session with pending file changes is refused (`ErrPendingFileChanges`); its next commit checkpoints that work. Pending changes come from `resolveFilesTouched`, not `FilesTouched` alone: most agents emit no per-tool file events, so `FilesTouched` stays empty until `SaveStep` at turn end, and an edit earlier in the current turn is visible only in the live transcript (paths outside the worktree, such as an agent's plan files, are dropped). An edit made through a shell command rather than an edit tool is seen by neither until turn end, so a snapshot in that turn is allowed and overlaps the next commit's checkpoint. The snapshot runs `CondenseSession` inside `MutateSessionState` and returns `ErrMutationSkip`: the lock keeps it from racing a commit's condensation over the session's redaction prefix cache, where an unlocked writer could delete the payload the other writer's entry names and cost the next checkpoint a full redaction; never saving keeps the session's window untouched, so repeated snapshots each cover the session from the same start and overlap one another (as carry-forward checkpoints already do; `tokens profile` discloses overlap). It passes `failOnRedactionError` (a snapshot exists for its transcript, so a redaction failure is an error rather than the hook paths' drop-and-continue). No skill telemetry is emitted, since unsaved state never marks the events persisted.
- **Session-end hooks that run under a host deadline** - an agent whose session-end hook fires inside its own shutdown may be killed part-way through. Such agents declare `agent.SessionEndBudgeter` (Codex: 3s cap, process tree killed on expiry). The budget bounds **only** the eager condense in `endSessionNow`, so the cheap step that un-sticks the session is never the one given up on; it is set below the host cap with enough headroom for the shell wrapper and binary load, which happen before Entire's own clock starts. Unbounded is not the same as guaranteed, though: mark-ended runs under `MutateSessionState`, whose flock acquire blocks, so a concurrent condense holding the lock can push it past the cap and get the tree killed — the exited-owner sweep above is the backstop. The bound is best-effort (condensation doesn't poll ctx between stages), and being cut off costs duplication rather than data: an incomplete condense leaves `FullyCondensed` false and PostCommit retries, except in the window between the v1 checkpoint write and the state save, where the checkpoint is already committed and PostCommit mints a second one over the same transcript range.
- **Turn-end finalize runs under the turn-end hook's deadline.** `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` rewrites every checkpoint of the turn, and each rewrite can fetch from the remote. The per-fetch memos catch a dead network but not a slow one, so the store open and the write loop run under a deadline of `processStart` plus `agent.TurnEndBudgetWithin` the agent's turn-end hook timeout (the host limit it declares through `agent.TurnEndHookTimeouter`; built-in agents that declare none, or a non-positive one, get `defaultTurnEndHookTimeout`, and those that declare none must be listed in `turnEndHookTimeoutFallbacks` with their reason (`TestTurnEndHookTimeoutLedger`); external agents always take the default). The deadline is checked when finalize starts and during the network phase, never part-way through local work: if it has already passed at entry, finalize does not start, since nothing it prepared could be written and its time is the headroom for saving state; once started, transcript preparation and redaction are never interrupted, though their time counts against the budget. Cut-off checkpoints are reported once, as capture degradation, not also as finalize errors. Checkpoints the deadline or a host cancellation cuts off stay in `TurnCheckpointIDs`, and so does every checkpoint when finalize exits before writing for any other reason (no or unreadable transcript, an unflushed late transcript, a repository or checkpoint store that fails to open, a degraded scanner), so a repeated Stop in the same turn retries them; otherwise turn start clears the IDs and they keep their provisional transcripts for good. A checkpoint whose write fails is counted as an error and also kept, while the checkpoints written alongside it are dropped; an ID that is not a valid checkpoint ID is counted but not kept, since no retry can write it. All of these set `CaptureDegradedAt`, which `entire status` reports. Only a write loop in which every checkpoint is written clears the IDs.
- **Base commit follows HEAD** - if the user does stash/pull/rebase (HEAD changes without a commit), `syncBaseCommitToHead` moves `BaseCommit` to the new HEAD; amends and rebases remap it through `remapSessionForRewrite`. No git data moves with it, because pending work lives only in session state.
- **Legacy shadow branches** - older CLIs wrote `entire/<commit[:7+]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` shadow branches at turn end. Nothing reads them, and nothing deletes them automatically. `entire doctor` reports the strict shape (`checkLegacyShadowBranches`) and deletes it under `--force` or a confirmed prompt, which is the recommended remedy; plain `entire clean` deletes the strict shape too, but it also clears the state of every session based on HEAD, which is the only record of pending agent work, so its confirmation lists those sessions and branches; `entire clean --all` (behind its confirmation) and uninstall also delete the bare `entire/<hex>` form, which a human short-SHA branch can look like. Every deletion goes through `DeleteBranchCLI` (`git branch -D`), which refuses a branch checked out in a worktree.
- **Orphaned session state cleanup** (`isOrphanedSessionState`) - `listAllSessionStates` deletes a state only when it is ended (`State.IsEnded`: ENDED phase or `EndedAt` stamped), never condensed (no `LastCheckpointID`), and has no pending work (`!HasPendingWork()`). Legacy empty-phase records normalize to IDLE when listed, so they are no longer deleted here (they previously were) and instead remain until `StaleSessionThreshold` expiry. An IDLE never-condensed state is either a live session between turns — a read-only turn, or the turn right after a linked commit — or belongs to the exited-owner finalizer when `OwnerExited` is true. The store is listed by every worktree's hooks, so deleting either shape re-initialised live sessions from zero or erased the ownership evidence before `finalizeExitedSessions` could end the session cleanly. IDLE states therefore remain for lifecycle finalization or `StaleSessionThreshold` expiry.
- PrePush hook can push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch alongside user pushes
- **Checkpoint replay preserves independent sessions**: match sessions by ID, update their paths after assigning slots, and rebuild totals with the normal writer. Conflicting edits stop before refs move and leave the queued generation intact. Skip an old commit sequence only when its combined change is already present. During deletion reconciliation, remove the deleted checkpoint from both sides of each local change before replay.
- **Git-refs push failures stay fail-soft**: confirmed remote policy/hook rejections skip fetch/replay so repeated blocked pushes do not rewrite local commits. Other failures still attempt recovery; failed fetch/replay preserves the original push cause, not a presumed divergence. Confirmed remote rejections print one bounded example per flush with Git's line breaks intact (log errors remain single-line), without additional secret redaction of the remote's diagnostic output; unsuccessful refs stay queued. See [ref-backend pre-push flow](../architecture/ref-checkpoint-backend.md#pre-push-flow).
- **The git-refs per-ref fallback is bounded**: it runs under a `checkpointFlushBudget` context deadline and stops after `maxConsecutiveRefPushFailures` consecutive failures — always after at least one attempt, with skipped refs left queued for the next push. The batch error is logged before the fallback runs so a transport failure, which `checkpointRefRejectionReason` deliberately does not match, still names its cause; and `remote.Fetch` annotates its error with git's redacted output via `errWithGitOutput` — deliberately not a `PushError`, which is how a refused push is recognised — rather than the caller substituting that output for the error. See [ref-backend pre-push flow](../architecture/ref-checkpoint-backend.md#pre-push-flow).
- **Single checkpoint sync remote** - checkpoint data syncs only to the elected checkpoint sync remote (`strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` setting → captured election → `origin` → sole remote → first remote in `.git/config` order; fail-closed only when the setting names a missing remote — the captured tier is fail-soft), on both the git-branch and git-refs backends. **Capture**: during pre-push, a push whose target agrees with the branch's declared push destination (`branch.<name>.pushRemote` → `remote.pushDefault` → `branch.<name>.remote`) and differs from the current election persists that remote as the captured election (git common dir, `entire-checkpoint-sync-remotes.json`), announces it on stderr, and the same push carries the checkpoints — see `strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go`. Declaration alone is deliberately **not** a tier: electing from tracking config at rest silently drops checkpoint sync on every push to a different remote (`git push <other> HEAD`, a `git clone -o base` pushing checkpoints to a separately added `origin`, any repo with `remote.pushDefault` — the `74e239a9` regression), and a bare push to an undeclared remote never elects (the pre-single-remote transcript leak). Phase-1 capture rules: at most one captured remote, first still-configured capture sticks (no per-push ping-pong in mixed-habit repos; a captured remote that was renamed or removed no longer vetoes the next capture), explicit `checkpoint_push_remote` outranks and disables capture. Pushes to any other remote or to a raw URL never carry checkpoint data, except a configured remote whose every push URL names the same known-forge repository as the elected remote's (a GitHub remote and its `entire://…/gh/` mirror; identity is `gitremote.Repository`, owner/repo compared case-insensitively; only direct transports (`gitremote.NamesGitHost`: ssh, https, http, git) and `entire://` qualify, so a remote-helper scheme such as `bogus+ssh://github.com/…` never matches however its host reads; the elected remote is resolved first and an unmatchable one ends the check before the push remote is resolved; an SSH host alias is resolved through `ssh -G` only when git runs plain `ssh`; unknown hosts and Entire-native `et/` repos never match) — mirrors push through and sync every ref back, so both reach one repository (`pushesToSameForgeRepository`). Push-through covering **checkpoint refs** (`entire/checkpoints/v1` and the git-refs backend's `refs/entire/*`, not just branches) is a verified external contract, confirmed with the server side on 2026-10-06 and not enforced by CI: if the mirror ever stops forwarding them, git-refs checkpoints strand in the mirror silently, because the push queue drains on the mirror's acceptance. After such a push delivers a branch ref, `advanceSyncRemoteTrackingRef` fast-forwards the elected remote's tracking ref to the pushed remote's, so `entire status` and the gated-sync hint stop counting delivered checkpoints as unpushed; a non-fast-forward is left for the next fetch. This widens the gate only; the election, capture, and read candidates are unchanged; the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL mode is exempt. `entire status` shows the sync destination, its source (`observed` renders as "follows your branch's push destination"), and an unpushed-checkpoint count.
- **A refused `checkpoint_remote` says so where it will be seen** - `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` refuses a committed `checkpoint_remote` whose owner does not match every remote identifying this repo, and used to say so only in a WARN. The visible symptom — checkpoints arriving in the code repository — is a working setup, just not the one that was asked for, so the rejection now reaches the user in `entire status` (text and `--json`, with `checkpoint_remote_ignored_verdict`) and `entire enable`, which take one verdict from `ignoredCheckpointRemote` and print the same sentence — "Checkpoints sync to X, not to the configured checkpoint_remote Y: reason" — plus the claim command built by `remote.ClaimCheckpointRemoteCommand`, for a disproved owner (a fork; rendered as information) and an unprovable one (a warning) alike. With `push_sessions` disabled both commands judge the read path instead, and also report a store the fetch side declined for a non-ownership reason. Pre-push stderr (`warnIgnoredCheckpointRemote`) is narrower: it warns only for an **unprovable** owner, because a disproved one is the ordinary fork contributor, for whom checkpoints landing in their fork is the correct outcome and a warning on every push would be noise they could silence only by claiming someone else's store. The repo is printed through `tuiutil.SanitizeDisplayText`, because it comes from the committed settings file. A local settings file present in the index or HEAD is never accepted as consent: `entire enable --local --checkpoint-remote` refuses to write it and says to untrack it, and the enable claim prompt is not offered. The enable claim prompt respects `--yes` and `--agent`, and any successful claim precedes destination resolution for the final report. It blocks nothing: checkpoints keep flowing to the elected remote, because refusing to push them turns a misconfiguration into lost work. The pre-push warning fires on **every push that delivered checkpoints** while the condition holds — a one-shot notice is seen by whoever set the repo up and not by whoever hits the problem — and is emitted after delivery, so a push carrying no checkpoints says nothing. Two gates guard it and neither is redundant: `checkpointRemoteConfigured` is the free half (an empty `checkpointURL` means "none configured" as often as "configured and refused"), and `hasCheckpointURL` is authoritative, because `PushURL` decided where this push goes while `InheritedCheckpointRemote` re-runs the vote over an identity set that can diverge from it. The claim command is offered **only for providers `parseCheckpointRemoteFlag` accepts** (github, and gitlab including nested groups): `GetCheckpointRemote` validates no provider at all, so naming any other would print a command that fails when pasted.
- **Checkpoint reads follow the election** - reads consult an ordered candidate chain: the elected sync remote first, then `origin` as a **read-only legacy tier** (pre-single-remote checkpoints live there; `strategy.CheckpointReadRemotes` / `CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection` resolve the chain, failing OPEN to `[origin]` on an election error). Metadata-branch fetches refresh every candidate tracking ref because branch existence does not prove a requested checkpoint exists there; other fetch targets, tracking-ref readers, and blob hydration try candidates in order. Git-refs remote discovery ls-remotes every candidate **without** needing a dedicated `checkpoint_remote` and merges the listings. Local-ref writers stay **elected-remote-only**: `EnsurePrimaryRef`, the metadata-fetch advance, and `promoteRemoteTrackingPrimary` never act on the legacy tier (a stale origin feeding `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` is the #1374-class hazard), keyed on the explicit election result, never on the chain's first entry. A remoteless repo keeps its "checkpoint absent" classification, which requires positive evidence (successful empty `git remote` listing, live ctx, readable settings without a `checkpoint_remote` key).
- **Dedicated `checkpoint_remote` accepts `github` and `gitlab` providers**: `{"provider": "github"|"gitlab", "repo": "owner/repo"}` in `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote` (`entire configure --checkpoint-remote <provider>:<owner>/<repo>`). Nested GitLab groups (`group/subgroup/project`) pass validation; `CheckpointRemoteConfig.Owner()` takes the first path segment for the ownership vote, as the origin parser does. The checkpoint URL keeps the push remote's protocol and host (`checkpoint/remote/util.go:deriveCheckpointURLFromInfo`: SSH→SSH, HTTPS→HTTPS, `entire://`→same-cluster mirror when the origin's forge matches the provider); the provider's canonical host (`providerHost`) is used only when that derivation fails (`resolveProviderCheckpointURL`) or on the fetch side when `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` forces HTTPS. SSH/HTTPS derivation fails on purpose on a public forge of another provider (`checkPublicForgeMatchesProvider`: `github.com` for a gitlab store, `gitlab.com` for a github one), because that host names its provider and keeping it would send checkpoints — and a token — to the wrong forge; any other host (GitHub Enterprise, self-managed GitLab) is the user's own installation and is kept. That coercion is allow-listed by transport (`deriveTokenOriginURL` → `isTokenRewritableTransport`): only an origin whose host is the git host itself (`ssh`, `https`, `http`, `git`) is rewritten into a token-bearing HTTPS URL, because that URL becomes the fetch target and carries the credential. An `entire://` origin names an Entire cluster rather than a git endpoint, and `file://` names no host, so both are left as configured and no token is attached. The allow-list reads a transport, not a spelling: `gitremote.ParseURL` folds git's `git+ssh://` and `ssh+git://` aliases into `ssh` (`normalizeProtocol`), so one SSH remote cannot be admitted under one spelling and refused — silently, with no token and no SSH warning — under another; unrecognized `<x>+ssh` schemes are remote helpers to git and stay themselves so they still fail closed. The token is one Basic-auth header for both providers (`x-access-token:<token>`, `checkpoint/remote/git.go:appendCheckpointTokenEnv`); this relies on GitLab ignoring the Basic-auth username for Personal/Project Access Tokens — an external contract verified manually against gitlab.com, not enforced by CI. A gitlab `checkpoint_remote` is therefore direct transport only: `gitremote.hostToForge` maps only `github.com`, so the `entire://` mirror derivation never matches and falls back to `providerHost`. Everything else that is github-only has its own gate, not this one: trails (`trail_context_cache.go`, `info.Forge != ""` via `hostToForge`), `--issue-link` (`investigate/issuelink.go`, github.com hosts only), repo protection (control-plane repo `provider` enum, `github`/`entire`), and entire.io checkpoint discovery (server-side).
- **Scanner engine selection is a settings-only, fail-closed choice**: `redaction.betterleaks.enabled` (default `true`) and `redaction.goredact.enabled` (default `false`) pick which pattern-matching engine(s) feed layer 2 of `detectAllLayers` (`redact.ConfigureScanners`, `redact/scanners.go`). Both keys are honored from committed `.entire/settings.json` only — a `settings.local.json` copy is ignored with a logged warning, because the choice affects everyone who reads the repo's checkpoints, not just the developer who set it. `validateScannerSettings` fails settings load with `settings.ErrScannerConfig` when both engines are disabled. If goredact is the sole enabled engine and its scan fails at runtime, `redact.ErrScannerDegraded` propagates out of `JSONLBytes`; every checkpoint-write call site (`checkpoint/persistent.go`, `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`) must `errors.Is` for it and fail the write rather than fall back to under-scanned content. See `docs/security-and-privacy.md` for user-facing details.
- **`external_agents` is an exec-bearing setting, so it is a trust boundary**:
  it enables the `$PATH` scan that globs for `entire-agent-*` binaries and runs
  each one's `info` subcommand, so a committed `{"external_agents": true}` would
  let a pull request turn on execution of whatever binary it could get onto a
  developer's `$PATH`, with no prompt in front of it. `settings.enforceExternalAgentsTrust`
  (`settings/external_agents_trust.go`) honors it only from a
  `classifyLocalSettingsDeep`-verified `.entire/settings.local.json` (untracked
  in **both** the index and `HEAD` — the filename is not the check, because
  `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path); only a `true` value is gated, since `false` grants
  nothing. Rejection is a downgrade recorded on
  `EntireSettings.ExternalAgentsRejection()`, surfaced by `entire status` and by
  `external.DiscoverAndRegister` — without it, a refused grant and a setting the
  user never wrote look identical (no agent appears). **Consequence for every
  write site**: the auto-enable that fires when a user picks an external agent
  must go through `enableExternalAgentsLocally` (`setup_external_agents.go`),
  which raw-writes the single key to the local file whatever `--local`/`--project`
  said about the rest — writing it into the project file produces a setting the
  user can read back and that never takes effect.
  **The grant also gates `summary_generation.provider`**, which is the other
  place a tracked file names a binary to execute: `discoverSummaryProviderIfMissing`
  resolves an unregistered provider by name, so `{"summary_generation":
  {"provider": "evil"}}` in a pull request was enough to run
  `entire-agent-evil info` on whoever pulled it and ran `entire explain`.
  Resolving by name rather than sweeping `$PATH` bounds the blast radius to one
  binary; it does not make it zero. The check sits *after* the
  already-registered early return, so a committed `"provider": "claude-code"`
  is unaffected — the gate lands only on the external case — and the
  unresolvable-provider error gains a line naming the grant, since "unknown
  summary provider" about a plugin that is plainly installed is not actionable.
  A dedicated `enforceSummaryProviderTrust` beside the other two gates would let
  a developer name an external provider in their own `settings.local.json`
  without granting the `$PATH` sweep; that is a real want, but it costs a third
  settings-layer classification and a third rejection channel, so it waits until
  someone asks for the combination.
- **Agent instruction fields get the same provenance gate**:
  every `ReviewConfig.Prompt` (per-worker and judge, in `review_profiles` and
  the legacy `review` map) and every
  `ReviewProfileConfig.Task` land verbatim in prompts of agents that
  review spawns with approval checks disabled, so a committed value
  would let a pull request steer a permission-bypassed agent. Task and Prompt
  are adjacent sections of the same composed prompt, which is why gating one
  without the other would be a formality. `settings.enforceAgentPromptTrust`
  (`settings/agent_prompt_trust.go`) honors them only from a developer-owned
  layer: clone-local preferences (in `.git/`, unreachable by clone) or a
  `classifyLocalSettingsDeep`-verified `.entire/settings.local.json`.
  Provenance follows merge order (local replaces
  review profiles per profile name). Rejection is a downgrade recorded in
  `EntireSettings.AgentPromptRejections()`, and review prints a
  one-line stderr notice for fields they would have used — suppressed for a
  dropped task equal to review's built-in default, which the fallback
  reproduces anyway (the non-interactive first-run setup persists exactly
  that). Deliberately ungated, each with a mechanism or reason: Skills
  (validated against installed skills before spawning), Agent/Model (registry
  keys and routing hints), review_default_profile (selects among profiles whose
  instruction content is itself gated).
  `TestAgentPromptGate_CoversEveryReviewConfigInSchema`
  pins that a future `ReviewConfig` placement cannot bypass the gate.
- **A tracked `.entire/settings.local.json` is ignored wholesale**: the local layer's premise is that it is per-clone and per-developer (it is gitignored, `entire enable --local` writes it, and `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` treats presence there as proof the developer chose it). `.gitignore` does not apply to an already-tracked path, so a committed one arrives by cloning and would override project settings for everyone. `loadMergedSettings` drops the layer when the file is **proven** tracked, records `EntireSettings.LocalLayerRejection()`, and the redaction consumer prints it with the `git rm --cached` fix. It never errors — one committed file must not brick `status`/`doctor`. Two deliberately opposite failure directions, expressed as the three-state `localTrust` (`localUnverifiable` is the zero value so a forgotten assignment fails safe): an *unverifiable* repo keeps the layer (losing all local settings is worse than the risk) but still drops the exec-bearing `external_agents` setting (being wrong there means running someone else's binary); *no* repository counts as proof of locality. `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` reads the raw file outside the loader, so it repeats the check itself.
- Safe to use on main/master since it never modifies commit history

#### Key Files

- `strategy.go` - Shared types only, no behaviour: the argument and result structs (`PendingCheckpoint`, `StepContext`, `RestoredSession`), and `TaskMetadataDir()`. The strategy type itself and its constructor live in `manual_commit.go`.
- `common.go` - Helpers for metadata extraction, tree building, `ListCheckpoints()`
- `manual_commit*.go` - Manual-commit strategy: main impl, types, session state, condensation, pending-checkpoint listing + log restore (`manual_commit_pending.go`), git ops, logs, hook handlers (prepare-commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite, pre-push), reset
- `cleanup.go` - Cleanup discovery/deletion for legacy shadow branches, session states, and checkpoint metadata
- `session_state.go` - Package-level session state functions
- `hooks.go` - Git hook installation

Note: `checkpoint/configloader.go` overrides go-git's default config loader with a symlink-following `billy.Basic` (`osSymlinkFS`) — go-git's default reads config via `os.Root`, which rejects absolute symlinks in any path component (e.g. a `~/.config` managed by a dotfile tool), silently dropping global config so author identity fell back to "Unknown" and signing was skipped.

#### Deep-Dive Reference

The phase state machine, metadata directory layout, sharded checkpoint format, multi-session metadata, checkpoint ID linking, commit trailers, and concurrent-session behavior are documented in:

- [Sessions and Checkpoints](../architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md) - domain model, storage layout, checkpoint ID linking, commit trailers, package structure
- [Checkpoint Scenarios](../architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md) - phase state machine and worked condensation scenarios
- [Ref-Based Checkpoint Backend](../architecture/ref-checkpoint-backend.md) - git-refs backend: primary/mirror taxonomy, ref layout + sharding, push-discovery queue, read routing, config + rollout

#### When Modifying the Strategy

- Adding a method to `*ManualCommitStrategy` is enough — there is no interface to satisfy, and no second implementation to keep in step
- Test with `mise run test` - strategy tests are in `*_test.go` files
- Update this reference and `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` when strategy behavior changes. Update root instructions only when a repository-wide development rule changes.
