","state":null,"user":null,"assignees":null,"labels":null,"milestone":null,"state_reason":null,"comments":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"closed_at":null,"display_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2122","display_title":"Install Entire CLI in Cursor Cloud Agent environments on enable"},{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1777","title":"fix(session): auto-adopt across git common dirs on commit","issue_number":1777,"body":"**Trail:** [https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/875]() ## Summary Fixes entireio/cli#1439 ## What Auto-adopt a unique ACTIVE agent session from another git common dir during `prepare-commit-msg`, so commits in an enabled repo B get an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer when the live session state still lives under repo A. ## Why / how it helps Long agent sessions often move across independently enabled repos. Hooks fire in B, but B's `.git/entire-sessions` is empty, so the trailer is silently skipped even though Entire is installed. Manual `entire session adopt` (entireio/cli#1472) already exists; this wires a safe automatic path on commit. ## How * Maintain a best-effort live-session registry under the user cache whenever an ACTIVE session is saved (cleared on end/clear/tombstone). * On `prepare-commit-msg`, if the current repo is enabled and has no local ACTIVE session, discover exactly one recent cross-common-dir candidate via: 1. live-session registry — reaches **non-sibling** worktrees under unrelated parents (covers #1439's own repro: a session in `…/entire.io/.worktrees/…` committing in an unrelated `/private/tmp/…` checkout), then 2. immediate sibling repos under the parent directory (microservices / seeded repro). * Require a **non-boilerplate** `FilesTouched`∩staged overlap **and** a process-owner match for every candidate (the registry path drops proximity and leans on these stronger guards to prevent cross-repo steals); ambiguous candidates skip. * The adopt is **split across the two commit hooks**: `prepare-commit-msg` registers the adopted session in the target (so the trailer lands) and stamps a `PendingSourceRetire` marker, but leaves the source ACTIVE; `post-commit` completes the destructive source-side retire once the commit is a fact. An aborted commit therefore never strands the source with its checkpointing retired and no commit. * Tradeoff: this is direction-1 handoff (adopt/retire), not a full joint multi-repo session model (issue direction 3). Coordinated A+B commits in one turn still need a future fan-out model. ## Testing * Live repro (before): A trailer present; B message unchanged / no trailer; B `entire-sessions` empty. * Live repro (after, same script with `/tmp/entire-1439`): * A: `Entire-Checkpoint: …` * B: `Entire-Checkpoint: …` and session state present under B. * Edges: no FilesTouched overlap → no adopt; two overlapping sibling sources → no adopt. * Unit/regression: `TestAutoAdopt_*`, `TestLiveRegistry_*`, existing `TestSessionAdopt_*`. * Mutation: early-return no-op in `tryAutoAdoptCrossCommonDirSession` → `TestAutoAdopt_PrepareCommitMsg_ViaLiveRegistry` FAIL; restore → PASS. * Audit: two clean passes after requiring overlap (blocks owner-only steal) + wrapcheck/lint fixes. * `mise run fmt && mise run lint` green; `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/session ./cmd/entire/cli` green on committed tree. ## Review follow-ups (trail 875) Three architectural review findings addressed on top of the initial change: * **Deferred source retire (HIGH):** the destructive source-side tombstone moved from `prepare-commit-msg` to `post-commit` (`finalizePendingSourceRetires`), so an aborted commit no longer retires the source with no commit. Idempotent, panic-guarded, time-bounded. * **Non-sibling registry reach (HIGH):** dropped the parent-dir proximity gate from the registry discovery path so #1439's own cross-parent repro actually gets a trailer; steal-safety now rests on owner + non-boilerplate-overlap + uniqueness. Removed the now-unused `autoAdoptSiblingProximity` helper. * **Integration coverage (MED):** added `integration_test/auto_adopt_integration_test.go` driving the real `entire hooks git post-commit` binary after a real `git commit` — post-commit finalize retires the source, a held source flock makes finalize give up without corruption, and a disabled target stays inert. Full integration suite green (440 passed). Post-commit then declined the same session: - `hasNew`: post-commit ran the same live-transcript check with no staged files, so the overlap could never match (without task records the session had "no new content"). - Overlap: for IDLE sessions `filesTouchedBefore` came only from persisted `FilesTouched`, which is empty here, so `shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck` returned false. The commit kept a trailer pointing at a checkpoint that was never written, and the session's usage went to its next checkpoint, possibly on another branch. ## Fix - `liveTranscriptCheckApplies` is the one condition both hooks use for "judge this session by its live transcript"; `sessionHasNewContent` now calls it instead of two separate branches. - The live-transcript check overlaps with the commit's files: staged in prepare-commit-msg, committed in post-commit (`contentCheckOpts.committedFiles`). - Post-commit takes such an IDLE session's overlap from its transcript's uncheckpointed edits (`filesTouchedWithLiveTranscript`). ENDED sessions are unchanged: with no persisted files they take the discard action. - `hasMidTurnClaimant` → `hasLiveTranscriptClaimant`: it also counts these IDLE writers, so a file-less ACTIVE reader is held off the commit by the read-only gate instead of condensing into the writer's checkpoint (this predated the change). An IDLE writer counts only if its transcript grew since its last checkpoint, so a Claude subagent's already-checkpointed edits can't claim the commit. - Only IDLE sessions get the committed files in post-commit. An ENDED one would otherwise count its transcript edits as new content, take the discard action anyway, and never be marked fully condensed. - Transcript edits are made relative to the session's home, so a non-ACTIVE session is judged by them only for commits at its home (`transcriptEditsApplyHere`), in both hooks and the claimant check. In stacked worktrees that touch the same files, a sibling's commit otherwise got the session's trailer and guest-condensed it, consuming the work the home's later commit needed. ## Tests `idle_live_transcript_condense_test.go`, through the real prepare-commit-msg → commit → post-commit hooks: - Trailer resolves for no turn-end step, completed task records, and a turn-end step without a record (all red before the fix). - The session stays out of a commit its transcript didn't edit. - An ACTIVE reader is not condensed into the IDLE writer's checkpoint. - Sibling worktree: with a record of the sibling the trailer resolves; with only transcript evidence nothing is linked, with or without files pending at home. Either way the home's and a third worktree's pending files survive. - Stacked worktrees: a sibling commits its own `feature.go` before the home commits the transcript's `feature.go`; the sibling gets no trailer and the home's trailer resolves. - An ENDED session with transcript-only edits is marked fully condensed after a commit. - An IDLE session whose only matching edits are an already-checkpointed subagent's doesn't hold an ACTIVE reader off the commit. Each half of the fix and the claimant change were mutation-checked against these tests. `TestPostCommit_IdleSession_NoTranscriptFallbackForCarryForward` still passes: its session has a stored transcript, so the helper leaves it alone. ## Not covered - An ENDED session with no persisted files can still be stamped by prepare-commit-msg and discarded by post-commit. Fixing it means deciding whether to condense such a session or not stamp it. - The ticket's exact incident state is unconfirmed. The stacked-worktree case (1652 stacked on 1651, touching the same files) fits it: on main both commits got trailers that resolve to nothing. The `files_touched_before` field of the incident's `post-commit: carry-forward prep` log line would settle it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes post-commit condensation and read-only gate logic for IDLE/transcript-only sessions; mistakes could mis-attribute checkpoints or skip condensation, but behavior is heavily covered by new hook tests. > > **Overview** > Fixes **ENT-3537**: when **prepare-commit-msg** links an **IDLE** session using only its **live transcript** (no turn-end step, or a step that left no `FilesTouched` / stored transcript), **post-commit** now **condenses** into that trailer instead of leaving a checkpoint ID that was never written. > > **prepare-commit-msg** and **post-commit** now share **`liveTranscriptCheckApplies`** for “judge this session by the live transcript.” The live-transcript overlap check uses **`contentCheckOpts.commitFiles()`**—staged files before commit, **committed files** after—so both hooks agree. Post-commit passes **`committedFiles`** into **`sessionHasNewContent`**, derives overlap for those IDLE sessions via **`filesTouchedWithLiveTranscript`**, and **`hasMidTurnClaimant`** is renamed to **`hasLiveTranscriptClaimant`** so transcript-only IDLE writers block file-less ACTIVE readers on the read-only gate. > > New hook integration tests in **`idle_live_transcript_condense_test.go`** cover trailer resolution, unrelated commits, reader vs writer, and sibling worktrees; **`mid_turn_commit_test.go`** updates for the **`commitFiles` set** API on **`sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript`**. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 27884f98d29a8e33957f1b7ea611d0e7a9d7bfbf. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). ","state":null,"user":null,"assignees":null,"labels":null,"milestone":null,"state_reason":null,"comments":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"closed_at":null,"display_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2892","display_title":"Condense an IDLE session prepare-commit-msg linked by its live transcript"},{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2785","title":"Redone commits don't mint a fresh checkpoint for inherited work","issue_number":2785,"body":" https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1582 ## Problem E2E run [38724857355](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/38724857355/job/116388096213) failed `TestExplainCheckpoint` (claude-code). Haiku committed `docs/feature.md` itself, then ran `git reset HEAD~1`, and the test's own commit came out with two checkpoint trailers: the inherited `3afa00e9bfa6` (correct, via the redo inheritance from 6170bc1612) and a fresh `93418f0f011f`. The fresh one was wrong. The reset put the file back in the worktree, the next turn end recorded it as touched again, and session matching saw transcript growth plus an overlapping staged file. The new checkpoint's transcript slice held only the agent's commit and reset, which the turn-end finalize had already folded into `3afa00e9bfa6`. ## Fix - The redo step (`inheritReplacedCommitsTrailers`) now also reports which staged paths the inherited checkpoints already hold. A path counts only when the newest dropped commit that changed it carries a checkpoint that is not deleted and exists in this clone's store (`capturedCheckpoints`), and the staged content and mode both match what that commit left. Inheriting the trailer stays permissive: a trailer whose capture failed still links, but holds nothing, so the session's work gets a fresh checkpoint. Content, mode and deletions come from one rename-free read of the commit index git is preparing (`parseStagedRaw` now also keeps the staged mode, building on #2330), so `git commit -a` and path-limited commits compare what they commit. - `PrepareCommitMsg` returns right after inheriting when every staged path is held, so a pure redo gets no fresh trailer, whatever the session phase. - Otherwise the staged-files overlap check in `filterSessionsWithNewContent` sees only the redo's other staged paths, from the same rename-free view, so only other session work earns a fresh checkpoint. (A rename-detecting list would hide a staged deletion paired with a held file.) - Prepare records the held paths in the inherited-trailers marker. After a redo that stamps no fresh trailer (pure, or partial with no session's other work), which condenses nothing, post-commit (`reconcileRedoneFiles`) drops them from this worktree's sessions' touched files when the commit holds the recorded content, as carry-forward would. Only held files go through that check; other touched files, steps and transcript growth stay pending untouched. - `openRepositoryTimed` is extracted to keep `PrepareCommitMsg` under the `maintidx` limit; the `open_repository` span no longer includes the redo lookup. - The deleted-checkpoint list is loaded once per commit, each dropped commit's diff is computed once, and store lookups are memoized. - Documented in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and `docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md`. ## Deliberately not changed Whenever a fresh trailer is stamped, a redundant checkpoint is preferred to a lost or dangling link: - On a partial redo (redone files staged together with other files), the mid-turn agent fast path still stamps a fresh trailer. Transcripts miss edits made through shell commands (`sed -i`, formatters, codegen), so it cannot rule out new work. - Post-commit judges overlap without the redo, so a session that only redid work may fold into another session's fresh checkpoint. An earlier commit on this branch excluded redone paths there, but that left a fresh trailer with no checkpoint behind it when a stale ACTIVE session tracked only redone files, or when a read-only ACTIVE session was gated out by a redo-only claimant. ## Tests Regression tests in `manual_commit_redo_test.go`. The fixture writes real checkpoints for its trailers through the hooks' own store. Each test fails without its fix (mutation-checked), except the aborted-commit one, which two independent guards cover. Every test that expects a fresh trailer runs prepare, the commit and post-commit, and asserts the trailer resolves in the checkpoint store: - a pure redo, with an ended or an active session, gets only the inherited trailers; - after a pure redo, only the redone file leaves the session's touched files, and a later human edit to it doesn't link back to the session; - a redo plus new session work gets the inherited trailer and a fresh one; - a redo plus a file the session never touched gets only the inherited trailer; - a mode change after the reset gets a fresh trailer; - a later dropped commit without a checkpoint that changed the same file leaves it uncovered; - a partial redo by an active session keeps its fast-path trailer; - a stale ACTIVE session tracking only redone files, a read-only ACTIVE session beside a redo-only claimant, and two ended sessions all leave the fresh trailer resolvable; - a dropped commit whose checkpoint is missing or deleted keeps the session's fresh capture; - a staged deletion git pairs with a held file as a rename stamps no fresh trailer; - content and mode are read from the temporary commit index, not `.git/index`; - an aborted commit's marker never settles files a later commit didn't contain; - the cleanup never prunes touched files the redo doesn't hold. `mise run check` passes. ## Follow-ups - The amend fold (`git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git commit --amen…59385 chars truncated…t rewriting is included. Claude's non-interactive mode treats its working directory as trusted, so the reviewer was taking execution-capable configuration from the checkout under review. The reviewer now loads no Claude settings at all and starts no MCP servers. Entire's own lifecycle hooks are supplied through a settings file the CLI writes outside the worktree, so reviews are still captured; the profile's configured skills are supplied by staging them into a plugin directory the CLI owns, so the user's chosen skills still run. | Flag | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `--setting-sources ""` | No settings are read: project and local are branch-controlled, and a user-level hook would run with the reviewed checkout as its working directory | | `--strict-mcp-config` (no `--mcp-config`) | No MCP servers start; setting sources do not gate these | | `--permission-mode default` | Pinned, so a future default cannot widen the reviewer | | `--settings ` | Entire's lifecycle hooks, written outside the worktree, mode 0600 | | `--plugin-dir ` | Only the profile's configured skills, copied into a directory Entire owns | | `--append-system-prompt` | Trust-boundary instruction, appended so a profile prompt cannot displace it | ## Why user settings are excluded too An earlier revision of this branch kept `--setting-sources user` to preserve user- and plugin-provided review skills. That reintroduced an execution path: a user-level hook running `npm run …`, `make …`, or any checkout-relative script executes code from the branch under review, because that branch is the reviewer's working directory. The trail security monitor flagged it, correctly. The trusted settings file also no longer carries the user's `apiKeyHelper`. Claude runs that helper as a shell command with the reviewed checkout as its working directory, so a relative helper executes branch content before the first request; the generation path re-injects it safely only because it runs in `os.TempDir()`, which review cannot. Reviewers authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a Claude sign-in, and Entire prints a note before launch when a helper is configured and no env key is set. Skill staging (`review_skills.go`) resolves the tension without that trade. Each configured skill is copied from the user's own configuration into a temporary plugin directory, loaded with `--plugin-dir`, and its invocation rewritten to `/entire-review:`. Only the chosen skill is copied — never a whole plugin, which can define hooks of its own. Curated builtins such as `/review` need no staging. A skill that cannot be staged fails the review before launch, because a reviewer started without its skill prints `Unknown command` and reviews nothing while still exiting 0. ## Also in here - **Same hooks as `entire enable`, installer untouched.** The review launch runs the installer (`installHookEntries`, a pure map transform) against an empty document and uses its output, so the reviewer's hooks cannot drift from what `entire enable` writes — and `hooks.go` is unchanged from main. - **Fail before launch.** If the trusted settings or a configured skill cannot be established, the review fails. There is no degraded fallback. - **An architectural test** requires every `claude` launch site in the package to record whether it is isolated. - **`PrepareCmd`** on `ReviewerTemplate`: a launch precondition that can fail and owns resources, released once the process exits or immediately if `Start` fails. ## Compatibility - Project-level MCP servers and project-level Claude settings do not apply to reviewers. - User-level hooks, permission modes and MCP servers do not apply to reviewers either. - The user's `apiKeyHelper` is not run for reviews; use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a Claude sign-in. - Review profiles keep working: builtin, user-level and plugin-provided skills all resolve through staging. This is configuration isolation, not an OS sandbox: the reviewer runs with the invoking account's privileges. ## Verification Full `mise run check` clean. Differential runs against a real Claude with a loopback mock API and synthetic credentials, each comparing an unpatched build with the fix so the fixture is proven to fire before the fix is credited with blocking it. Five canaries: a committed settings hook, a committed `settings.local.json` hook, a committed `.mcp.json` server, a **user-level hook that runs a checkout-relative script**, and a **relative `apiKeyHelper` with the branch supplying the script** — the last two added because the earlier harness only had branch-controlled canaries and could not see either path. | Platform | Claude | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | 2.1.237, 2.1.267 | pass — all four canaries fire unpatched, all four blocked by the fix, capture intact | | Linux | 2.1.237, 2.1.267 | pass — same | | macOS | 2.1.237, 2.1.268 | pass — same; the `user`-sources revision runs the fourth canary here, reproducing the monitor's finding | Matrix run (private validation repo): https://github.com/peyton-alt/cli-review-windows-validation/actions/runs/34567618641 Covers current-branch and remote-only `--target` with `--cleanup-worktree`, multi-worker profiles, builtin / user-level / plugin-provided skills, and session/transcript capture throughout. Not covered: live-service authentication. ## Review notes Separately, and pre-existing: a review whose agent makes zero model requests still reports `1 succeeded` and exits 0. It warns that findings were not persisted. That one ID keyed both transcript paths (the staged capture `.entire/tmp/pi/.json` and the shadow archive `.entire//`), so runs overwrote each other and a checkpoint condensed whichever run wrote last — storing a *different* subagent's conversation. Reproduces with a single Pi session and one subagent; no concurrency required. This takes **direction 1** from the issue: model Pi subagents as subagents — roll the session ID up to the parent UUID, give each run a distinct identity, and route runs through the existing subagent mechanism so each gets its own transcript. ## What Changed - **`agent/pi/lifecycle.go`** — new `parsePiSessionIdentity` (+ `parsePiSubagentPath`, `parsePiParentID`, `derivePiParentTranscript`) resolves the path shape: - parent `…/_.jsonl` → session ID = `` - subagent `…/_//run-N/session.jsonl` → session ID rolls up to the parent ``, plus a distinct `-run-N` id. `ParseHookEvent` now routes subagent `before_agent_start`/`agent_end` to `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` (parent turns still emit `TurnStart`/`TurnEnd`), and stages each run's transcript under its own identity. The parse validates the derived id against **both** consumers (`ValidateAgentID` for the dispatcher and the stricter `ValidateSessionID` for the capture key) so an exotic dir name can't parse-pass then silently fail to stage. - **`agent/event.go`** — added `Event.SubagentTranscriptPath` for agents whose per-subagent transcripts can't be reconstructed from `SessionRef` + `SubagentID` (Pi's nested `//run-N` layout). - **`lifecycle.go`** — `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` prefers `event.SubagentTranscriptPath`, falling back to the existing `agent-.jsonl` convention. Claude Code / Cursor are unaffected (the new field is empty for them). Net effect: one Pi session per conversation (no phantom `session · turns N` row), a distinct staged/stored transcript per run, and task checkpoints that roll up under the parent session with uncontaminated content. ## Tests Written test-first, all confirmed **red** before the fix, green after: - `TestExtractSessionIDFromPath_SubagentRollsUpToParent` — subagent paths roll to the parent UUID, never `"session"`. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentRunsRouteAsSubagents` — subagent runs emit `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd`, share the parent `SessionID`, carry distinct `SubagentID`s. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentCaptureDoesNotClobber` — parent + each run stage distinct, content-correct transcripts. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentTranscriptSurvivesLaterRun` — one run's staged transcript isn't overwritten when a later run ends (the exact corruption). - `TestExtractSessionIDFromPath` — extended the canonical table with the nested subagent shape and dropped the case that pinned the wrong fallback. ## Verification - `mise run fmt`, lint (golangci-lint v2.11.3, pinned) — clean. - `mise run test:ci` (full race suite + e2e canary) — green; `pi`, `agent/*`, `checkpoint/*`, `strategy`, `cli` suites green. - **End-to-end smoke test** with the real binary in a scratch repo, driving a parent turn + two subagent runs that each modify a file: - `entire session list` → one Pi session with the real parent UUID, no phantom `session` row. - `.entire/tmp/pi/` → three distinct captures (`019fab4c-….json`, `d93a3451-run-0.json`, `716671d6-run-1.json`), no shared `session.json`. - Shadow branch → task checkpoints under `…//tasks//agent-.jsonl`, each storing its **own** run's content (run-0 → run0 marker, run-1 → run1 marker), zero cross-contamination. ## Deferred The issue's optional "have `entire_extension.ts` send `session_id` explicitly" was intentionally dropped: the path parse is now correct and load-bearing, so it's unnecessary. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes Pi hook routing and subagent checkpoint transcript resolution; mistakes could mis-attribute sessions or corrupt task checkpoints, but scope is Pi-specific with a clear fallback for other agents. > > **Overview** > Fixes **#1870**: Pi subagent hooks used to derive session ID from `session.jsonl` basenames, so every run shared the ID `session` and **staged transcripts / task checkpoints overwrote each other**. > > **Pi lifecycle** now parses nested paths (`…/_//run-N/session.jsonl`), rolls **SessionID** up to the parent UUID, assigns a distinct **`-run-N`** subagent ID, and emits **`SubagentStart` / `SubagentEnd`** instead of normal turns. Each run is staged via `captureTranscript` under its own cache key. > > **Framework**: `agent.Event` gains **`SubagentTranscriptPath`**; `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` prefers it over the `agent-.jsonl` convention beside the main transcript. > > Other agents are unchanged when the new field is empty. Regression coverage lives in `subagent_1870_test.go`. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a9b8d49248cc78b2ac4ea1aecc961a711a89343e. This addresses the Windows Copilot failure in nightly install smoke [run 34583415795](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34583415795), `TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli`. The turn-end guard previously compared raw bytes against HEAD, so line-ending conversion made committed files appear uncommitted. #2341 exposed this by teaching Copilot's transcript analyzer to read `restrictedProperties.filePaths`. ## Why Copilot exposed this on Windows Windows does not force every file to use CRLF. The agent's file-writing tool chooses the line endings. With `core.autocrlf=true`, `git add` normalizes the stored blob to LF without rewriting the working file: | Agent writes | Working file after commit | Git blob | Previous raw comparison | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | LF | LF | LF | Correctly reports committed | | CRLF | CRLF | LF | Incorrectly reports modified | The original Windows smoke artifacts show different paths through this shared code: - **Codex and OpenCode:** Git warned that the working files contained LF and would be converted to CRLF the next time Git touched them. Their LF working copies matched the committed LF blobs, and turn-end capture reported no remaining modifications. - **Copilot:** Post-commit cleanup removed the shadow branch successfully. About two seconds later, turn-end capture counted the committed file as modified and recreated the branch, consistent with the diagnosed CRLF-versus-LF mismatch. #2341 exposed this path by making Entire recognize Copilot's modified-file telemetry under `restrictedProperties.filePaths`. - **Claude Code:** Turn-end parsing used a transcript offset advanced past the commit and reported no remaining modifications. The saved artifacts do not establish its working-file line endings, so LF cannot be asserted as the explanation for Claude's passing result. This is a shared Entire bug. Any agent that writes CRLF and reports the file again at turn end after committing it can hit the same faulty comparison. Passing Windows tests for other agents do not establish that those agents are immune. ## What Changed Main independently merged a CRLF fix in #2482. After merging main, this PR retains the raw-byte fast path and batch-normalizes only raw mismatches. It uses main's shared `worktreedir.HashableEntry` safety check and retains main's CRLF and symlink regression tests. - Preserve the existing raw-byte comparison in `filterToUncommittedFiles`. - For safely readable regular files whose bytes differ from HEAD, reuse `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` to check whether Git normalization makes the content equal. Hash candidates in a batch; keep actual changes and paths whose normalized content cannot be confirmed. - Leave post-commit carry-forward logic unchanged. No new comparison API, temporary index, or attribute-copying implementation. - Preserve existing raw-equal acceptance, including legacy CRLF blobs. This change only adds a normalization check for raw mismatches; it does not redefine existing decisions for raw-equal files when attributes or filters change. ## Verification Merge update `776568da2` incorporates main at `c21ef7f00`. The resolved tree passed the focused turn-end tests, formatting, lint, and `mise run test:ci`, including race-enabled unit/integration tests and deterministic canaries. A final standard `mise run lint` passed after committing. The real-agent matrix below tested the earlier `97ace0cc2` commit and was not rerun for this merge. `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), and `mise run test:ci` passed, including race-enabled unit/integration tests and deterministic E2E canaries. Focused Windows Copilot `TestMultiSessionSequential` (git-refs) [passed on the fix](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34981705375) on its first attempt. The same scenario [failed on the unfixed base](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34981709072), including its retry, with a shadow branch recreated after post-commit cleanup. On the fix, both sessions instead reported no files modified at turn end. [Full cross-platform E2E validation](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34983337829) completed across 32 combinations. **26 passed; six Windows combinations failed.** This is not a clean cross-platform result. | Platform | Result on both checkpoint backends | | --- | --- | | Linux | All six real agents passed | | macOS | All six real agents passed | | Windows | Claude Code passed; Copilot, Codex, and OpenCode failed | Linux Cursor's installer returned HTTP 500 in the original matrix; its [isolated retry](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34983680912) passed the full suite. macOS Copilot `TestRapidSequentialCommits` and macOS Cursor `TestMultiSessionSequential` each passed after one test rerun. Existing unsupported-test skips remain in the reports. Windows failure investigation: - **Copilot:** [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34985025028) failed 33/32 tests (git-branch/git-refs), versus 25/26 on this fix. Failures include missing `tmux` and a separate existing post-commit CRLF mismatch: ended-session matching compares an LF commit blob with a CRLF shadow blob and declines to condense. The relevant comparison code is unchanged from the base. An isolated temporary Go test reproduces it without an agent: an LF shadow file matches after native Git commits it, while the same CRLF content does not. The original multi-session cleanup scenario passes on the fix with both backends. - **Codex:** [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34985029320) failed 23/11 tests, versus 17/16 on this fix. Both runs show subprocess `WaitDelay` errors and missing `tmux`; which tests hit the subprocess error varies between runs. - **OpenCode:** The fixed-branch runs failed 39/40 tests, with agent exit failures and missing `tmux`. The existing Windows dependency-link fallback also makes each test install dependencies again. [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34986273918) also failed: git-branch completed with 37 failed tests, and git-refs hit the suite’s 30-minute timeout after recording 33 failures, leaving tests unfinished. The baseline shows the same agent-exit and missing-`tmux` failure classes; it does not provide a complete git-refs comparison. The Windows failures prevent a clean cross-platform conclusion. No new failure class was identified, but the existing failures and incomplete OpenCode baseline limit regression confidence. The workflow expansion lives on `validation/turn-end-autocrlf-20260915`, outside this PR. Every fixed-branch job built commit `97ace0cc20c8b208a4fbdc77f4b08b314e1f517b`. The turn-end regression test covers a CRLF working copy of an LF commit, genuinely modified CRLF content, staged changes compared against HEAD, missing paths, legacy CRLF raw matches, and input ordering. `BenchmarkFilterToUncommittedFiles` measures the complete turn-end filter, including repository and blob reads. Example local medians on Apple M2, three samples of ten iterations each: | Case | Time | | --- | ---: | | Raw match, 1 file | 1.66 ms | | Raw match, 100 files | 19.23 ms | | CRLF normalization, 1 file | 11.47 ms | | CRLF normalization, 100 files | 39.05 ms | Raw matches need no hashing subprocess. Raw mismatches reuse the existing batched Git hashing helper. In the focused Windows Copilot run, the logged filter-and-normalize step took 20 ms and 46 ms for the two sessions; total agent-stop hooks took 206 ms and 232 ms. These are individual observations, not a performance bound. This addresses the case we hit where hooks were firing correctly, but the commit happened in a repo/worktree that did not have matching local session state, so the commit had nothing to link and missed the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. ## What changed - Adds the `session adopt` subcommand under `entire session`. - Reads source session state from the source worktree’s `.git/entire-sessions` store. - Supports either an explicit session ID or a single recent active source session. - Filters shared source stores by the requested `--from` worktree, using `WorktreeID` when available and canonical path fallback otherwise. - Supports independent repo/worktree adoption by writing target-local session state. - Supports same-git-common-dir linked worktree adoption by moving the shared session state to the current worktree instead of rejecting it. - Rejects no-op adoption when source and target resolve to the same worktree. - Validates that a preserved live transcript path is owned by the source session’s registered agent. - Keeps the live transcript path because the transcript belongs to the continuing agent session, not necessarily the target repo. - Seeds `FilesTouched` from current target repo changes so the next commit can pass the staged-file overlap check. - Resets target-local checkpoint/transcript bookkeeping so long-running source sessions do not inherit stale checkpoint offsets, checkpoint IDs, prompt windows, or legacy transcript fields. - Preserves cumulative turn/context metrics while anchoring the adopted prompt window at the current source turn count. - Leaves `AttachedManually` false because adoption is not `entire session attach`. This closes the sibling-worktree gap from #573 through an explicit agent/user command, without adding hook-time automatic matching across worktrees. ## Verification - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run TestSessionAdopt -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run TestSessionAdopt_MovesSameStoreSessionIntoCurrentWorktree -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run 'Test(SessionAdopt|PrepareCommitMsg)' -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -count=1` - `mise run lint` - `mise run check` `mise run check` passed locally after rebasing on current `main`, including lint, integration tests, Vogon canary, and roger-roger canary. Latest commit/checkpoint: - `db9ada812c38dc67e0750d4e2633662316ffb5bf` - `Entire-Checkpoint: 48521e055655` Push output confirmed `entire/checkpoints/v1` was already up to date on the checkpoint remote. ## Caveats This is explicit adoption, not automatic discovery. Agents or users should run it from the target repo/worktree before committing, and the source transcript path must still be readable on the same machine.","state":null,"user":null,"assignees":null,"labels":null,"milestone":null,"state_reason":null,"comments":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"closed_at":null,"display_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1472","display_title":"feat: adopt active sessions across repos and worktrees"},{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1573","title":"Add hidden experts CLI command","issue_number":1573,"body":" https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/709 ## What is this? Adds a hidden/labs CLI command: **`entire experts`**. ## Problem

Claude Code keeps a session's transcript under `~/.claude/projects/<working dir>/`. When a session moves into a worktree with `EnterWorktree`, Claude writes the whole transcript under the worktree's folder. The path its hooks reported at session start never exists, and hooks report the new path only at turn end.

If the agent commits in that first turn, the commit gets an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, but condensation finds no live transcript at the recorded path. It also finds no stored copy, because no turn has ended yet. So condensation fails with "live transcript is empty or unreadable", and the trailer points to a checkpoint that is never written.

Main has the same bug. #2531 handles a session's home worktree, but it doesn't follow a transcript that Claude moved.

## Fix

When the recorded transcript is missing, `resolveTranscriptPath` now looks for the session's file in the agent's session folders for each worktree of the repo, and for any directory inside one, the current worktree first. It uses the first file it finds, and records that path in the session state so later reads go straight to it.

The lookup runs only when the recorded path is one the agent would derive for the session's home worktree or a directory inside it (Claude names its folder after the launch directory, so a session started in `<repo>/frontend` records `<home>-frontend`), so attached or imported sessions with custom paths are left alone. External agents are skipped, because looking up their session folder starts a process. Only Claude Code's flat folder layout (one sibling folder per working directory) is searched; agents with a nested layout, such as Cursor, return before any worktree is listed. `ctx` is passed through to the callers so the lookup can list worktrees.

## Tests

- The moved transcript is found from inside the worktree and from the main checkout, and the state follows it.
- A session whose file is in no worktree's folder still reports it missing.
- A session launched from a subdirectory is followed whether it moves to the worktree root or the same subdirectory.
- A custom recorded path, or one under a different projects folder, isn't second-guessed.
- A test that runs the commit hooks: a first-turn commit made after moving into a worktree gets its checkpoint written. Run for a launch at the repo root and in a subdirectory; both fail on the base commit (no checkpoint, stale transcript path).

## Live check (real Claude Code, headless)

One turn: `EnterWorktree`, edit a file, commit.

| Build | Launched in | Trailer | Checkpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (`fedd31ca10`, this PR's parent) | repo root | yes | not written ("condensation failed") |
| this branch | repo root | yes | written |
| base | `frontend/` | yes | not written ("condensation failed") |
| this branch | `frontend/` | yes | written |

Launched from `frontend/`, Claude wrote the moved transcript under the worktree root's folder.

## Not in this PR

- Amend and post-rewrite still use the stored-copy fallback.
- Worktree paths that go through a symlink may not match how Claude names its folders.
- A session that changes folders in turn 2 or later, while its old file still exists, reads the stale file until the turn ends.

## Problem

Two paths count the same model calls in two checkpoints when a commit lands in the middle of a turn.

**A. Pending tokens after a mid-turn commit.** The agent commits mid-turn, so a checkpoint stores the turn so far and `TokenStart` moves to the commit's transcript end. At Stop, `resolveTurnTokenUsage` counts the whole turn from the turn start and adds it to `CheckpointTokenUsage`. If no model call followed the commit, the next condensation's recount from `TokenStart` is empty and falls back to that pending usage, so it stores the pre-commit calls again. Attach has the same fallback. Live runs on main showed this on Claude Code, Codex and Pi.

**B. A Claude message split by a commit.** Claude writes one transcript line per content block, all with the same `message.id` and identical usage (checked on 4,339 multi-line messages). With parallel tool calls, the tools run between those lines, so a `git commit` from an earlier tool can land before the message's later lines. The checkpoint before the commit counts the message, and the one after counts it again, because dedupe by id only covers `[startLine, end)`.

Replaying 7 real long Claude sessions through main's hooks: session totals were exact, but in 2 sessions the checkpoints added up to one call more than Claude's own total (+3,112 and +1,061 output tokens), both from B.

## Change

**Pending tokens are scoped to what no checkpoint stored.** The session total (`TokenUsage`) still gets the whole turn. For transcript-derived usage, `resolveTurnTokenUsage` also returns a recount callback (`TurnTokenRecount`). `ApplyTurnTokenUsage` calls it under the session-state lock: if a condensation moved `TokenStart` during this turn (compared with `TokenStart` at turn start, now kept in `PrePromptState`), the pending part is recounted from `TokenStart`; otherwise it is the whole turn. Subagent tokens keep their existing rescope.

- Codex recounts with `CalculateTokenUsage(parent, from)` and keeps the inventory's subagent fields.
- Hook-reported (Cursor) and out-of-band (Antigravity, Droid) usage have no recount: their mid-turn checkpoints store none of the turn, so the whole turn stays pending.

**A transcript rewritten shorter than the token offset is handled at turn start** (Claude Code and Pi). `entire session resume --force` restores the agent transcript from an older checkpoint, leaving the offset past its end. Without handling, a mid-turn commit stores none of the turn's earlier tokens, and usage still pending from before the resume is lost with its erased lines. `CapturePrePromptState` now:
- moves the offset down to the turn-start transcript position, only when that position is known (the file exists), with a compare-and-set under the session lock so a concurrent condensation wins; the turn's baseline records the rebased offset;
- in the same mutation, moves the pending main-agent usage into a new `RewrittenTokenUsage` field. No recount can find those lines again, so the next checkpoint (or attach) adds it as-is; it is cleared only by the window reset after a checkpoint is written, and an ended state holding it is not deleted as an orphan. Subagent totals stay pending.

Limited to Claude Code and Pi, whose usage is a per-line sum: Codex's is a delta of a cumulative total, OpenCode's export can read short when stale, Cursor's comes from the Stop hook (the fallback already stores it), and Copilot recounts the whole transcript for its session total.

**A Claude message counts in the window holding its first line.** `CalculateTotalTokenUsage` skips the first non-sidechain assistant message at or after `startLine` when an earlier line of the same message sits before `startLine`. The backward scan stops at the first assistant line with another id, so it is bounded.

## Tests

- **Integration** (`token_midturn_double_count_test.go`): mid-turn commit then Stop with no later call; clean-tree commit-all; two commits in one turn; missing pre-prompt state; subagent finishing after the commit; only the straddling tail after the commit; a transcript rewritten shorter than `TokenStart`; Codex, Cursor and Antigravity. Each checks the session total and that checkpoints plus pending equal the true total.
- **Rewrite then mid-turn commit:** one commit, two commits, a rewritten turn as long as the old offset, and a pending turn rewritten away; each asserts the mid-turn checkpoint holds the right tokens (fails without the fix). Unit tests cover the rebase and carry, a missing transcript, a concurrent advance, a lock timeout, the agent allow-list, the carry on the recount/fallback/attach paths, and its reset.
- **Unit:** Claude straddle cases (boundary at turn start, interleaved tool_result, sidechain, malformed line, start past EOF); `ApplyTurnTokenUsage` and `SaveStep` rescoping; `resolveTurnTokenUsage` returning a recount for transcript usage.
- **Replay** of the 7 real sessions: checkpoints and session totals now match Claude's own totals exactly. Subagent undercounts are unchanged (separate fix).
- **Live runs** (Claude haiku, Codex, Pi; 6-turn script with mid-turn, user and subagent commits): checkpoints + pending equal each agent's own totals on every token field. Before this PR, Pi's were 29,025 input / 11 calls against a true 23,562 / 9. Codex shows one extra `api_call_count` from a duplicate `token_count` event (separate issue); its self-committing subagent's early calls are the known subagent gap.
- **Live forced resume** (Claude haiku: 3 turns with commits, `entire session resume --force` to the first checkpoint, a turn with a mid-turn commit): the offset was rebased 65 → 39 and the post-resume checkpoint held that turn's pre-commit call (the build before it stored a stale call instead). That run still missed the pending call erased by the resume, which the carry now covers.
- Unit, token integration tests and lint pass.

## Not in this PR

- A partial trailing line racing the straddle check.
- OpenCode updates tokens in place, which may undercount across a boundary (unverified).
- `countTranscriptItems` counts a partial trailing line that `SliceFromLine` skips.
- Older Claude versions whose output rises across a message's lines would make part B undercount slightly.
- Attach does not run under the session lock (existing).
- A rewrite that drops pending lines but leaves the transcript at least as long as the old offset isn't detected.
- OpenCode undo: its transcript export isn't refreshed at turn start, so the rebase doesn't see it.

This is fix 2 of 6 from the per-agent token check; each fix is its own PR off main.

## Summary

This fixes a metadata loss bug in checkpoint condensation for Claude Code sessions that spawn Task subagents.

Before this change, live session handling could see subagent token usage, but the later condensation step recalculated token usage without passing the session's subagent transcript directory. As a result, `SubagentTokens` were silently dropped from the committed checkpoint metadata written to `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

## Issue

Claude Code stores Task subagent transcripts separately from the main transcript:

```text
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
```

The lifecycle path already knows that convention and passes the subagent directory into token/file extraction. Condensation did not. Both condensation paths called:

```go
agent.CalculateTokenUsage(ctx, ag, data.Transcript, checkpointTranscriptStart, "")
```

For subagent-aware agents, the empty directory intentionally disables subagent transcript reads. That means the main transcript token totals survived, but spawned subagent token totals disappeared when checkpoint metadata was committed.

## How to reproduce

One reproducible shape is:

1. Enable Entire in a repo and start a Claude Code session.
2. Have Claude invoke the `Task` tool so the main transcript contains a Task `tool_use` and a corresponding `tool_result` with an `agentId`, for example `agentId: sub1`.
3. Ensure the subagent transcript exists at:

   ```text
   <main-transcript-dir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-sub1.jsonl
   ```

   and contains assistant usage metadata.
4. Let the normal stop hook run. At this point live session state can include subagent token usage because the lifecycle path passes the subagent directory.
5. Make a user commit so the post-commit hook condenses the session into committed checkpoint metadata.
6. Inspect the committed checkpoint metadata from `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

Before this fix, the condensed checkpoint metadata had main token usage but no `subagent_tokens` field, even though the subagent transcript was present and readable.

The added regression test builds that shape directly: a main Claude transcript with a Task result referencing `sub1`, a matching `agent-sub1.jsonl` subagent transcript, and a condensation call that verifies `SubagentTokens` survive in committed metadata.

## Impact

This affects checkpoint metadata for Claude Code sessions that use Task subagents.

Observed effects:

- `entire/checkpoints/v1` underreports total work done by spawned subagents.
- Later checkpoint consumers such as activity, explain/status views, or metadata sync consumers cannot recover those subagent token totals from the committed metadata.
- The bug is silent: checkpoint writes succeed, but the committed metadata is incomplete.

The code path is shared through the `SubagentAwareExtractor` token interface, so passing the directory also keeps condensation aligned with other subagent-aware implementations that use the same transcript layout convention.

## Fix

- Add `subagentsDirForTranscript(transcriptPath, sessionID)` in the strategy package.
- Pass the derived subagent directory into `agent.CalculateTokenUsage` from both condensation paths:
  - shadow-branch extraction with live-transcript preference
  - direct live-transcript extraction
- Add `TestCondenseSession_ClaudeSubagentTokenUsage` to lock the end-to-end condensation behavior.

## Problem
OpenCode emits a user `message.updated` event before the `message.part.updated` event containing the prompt text. The plugin starts the turn from that metadata event with an empty prompt so a fast agent commit still sees an ACTIVE session. Because the message was then marked as seen, the later text part was ignored and checkpoints lost the user prompt.

The first version of this PR kept a marker for those promptless starts and fired `turn-start` again when the text arrived. That recovered the prompt, but `turn-start` is not a prompt setter. It captures pre-prompt Git state, creates a new `TurnID`, recalculates prompt attribution, and clears `LastCheckpointID` and `TurnCheckpointIDs`.

The timing this fallback exists for makes that destructive. A checkpoint may already have been created between the empty metadata event and the text event.

The new integration regression exercises exactly that order:

```
message.updated
  → turn-start with empty prompt
  → agent commit and checkpoint
  → message.part.updated with prompt text
```

Against the second-`turn-start` implementation, the prompt was recorded, but the original turn ID changed, the pre-prompt snapshot was replaced, attribution was recalculated, and both checkpoint fields were cleared.

## Fix
Keep the early empty `turn-start`, but repair the missing text through a new internal `PromptUpdate` lifecycle event.

`PromptUpdate` writes the late text to `prompt.txt` and updates session `LastPrompt`. It does not call `CapturePrePromptState` or `InitializeSession`, so it cannot start another logical turn or reset checkpoint bookkeeping.
The file and state updates run inside `MutateSessionState`. Checkpoint condensation clears `prompt.txt` while holding the same session lock, so either ordering is safe:

- If repair gets the lock first, condensation sees and checkpoints the prompt before clearing the file.
- If condensation gets the lock first, repair writes the prompt after condensation finishes, leaving it available for turn-end finalization.
The OpenCode plugin keeps a `promptlessTurnStarts` marker per message. Empty text updates leave the marker pending; the first non-empty part sends one synchronous `prompt-update`; later duplicates do nothing. Multiple pending messages are tracked independently. The set is cleared on session switches, session deletion, and server disposal.

The generated plugin template and the checked-in dogfood plugin remain byte-identical.

## Cost
The plugin does expected `O(1)` set work per event and keeps `O(P)` additional state for `P` promptless messages awaiting text.
A late repair starts one synchronous hook subprocess, reads and rewrites `prompt.txt` in `O(Q + L)` time for existing prompt data `Q` and incoming prompt length `L`, and performs `O(S)` session-state I/O for state size `S`.

It performs no worktree scan. The earlier second-`turn-start` path repeated work proportional to worktree size `F`, including both status walks used by turn initialization.

In the real OpenCode run, the empty `turn-start` took 74 ms and the subsequent `prompt-update` took 5 ms in the same repository.

## Verification

- [x] Regression test fails before the fix by capturing only the empty fallback prompt.
- [x] Regression test passes after the fix with `turn-start("")` followed by `prompt-update("preserve this prompt")`.
- [x] Duplicate text-part updates do not trigger additional hooks.
- [x] OpenCode package tests pass.
- [x] `mise run check` passes, including lint, race-enabled unit and integration tests, and E2E canary tests.
- [x] The generated plugin template matches the repository’s installed OpenCode plugin.
- [x] A real `opencode run` session produced a checkpoint containing the complete original prompt.
- [x] A checkpoint occurring between the metadata event and prompt-text event preserves the original turn and checkpoint bookkeeping.
- [x] Prompt repair avoids repeating the complete `turn-start` lifecycle.

## Scope
`PromptUpdate` is an internal lifecycle event used only by OpenCode in this change. There are no new CLI flags, settings, dependencies, or changes to other agent integrations.

## Summary

The root corruption is git's own bug, not Entire's, and cannot be prevented from a hook: git (and go-git v6, independently) treats a missing \`.git/index\` (ENOENT) as an empty in-core index, and \`git status\` renames a fresh index over the real one as a side effect — so any concurrent process running \`git status\` at the wrong moment can cause a commit to record an empty tree. The previously-merged mitigation (#2143) already scrubs Entire's own \`git status\` calls, but by the time any hook runs, git has already read the index — prevention was never available from here, only detection.

**A second, previously-unknown data-loss bug was found while investigating, and that one is Entire's, and is fixed here**: when an empty-tree commit happens, Entire's \`post-commit\` hook still ran condensation on it — consuming the session's pending checkpoint data. So even if a user notices and runs \`git reset --mixed HEAD~1\` to recover, the checkpoint data backing that work was already gone. \`post-commit\` now detects an empty-tree commit and skips condensation entirely; \`prepare-commit-msg\` warns before the commit lands, naming the recovery command and \`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0\`.

## Evidence
- Real repro against a binary built from \`origin/main\`: staged files silently committed as an empty tree, exit 0, files still on disk — confirmed with real git, not simulated.

Follow-up to #2029 (trail 1073), from re-reviewing it after the fixes landed.

## Problem

A session state can carry `EndedAt` without `PhaseEnded`. `State.IsEnded` exists for exactly that shape, and its doc names it:

> Both halves matter and neither implies the other in practice: Phase is what the state machine sets, EndedAt is what the finalizing write stamps, and a state file can carry one without the other (a legacy record, or a partial write). Callers that filter for active sessions must agree on this rule, so it lives here rather than being re-spelled at each site.

The sweep re-spelled it, and its two halves ended up disagreeing. `isSweepableZombie` correctly used `IsEnded()` to route non-ended zombies to `finalizeExitedSessions`, then three lines later re-tested `Phase == PhaseEnded` before nominating a condense.

For a half-ended state, **both halves declined**:

- `finalizeExitedSessions` skips it, because `OwnerExited()` returns false once `IsEnded()`.
- the condense path skipped it on the phase test.

`entire doctor` does not reach it either — `classifySession`’s phase switch falls through to `default: return nil`. So the only thing that ever touched such a session was the 7-day stale purge, which **deletes** the uncondensed content rather than condensing it.

## Fix

Three gates had to move together, and each is independently load-bearing — reverting any one alone fails the new end-to-end test (verified, see below):

| Gate | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `isSweepableZombie` | Drop the `Phase` re-test. Reaching that line already means `IsEnded()`, so the test could only ever exclude the half-ended shape. |
| `runSessionSweep` | Both loop guards keyed on `Phase`, so a nominated half-ended session was skipped before *and* after the fresh re-load. |
| `IsCondensableEndedSession` | Same `Phase` test, so a session that survived both guards was still reported non-condensable. |

## Blast radius

`IsCondensableEndedSession` is shared with the PostCommit stale-session warning, which now also counts half-ended sessions holding uncondensed content. That is the same correction, not a side effect: they are stale and actionable by doctor for the same reason a `PhaseEnded` one is.

## Deliberately not changed

`doctor`’s `classifySession` has the same phase-switch gap, so a half-ended session is still not listed by `entire doctor`. It is a separate command on a separate path, and the sweep now condenses these before doctor would have to. Happy to fold it in if you would rather have the two consistent.

## Verification

`TestRunSessionSweep_CondensesHalfEndedSession` builds the shape end to end (`Phase: PhaseIdle`, `EndedAt` 48h old, `StepCount: 2`, shadow ref present) and asserts the sweep actually condensed it — not merely that the predicate stopped matching. Mutation-probed all three gates:

```
revert isSweepableZombie          -> FAIL "a half-ended session with uncondensed steps must nominate the sweep"
revert runSessionSweep guards     -> FAIL "the half-ended session must no longer hold uncondensed content"
revert IsCondensableEndedSession  -> FAIL "the sweep must have condensed the half-ended session, not just skipped it"
```

Plus a table case in `TestIsSweepableZombie`. `mise run check` clean (fmt, lint 0 issues, unit + integration + canary all green).

Add a sidecar commit log that enables session timeline reconstruction from any checkpoint, without complex cross-referencing or git log scanning.

### The problem

Today, if you want to see "what commits happened during this session," you'd need to cross-reference checkpoint IDs across git history, session metadata, and the checkpoint branch. For a UI timeline view — where you pick checkpoint 4 and want to see the full session history including checkpoints 1-3 — this requires expensive backward lookups across potentially weeks of git history.

### The approach

Each time PostCommit condenses a session, we append a one-line JSON entry to `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/commits.jsonl`:

```jsonl
{"hash":"abc123...","short_hash":"abc123d","subject":"Add login","timestamp":"2026-04-16T12:11:06Z","checkpoint_id":"a3b2c4d5e6f7","session_id":"..."}
```

This file accumulates across the session. When checkpoint N is condensed, its `commits.jsonl` contains entries for all N commits — no backward lookup needed. The log is:

- **Built in-memory before condensation** so it's included in the checkpoint tree it belongs to (not written too late)
- **Persisted to filesystem after condensation** so the next checkpoint picks up the full timeline
- **Written to both v1 and v2** checkpoint trees via `WriteCommittedOptions.CommitLog`

### What this enables (future)

- **Session timeline UI**: Read one checkpoint → render full commit history with expandable details
- **Orphaned checkpoint detection**: "There was a checkpoint here, but it was rebased away"
- **Foundation for Phase 2**: Adding `Change-Id` trailers to capture mid-turn commits (without checkpoint trailers) in the timeline

### What this does NOT change

- No new git trailers
- No changes to SaveStep, condensation logic, or session state machine
- No tree-building changes (`commits.jsonl` flows through existing `WriteCommittedOptions`)
- No consumers yet — this is write-side plumbing

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: append/read round-trip, nonexistent file handling, commit subject extraction
- [x] Integration test: `commits.jsonl` present in v1 checkpoint tree after PostCommit
- [x] Integration test: second checkpoint contains entries for both commits (accumulation)
- [x] `mise run check` (fmt + lint + test:ci + e2e canary) passes

Adds a **RED** regression test that reproduces and proves a silent `prepare-commit-msg` / `post-commit` mismatch: a commit can end up carrying an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer that points at a checkpoint **that was never materialized locally** (a *dangling trailer*).

This is a test-only, TDD-first PR — the test is **intentionally failing** and documents the invariant a follow-up fix must restore. CI will be red until the fix lands.

New file: `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/phase_postcommit_dangling_trailer_test.go` → `TestPostCommit_IdleSession_NewLiveTranscriptEdits_DanglingTrailer`.

## Scenario (reconstructed from a real Pi session)

1. A session is condensed (clears `state.FilesTouched`, stamps `LastCheckpointID`), then goes IDLE.
2. A new turn arrives **without a TurnStart** (rapidly submitted prompt), so the session stays IDLE and `SaveStep` never repopulates `FilesTouched`. No shadow branch exists for the new edits yet.
3. The agent edits files and commits them.

## Root cause

- **`PrepareCommitMsg`** re-extracts the edited files from the **live** transcript (`sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript`), overlaps them with the staged files, and **adds the trailer**.
- **`PostCommit`** computes `filesTouchedBefore` only from *persisted* `state.FilesTouched` for non-ACTIVE sessions (the active-only fallback in `manual_commit_hooks.go:1246-1252`) and never passes the committed files as an overlap signal. With `FilesTouched` empty and no staged files, `hasNew` collapses to false and/or the guard in `shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck` (`len(filesTouchedBefore)==0 → return false`) rejects condensation.

Net: the commit keeps the trailer, but no checkpoint is ever written for it.

## What the test proves

- **Premise passes** — `PrepareCommitMsg` adds the trailer purely from the live transcript (log: `prepare-commit-msg: trailer added ... checkpoint_id=...`).
- **Invariant fails** — after commit + `PostCommit`, `entire/checkpoints/v1` does not exist and `LastCheckpointID` stays pinned to the prior checkpoint. The trailer dangles.

## Notes for the fix (out of scope here)

- `TestPostCommit_IdleSession_NoTranscriptFallbackForCarryForward` **explicitly asserts IDLE sessions must NOT re-extract** from the transcript (it guards an earlier carry-forward + 3s sentinel-wait regression). A naive "always re-extract for IDLE" fix would re-break it.
- Safer direction: **persist the positive prepare-hook file association**, and **log a warning** whenever a commit carries a trailer with no materialized checkpoint.
- Separately worth investigating: why Pi emitted no TurnStart for that rapidly-submitted third turn.

## Verification

- `mise run fmt` / `mise run lint` → clean (0 issues).
- New test fails **only** at the invariant; premise and the two related existing IDLE tests pass.

## What Copilot changed

Copilot CLI no longer puts `outputTokens` on `assistant.message`. Starting with 1.0.94, it writes a `session.usage_record` for each API call (main agent and subagents) instead. The record carries `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens` and `reasoningTokens`, and joins to its message by `apiCallId`. Local sessions from 1.0.83 through 1.0.93 have neither field, and 1.0.63 and earlier have only `outputTokens`. As a result, every checkpoint from a current Copilot session recorded zero tokens.

## Audit

| Path | Verdict | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `copilotcli.CalculateTokenUsage`, sliced read | Wrong for the new format: it reads only `assistant.message.outputTokens`, which no longer exists, so the result is 0 | Sum `session.usage_record` within the slice, and keep `outputTokens` as the fallback |
| `copilotcli.CalculateTokenUsage`, full read with `session.shutdown` | Wrong on every version. `inputTokens` includes cache read and write (Copilot's own `tokenDetails.input` equals input − cacheRead − cacheWrite), so cached input was counted twice. Only the last shutdown was read, but a resumed session writes one per run: per-run on 1.0.3 and cumulative on 1.0.97 | Normalized to fresh input. Each shutdown is classified by its request count, which matches the `assistant.message` count it covers on every release seen: the run's messages for a per-run shutdown, every message so far for a cumulative one. A run whose calls all have records is counted from the records. A shutdown that matches neither reading is ignored |
| `agentimport` Copilot importer | Delegates to the calculator, so it inherited the zero counts | Fixed through the calculator; comment updated |
| `compact` Copilot `output_tokens` | Empty on the new format | Joins `session.usage_record` by `apiCallId` and sets `output_tokens` plus fresh `input_tokens`, matching Claude's compact lines |
| `strategy` session-total backfill | Correct. It runs a full read at condensation, so it picks up the fix | No change; test added |
| Copilot hook payloads | No token fields | n/a |
| `AGENT.md` | Described the old format only | Rewritten with the observed format facts |

Confirmed on live 1.0.94 and 1.0.97 sessions: `reasoningTokens` is a subset of `outputTokens`, and `cacheWriteTokens` maps to `CacheCreationTokens`. The per-turn sums of `usage_record` equal the `session.shutdown` totals exactly, so checkpoint totals now add up to the session total. Subagent calls are counted in the main totals, and `SubagentTokens` stays unset as before.

## Tests

- `usage_record_test.go`, using a scrubbed 1.0.94 capture: each slice holds only its own calls, the slices sum to the normalized shutdown total, a full read before shutdown gives the same total, and a sliced read ignores the shutdown.
- A scrubbed 1.0.97 resumed session where the second shutdown is cumulative. A full read must equal the record sum (64/151364/23237/898/8), with and without the records, and the slices must add up to it.
- Tests for per-run shutdowns as on 1.0.3, a shutdown matching neither reading, mixed formats (no double counting), and input clamping.
- Compact, import and backfill tests for the new format.
- `TestCalculateTokenUsage_SessionShutdown` and `_MultiModel` pinned the inclusive input values (64807 and 1500). They now expect the fresh values, 22082 and 1150.

Adds `strategy_options.sync_prompts` (default `true`). When set to `false`, prompt-bearing content is kept out of committed checkpoints, so it never reaches the checkpoint remote. Checkpoint metadata, attribution, files touched, token usage, and metrics are still recorded and synced.

```json
{ "strategy_options": { "sync_prompts": false } }
```

## What is omitted

- `prompt.txt`
- `full.jsonl` / `transcript.jsonl` and their image assets (also `TranscriptPath`, which the writer would otherwise re-read from disk)
- subagent transcripts and task descriptions (`task.json` records `transcript omitted by settings`)
- AI summaries (`SessionSummary` backfills are dropped)
- review prompts and investigate topics
- skill-event `Native` fields and transcript anchors (Pi records full slash-command invocations, arguments included)

## Design

- **Enforced at one seam:** `checkpoint.Open` wraps `Stores.Persistent` in `promptOmittingStore` (`checkpoint/prompt_omission.go`). Every persistent write path goes through it: condensation, finalize backfill, attach, import, and summary backfill. That covers both backends and mirrors. The wrapper preserves `AuthorReader`. Reads are untouched. Ephemeral shadow writes are unaffected because they are never pushed.
- **Narrow, cheap settings read:** `settings.LoadPromptSyncDisabled` mirrors `LoadCheckpointsConfig`. It spawns no git subprocesses and is fail-soft about unrelated settings breakage. The local file wins over the base file.
- **Fails closed:** a value that cannot be interpreted (non-boolean, unparseable or unreadable file) withholds prompts. The strict `Load` path also rejects a non-boolean `sync_prompts`.
- **Local opt-out allowed:** the setting is honored from `settings.local.json`. A tracked local file is honored for this key too, because the setting can only withhold data.

## Testing

- Unit: `omitPromptContent` per request type, wrapper pass-through and `AuthorReader` preservation, settings precedence and fail-closed cases.
- `Open`: write and read back under both `git-branch` and `git-refs` primaries.
- Integration (`sync_prompts_test.go`): full hook flow plus pre-push to a bare remote. The test scans every remote object and asserts the prompt marker is absent. A control test confirms the marker is present with default settings.
- `mise run check`: lint is clean. The unit, integration, and canary suites pass, except three reftable tests (`TestLocalReads_ReftableProcessCount`, `TestLocalRefReads_ReftableProcessCount`, `TestReplacedCommits_ReftableRepository`). Those fail identically on `main` locally (git 2.47 cannot migrate reflogs), so CI should be authoritative for them.

## Follow-up / for review

- Summary generation still runs locally and its result is then discarded. Skipping it when `sync_prompts=false` would save work.

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

Durable storage is the one open piece — this issue tracks it.

**Problem, one line:** condensation builds one `checkpoint.WriteOptions` per session with no

- `SubagentEnd` → small session-state entry only: correlation ID, agent type, description,
  **declared transcript path**, files touched, tokens. No shadow-tree write.
- Condensation → read the declared paths, sanitize → externalize images → redact, store.
- Path gone by then → keep the pointer record, metadata says transcript unavailable.

two mirrored ones (that duplication is what made unreachable code look durable); no misleading

stop hook and nowhere else. Dropping it means guessing layouts again — the bug #1958 fixed.

**Premise verified:** agents do *not* clean up subagent transcripts (CC 180 files / 121 older

otherwise is wrong, and it is what justified capturing mid-turn.

On Entire CLI 0.11.3 (I also checked current `main` and the nightlies, which have no change here), one shadow branch `entire/<base>-<worktree>` reached **3,643 commits and 168 GB of loose objects** in about 12 days. That helped fill a 926 GB laptop disk to 0 bytes free.

Each shadow commit stores `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl`, the **whole** transcript so far. Two long-running sessions in one worktree (3,299 and 502 turns) never committed code in that worktree, so the branch was never condensed. Every turn re-stored a transcript of 50–320 MB uncompressed. Sampled blobs show the same session id again and again at growing sizes.

## Why nothing reclaims it

- Entire writes these as **loose** objects (go-git `SetEncodedObject`) and never packs.
- `docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` (ENT-241) tells users to set `gc.auto 0`, so `git gc --auto` never runs either.
- The branch is reachable, so `git prune` can't free it. Only a manual repack shrinks it. Successive snapshots of an append-only JSONL delta to almost nothing: a synthetic reproduction packed 243 MiB of loose snapshots into 16.9 MiB.

`checkpoint-scenarios.md` limitation #5 acknowledges that storage "grows linearly with session length × number of commits". Since the transcript itself grows with the session, the total is effectively **quadratic** for long sessions (orchestrator-style agents run for days).

## Suggestion

Make each turn's storage cost proportional to what the turn **added**. Possible ways:

1. **Chunk `full.jsonl` in shadow commits at fixed, line-aligned offsets.** Committed checkpoints already chunk at 50 MiB; smaller chunks, say 1–4 MiB, would work here. An append-only transcript's unchanged prefix chunks would then hash to the same blobs and be stored once. Only the tail chunk is new each turn.
2. Or write each turn's objects into a pack (or run a bounded `git repack -d` after condensation or cleanup), so Entire doesn't leave the reclaim to a gc it tells users to disable.
3. Consider surfacing very large or long-lived shadow branches in `entire status` / `entire doctor`. A session that never commits in its home worktree pins its branch indefinitely, and nothing tells the user.
