Adds `strategy_options.sync_prompts` (default `true`). When set to `false`, prompt-bearing content is kept out of committed checkpoints, so it never reaches the checkpoint remote. Checkpoint metadata, attribution, files touched, token usage, and metrics are still recorded and synced.

```json
{ "strategy_options": { "sync_prompts": false } }
```

## What is omitted

- `prompt.txt`
- `full.jsonl` / `transcript.jsonl` and their image assets (also `TranscriptPath`, which the writer would otherwise re-read from disk)
- subagent transcripts and task descriptions (`task.json` records `transcript omitted by settings`)
- AI summaries (`SessionSummary` backfills are dropped)
- review prompts and investigate topics
- skill-event `Native` fields and transcript anchors (Pi records full slash-command invocations, arguments included)

## Design

- **Enforced at one seam:** `checkpoint.Open` wraps `Stores.Persistent` in `promptOmittingStore` (`checkpoint/prompt_omission.go`). Every persistent write path goes through it: condensation, finalize backfill, attach, import, and summary backfill. That covers both backends and mirrors. The wrapper preserves `AuthorReader`. Reads are untouched. Ephemeral shadow writes are unaffected because they are never pushed.
- **Narrow, cheap settings read:** `settings.LoadPromptSyncDisabled` mirrors `LoadCheckpointsConfig`. It spawns no git subprocesses and is fail-soft about unrelated settings breakage. The local file wins over the base file.
- **Fails closed:** a value that cannot be interpreted (non-boolean, unparseable or unreadable file) withholds prompts. The strict `Load` path also rejects a non-boolean `sync_prompts`.
- **Local opt-out allowed:** the setting is honored from `settings.local.json`. A tracked local file is honored for this key too, because the setting can only withhold data.

## Testing

- Unit: `omitPromptContent` per request type, wrapper pass-through and `AuthorReader` preservation, settings precedence and fail-closed cases.
- `Open`: write and read back under both `git-branch` and `git-refs` primaries.
- Integration (`sync_prompts_test.go`): full hook flow plus pre-push to a bare remote. The test scans every remote object and asserts the prompt marker is absent. A control test confirms the marker is present with default settings.
- `mise run check`: lint is clean. The unit, integration, and canary suites pass, except three reftable tests (`TestLocalReads_ReftableProcessCount`, `TestLocalRefReads_ReftableProcessCount`, `TestReplacedCommits_ReftableRepository`). Those fail identically on `main` locally (git 2.47 cannot migrate reflogs), so CI should be authoritative for them.

## Follow-up / for review

- Summary generation still runs locally and its result is then discarded. Skipping it when `sync_prompts=false` would save work.
- Product call: should unparseable settings really withhold prompts for repos that never opted out? This PR chooses fail-closed.

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

After a redo that stamps no fresh trailer (pure, or partial with no session's other work), which condenses nothing, post-commit (`reconcileRedoneFiles`) drops them from this worktree's sessions' touched files when the commit holds the recorded content, as carry-forward would. Only held files go through that check; other touched files, steps and transcript growth stay pending untouched. - `openRepositoryTimed` is extracted to keep `PrepareCommitMsg` under the `maintidx` limit; the `open_repository` span no longer includes the redo lookup. - The deleted-checkpoint list is loaded once per commit, each dropped commit's diff is computed once, and store lookups are memoized. - Documented in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and `docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md`. ## Deliberately not changed Whenever a fresh trailer is stamped, a redundant checkpoint is preferred to a lost or dangling link: - On a partial redo (redone files staged together with other files), the mid-turn agent fast path still stamps a fresh trailer. Transcripts miss edits made through shell commands (`sed -i`, formatters, codegen), so it cannot rule out new work. - Post-commit judges overlap without the redo, so a session that only redid work may fold into another session's fresh checkpoint. An earlier commit on this branch excluded redone paths there, but that left a fresh trailer with no checkpoint behind it when a stale ACTIVE session tracked only redone files, or when a read-only ACTIVE session was gated out by a redo-only claimant. ## Tests Regression tests in `manual_commit_redo_test.go`. The fixture writes real checkpoints for its trailers through the hooks' own store. Each test fails without its fix (mutation-checked), except the aborted-commit one, which two independent guards cover. Every test that expects a fresh trailer runs prepare, the commit and post-commit, and asserts the trailer resolves in the checkpoint store: - a pure redo, with an ended or an active session, gets only the inherited trailers; - after a pure redo, only the redone file leaves the session's touched files, and a later human edit to it doesn't link back to the session; - a redo plus new session work gets the inherited trailer and a fresh one; - a redo plus a file the session never touched gets only the inherited trailer; - a mode change after the reset gets a fresh trailer; - a later dropped commit without a checkpoint that changed the same file leaves it uncovered; - a partial redo by an active session keeps its fast-path trailer; - a stale ACTIVE session tracking only redone files, a read-only ACTIVE session beside a redo-only claimant, and two ended sessions all leave the fresh trailer resolvable; - a dropped commit whose checkpoint is missing or deleted keeps the session's fresh capture; - a staged deletion git pairs with a held file as a rename stamps no fresh trailer; - content and mode are read from the temporary commit index, not `.git/index`; - an aborted commit's marker never settles files a later commit didn't contain; - the cleanup never prunes touched files the redo doesn't hold. `mise run check` passes. ## Follow-ups - The amend fold (`git reset --soft HEAD~1 && git commit --amen…59385 chars truncated…t rewriting is included. Claude's non-interactive mode treats its working directory as trusted, so the reviewer was taking execution-capable configuration from the checkout under review. The reviewer now loads no Claude settings at all and starts no MCP servers. Entire's own lifecycle hooks are supplied through a settings file the CLI writes outside the worktree, so reviews are still captured; the profile's configured skills are supplied by staging them into a plugin directory the CLI owns, so the user's chosen skills still run. | Flag | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `--setting-sources ""` | No settings are read: project and local are branch-controlled, and a user-level hook would run with the reviewed checkout as its working directory | | `--strict-mcp-config` (no `--mcp-config`) | No MCP servers start; setting sources do not gate these | | `--permission-mode default` | Pinned, so a future default cannot widen the reviewer | | `--settings ` | Entire's lifecycle hooks, written outside the worktree, mode 0600 | | `--plugin-dir ` | Only the profile's configured skills, copied into a directory Entire owns | | `--append-system-prompt` | Trust-boundary instruction, appended so a profile prompt cannot displace it | ## Why user settings are excluded too An earlier revision of this branch kept `--setting-sources user` to preserve user- and plugin-provided review skills. That reintroduced an execution path: a user-level hook running `npm run …`, `make …`, or any checkout-relative script executes code from the branch under review, because that branch is the reviewer's working directory. The trail security monitor flagged it, correctly. The trusted settings file also no longer carries the user's `apiKeyHelper`. Claude runs that helper as a shell command with the reviewed checkout as its working directory, so a relative helper executes branch content before the first request; the generation path re-injects it safely only because it runs in `os.TempDir()`, which review cannot. Reviewers authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a Claude sign-in, and Entire prints a note before launch when a helper is configured and no env key is set. Skill staging (`review_skills.go`) resolves the tension without that trade. Each configured skill is copied from the user's own configuration into a temporary plugin directory, loaded with `--plugin-dir`, and its invocation rewritten to `/entire-review:`. Only the chosen skill is copied — never a whole plugin, which can define hooks of its own. Curated builtins such as `/review` need no staging. A skill that cannot be staged fails the review before launch, because a reviewer started without its skill prints `Unknown command` and reviews nothing while still exiting 0. ## Also in here - **Same hooks as `entire enable`, installer untouched.** The review launch runs the installer (`installHookEntries`, a pure map transform) against an empty document and uses its output, so the reviewer's hooks cannot drift from what `entire enable` writes — and `hooks.go` is unchanged from main. - **Fail before launch.** If the trusted settings or a configured skill cannot be established, the review fails. There is no degraded fallback. - **An architectural test** requires every `claude` launch site in the package to record whether it is isolated. - **`PrepareCmd`** on `ReviewerTemplate`: a launch precondition that can fail and owns resources, released once the process exits or immediately if `Start` fails. ## Compatibility - Project-level MCP servers and project-level Claude settings do not apply to reviewers. - User-level hooks, permission modes and MCP servers do not apply to reviewers either. - The user's `apiKeyHelper` is not run for reviews; use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or a Claude sign-in. - Review profiles keep working: builtin, user-level and plugin-provided skills all resolve through staging. This is configuration isolation, not an OS sandbox: the reviewer runs with the invoking account's privileges. ## Verification Full `mise run check` clean. Differential runs against a real Claude with a loopback mock API and synthetic credentials, each comparing an unpatched build with the fix so the fixture is proven to fire before the fix is credited with blocking it. Five canaries: a committed settings hook, a committed `settings.local.json` hook, a committed `.mcp.json` server, a **user-level hook that runs a checkout-relative script**, and a **relative `apiKeyHelper` with the branch supplying the script** — the last two added because the earlier harness only had branch-controlled canaries and could not see either path. | Platform | Claude | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Windows | 2.1.237, 2.1.267 | pass — all four canaries fire unpatched, all four blocked by the fix, capture intact | | Linux | 2.1.237, 2.1.267 | pass — same | | macOS | 2.1.237, 2.1.268 | pass — same; the `user`-sources revision runs the fourth canary here, reproducing the monitor's finding | Matrix run (private validation repo): https://github.com/peyton-alt/cli-review-windows-validation/actions/runs/34567618641 Covers current-branch and remote-only `--target` with `--cleanup-worktree`, multi-worker profiles, builtin / user-level / plugin-provided skills, and session/transcript capture throughout. Not covered: live-service authentication. ## Review notes Separately, and pre-existing: a review whose agent makes zero model requests still reports `1 succeeded` and exits 0. It warns that findings were not persisted. That one ID keyed both transcript paths (the staged capture `.entire/tmp/pi/.json` and the shadow archive `.entire//`), so runs overwrote each other and a checkpoint condensed whichever run wrote last — storing a *different* subagent's conversation. Reproduces with a single Pi session and one subagent; no concurrency required. This takes **direction 1** from the issue: model Pi subagents as subagents — roll the session ID up to the parent UUID, give each run a distinct identity, and route runs through the existing subagent mechanism so each gets its own transcript. ## What Changed - **`agent/pi/lifecycle.go`** — new `parsePiSessionIdentity` (+ `parsePiSubagentPath`, `parsePiParentID`, `derivePiParentTranscript`) resolves the path shape: - parent `…/_.jsonl` → session ID = `` - subagent `…/_//run-N/session.jsonl` → session ID rolls up to the parent ``, plus a distinct `-run-N` id. `ParseHookEvent` now routes subagent `before_agent_start`/`agent_end` to `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` (parent turns still emit `TurnStart`/`TurnEnd`), and stages each run's transcript under its own identity. The parse validates the derived id against **both** consumers (`ValidateAgentID` for the dispatcher and the stricter `ValidateSessionID` for the capture key) so an exotic dir name can't parse-pass then silently fail to stage. - **`agent/event.go`** — added `Event.SubagentTranscriptPath` for agents whose per-subagent transcripts can't be reconstructed from `SessionRef` + `SubagentID` (Pi's nested `//run-N` layout). - **`lifecycle.go`** — `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` prefers `event.SubagentTranscriptPath`, falling back to the existing `agent-.jsonl` convention. Claude Code / Cursor are unaffected (the new field is empty for them). Net effect: one Pi session per conversation (no phantom `session · turns N` row), a distinct staged/stored transcript per run, and task checkpoints that roll up under the parent session with uncontaminated content. ## Tests Written test-first, all confirmed **red** before the fix, green after: - `TestExtractSessionIDFromPath_SubagentRollsUpToParent` — subagent paths roll to the parent UUID, never `"session"`. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentRunsRouteAsSubagents` — subagent runs emit `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd`, share the parent `SessionID`, carry distinct `SubagentID`s. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentCaptureDoesNotClobber` — parent + each run stage distinct, content-correct transcripts. - `TestParseHookEvent_PiSubagentTranscriptSurvivesLaterRun` — one run's staged transcript isn't overwritten when a later run ends (the exact corruption). - `TestExtractSessionIDFromPath` — extended the canonical table with the nested subagent shape and dropped the case that pinned the wrong fallback. ## Verification - `mise run fmt`, lint (golangci-lint v2.11.3, pinned) — clean. - `mise run test:ci` (full race suite + e2e canary) — green; `pi`, `agent/*`, `checkpoint/*`, `strategy`, `cli` suites green. - **End-to-end smoke test** with the real binary in a scratch repo, driving a parent turn + two subagent runs that each modify a file: - `entire session list` → one Pi session with the real parent UUID, no phantom `session` row. - `.entire/tmp/pi/` → three distinct captures (`019fab4c-….json`, `d93a3451-run-0.json`, `716671d6-run-1.json`), no shared `session.json`. - Shadow branch → task checkpoints under `…//tasks//agent-.jsonl`, each storing its **own** run's content (run-0 → run0 marker, run-1 → run1 marker), zero cross-contamination. ## Deferred The issue's optional "have `entire_extension.ts` send `session_id` explicitly" was intentionally dropped: the path parse is now correct and load-bearing, so it's unnecessary. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes Pi hook routing and subagent checkpoint transcript resolution; mistakes could mis-attribute sessions or corrupt task checkpoints, but scope is Pi-specific with a clear fallback for other agents. > > **Overview** > Fixes **#1870**: Pi subagent hooks used to derive session ID from `session.jsonl` basenames, so every run shared the ID `session` and **staged transcripts / task checkpoints overwrote each other**. > > **Pi lifecycle** now parses nested paths (`…/_//run-N/session.jsonl`), rolls **SessionID** up to the parent UUID, assigns a distinct **`-run-N`** subagent ID, and emits **`SubagentStart` / `SubagentEnd`** instead of normal turns. Each run is staged via `captureTranscript` under its own cache key. > > **Framework**: `agent.Event` gains **`SubagentTranscriptPath`**; `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` prefers it over the `agent-.jsonl` convention beside the main transcript. > > Other agents are unchanged when the new field is empty. Regression coverage lives in `subagent_1870_test.go`. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a9b8d49248cc78b2ac4ea1aecc961a711a89343e. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). This addresses the Windows Copilot failure in nightly install smoke [run 34583415795](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34583415795), `TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli`. The turn-end guard previously compared raw bytes against HEAD, so line-ending conversion made committed files appear uncommitted. #2341 exposed this by teaching Copilot's transcript analyzer to read `restrictedProperties.filePaths`. ## Why Copilot exposed this on Windows Windows does not force every file to use CRLF. The agent's file-writing tool chooses the line endings. With `core.autocrlf=true`, `git add` normalizes the stored blob to LF without rewriting the working file: | Agent writes | Working file after commit | Git blob | Previous raw comparison | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | LF | LF | LF | Correctly reports committed | | CRLF | CRLF | LF | Incorrectly reports modified | The original Windows smoke artifacts show different paths through this shared code: - **Codex and OpenCode:** Git warned that the working files contained LF and would be converted to CRLF the next time Git touched them. Their LF working copies matched the committed LF blobs, and turn-end capture reported no remaining modifications. - **Copilot:** Post-commit cleanup removed the shadow branch successfully. About two seconds later, turn-end capture counted the committed file as modified and recreated the branch, consistent with the diagnosed CRLF-versus-LF mismatch. #2341 exposed this path by making Entire recognize Copilot's modified-file telemetry under `restrictedProperties.filePaths`. - **Claude Code:** Turn-end parsing used a transcript offset advanced past the commit and reported no remaining modifications. The saved artifacts do not establish its working-file line endings, so LF cannot be asserted as the explanation for Claude's passing result. This is a shared Entire bug. Any agent that writes CRLF and reports the file again at turn end after committing it can hit the same faulty comparison. Passing Windows tests for other agents do not establish that those agents are immune. ## What Changed Main independently merged a CRLF fix in #2482. After merging main, this PR retains the raw-byte fast path and batch-normalizes only raw mismatches. It uses main's shared `worktreedir.HashableEntry` safety check and retains main's CRLF and symlink regression tests. - Preserve the existing raw-byte comparison in `filterToUncommittedFiles`. - For safely readable regular files whose bytes differ from HEAD, reuse `gitrepo.HashWorktreeFiles` to check whether Git normalization makes the content equal. Hash candidates in a batch; keep actual changes and paths whose normalized content cannot be confirmed. - Leave post-commit carry-forward logic unchanged. No new comparison API, temporary index, or attribute-copying implementation. - Preserve existing raw-equal acceptance, including legacy CRLF blobs. This change only adds a normalization check for raw mismatches; it does not redefine existing decisions for raw-equal files when attributes or filters change. ## Verification Merge update `776568da2` incorporates main at `c21ef7f00`. The resolved tree passed the focused turn-end tests, formatting, lint, and `mise run test:ci`, including race-enabled unit/integration tests and deterministic canaries. A final standard `mise run lint` passed after committing. The real-agent matrix below tested the earlier `97ace0cc2` commit and was not rerun for this merge. `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), and `mise run test:ci` passed, including race-enabled unit/integration tests and deterministic E2E canaries. Focused Windows Copilot `TestMultiSessionSequential` (git-refs) [passed on the fix](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34981705375) on its first attempt. The same scenario [failed on the unfixed base](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34981709072), including its retry, with a shadow branch recreated after post-commit cleanup. On the fix, both sessions instead reported no files modified at turn end. [Full cross-platform E2E validation](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34983337829) completed across 32 combinations. **26 passed; six Windows combinations failed.** This is not a clean cross-platform result. | Platform | Result on both checkpoint backends | | --- | --- | | Linux | All six real agents passed | | macOS | All six real agents passed | | Windows | Claude Code passed; Copilot, Codex, and OpenCode failed | Linux Cursor's installer returned HTTP 500 in the original matrix; its [isolated retry](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34983680912) passed the full suite. macOS Copilot `TestRapidSequentialCommits` and macOS Cursor `TestMultiSessionSequential` each passed after one test rerun. Existing unsupported-test skips remain in the reports. Windows failure investigation: - **Copilot:** [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34985025028) failed 33/32 tests (git-branch/git-refs), versus 25/26 on this fix. Failures include missing `tmux` and a separate existing post-commit CRLF mismatch: ended-session matching compares an LF commit blob with a CRLF shadow blob and declines to condense. The relevant comparison code is unchanged from the base. An isolated temporary Go test reproduces it without an agent: an LF shadow file matches after native Git commits it, while the same CRLF content does not. The original multi-session cleanup scenario passes on the fix with both backends. - **Codex:** [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34985029320) failed 23/11 tests, versus 17/16 on this fix. Both runs show subprocess `WaitDelay` errors and missing `tmux`; which tests hit the subprocess error varies between runs. - **OpenCode:** The fixed-branch runs failed 39/40 tests, with agent exit failures and missing `tmux`. The existing Windows dependency-link fallback also makes each test install dependencies again. [The unfixed baseline](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34986273918) also failed: git-branch completed with 37 failed tests, and git-refs hit the suite’s 30-minute timeout after recording 33 failures, leaving tests unfinished. The baseline shows the same agent-exit and missing-`tmux` failure classes; it does not provide a complete git-refs comparison. The Windows failures prevent a clean cross-platform conclusion. No new failure class was identified, but the existing failures and incomplete OpenCode baseline limit regression confidence. The workflow expansion lives on `validation/turn-end-autocrlf-20260915`, outside this PR. Every fixed-branch job built commit `97ace0cc20c8b208a4fbdc77f4b08b314e1f517b`. The turn-end regression test covers a CRLF working copy of an LF commit, genuinely modified CRLF content, staged changes compared against HEAD, missing paths, legacy CRLF raw matches, and input ordering. `BenchmarkFilterToUncommittedFiles` measures the complete turn-end filter, including repository and blob reads. Example local medians on Apple M2, three samples of ten iterations each: | Case | Time | | --- | ---: | | Raw match, 1 file | 1.66 ms | | Raw match, 100 files | 19.23 ms | | CRLF normalization, 1 file | 11.47 ms | | CRLF normalization, 100 files | 39.05 ms | Raw matches need no hashing subprocess. Raw mismatches reuse the existing batched Git hashing helper. In the focused Windows Copilot run, the logged filter-and-normalize step took 20 ms and 46 ms for the two sessions; total agent-stop hooks took 206 ms and 232 ms. These are individual observations, not a performance bound. This addresses the case we hit where hooks were firing correctly, but the commit happened in a repo/worktree that did not have matching local session state, so the commit had nothing to link and missed the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. ## What changed - Adds the `session adopt` subcommand under `entire session`. - Reads source session state from the source worktree’s `.git/entire-sessions` store. - Supports either an explicit session ID or a single recent active source session. - Filters shared source stores by the requested `--from` worktree, using `WorktreeID` when available and canonical path fallback otherwise. - Supports independent repo/worktree adoption by writing target-local session state. - Supports same-git-common-dir linked worktree adoption by moving the shared session state to the current worktree instead of rejecting it. - Rejects no-op adoption when source and target resolve to the same worktree. - Validates that a preserved live transcript path is owned by the source session’s registered agent. - Keeps the live transcript path because the transcript belongs to the continuing agent session, not necessarily the target repo. - Seeds `FilesTouched` from current target repo changes so the next commit can pass the staged-file overlap check. - Resets target-local checkpoint/transcript bookkeeping so long-running source sessions do not inherit stale checkpoint offsets, checkpoint IDs, prompt windows, or legacy transcript fields. - Preserves cumulative turn/context metrics while anchoring the adopted prompt window at the current source turn count. - Leaves `AttachedManually` false because adoption is not `entire session attach`. This closes the sibling-worktree gap from #573 through an explicit agent/user command, without adding hook-time automatic matching across worktrees. ## Verification - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run TestSessionAdopt -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run TestSessionAdopt_MovesSameStoreSessionIntoCurrentWorktree -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -run 'Test(SessionAdopt|PrepareCommitMsg)' -count=1` - `GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-go-cache go test ./cmd/entire/cli -count=1` - `mise run lint` - `mise run check` `mise run check` passed locally after rebasing on current `main`, including lint, integration tests, Vogon canary, and roger-roger canary. Latest commit/checkpoint: - `db9ada812c38dc67e0750d4e2633662316ffb5bf` - `Entire-Checkpoint: 48521e055655` Push output confirmed `entire/checkpoints/v1` was already up to date on the checkpoint remote. ## Caveats This is explicit adoption, not automatic discovery. Agents or users should run it from the target repo/worktree before committing, and the source transcript path must still be readable on the same machine.","state":null,"user":null,"assignees":null,"labels":null,"milestone":null,"state_reason":null,"comments":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"closed_at":null,"display_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1472","display_title":"feat: adopt active sessions across repos and worktrees"},{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1573","title":"Add hidden experts CLI command","issue_number":1573,"body":" https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/709 ## What is this? Adds a hidden/labs CLI command: **`entire experts`**. Before you edit an unfamiliar part of a repo, it answers: > **“Which agents already have real evidence for this code — and what did they use?”** It is **agent/workflow provenance**, not a human popularity list. The output ranks prior **Codex / Claude / Cursor** (etc.) sessions by evidence: matching checkpoints, agent-attributed lines, skills invoked, tools used, MCP servers, and files touched — **without** exposing raw prompts or chat transcripts. Discover it via `entire labs` (listed as experimental). --- ## Example usage **Directory scope** (most common — “who knows this package?”): ```bash entire experts cmd/entire/cli/ ``` **Single file**: ```bash entire experts cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go ``` **Explicit repo** (`owner/repo` resolves to a repo ULID via your accessible repo list; ULIDs also accepted): ```bash entire experts cmd/entire/cli/ --repo entireio/cli --limit 5 ``` **Staged files** (what am I about to commit?): ```bash entire experts --staged ``` **Interactive browse** (TTY only — two-pane viewer, session links open on entire.io): ```bash entire experts cmd/entire/cli/ --tui ``` **JSON** (for scripts / agents): ```bash entire experts cmd/entire/cli/ --json ``` **Natural-language query** (requires code-search index on the API cell; otherwise 503 with a setup hint): ```bash entire experts "stripe webhook retry logic" --repo entireio/cli ``` --- ## Example output (plain text) ``` Agent provenance for entireio/cli (main) Codex evidence: 1 sessions, 1 matching checkpoints, 9 steps, 142 agent-attributed lines skills: go-cli (2) tools: shell (4), search (3) mcp: github (1) files: cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go - feat: experts provenance - 1 checkpoints, 9 steps Claude Code evidence: 1 sessions, 1 matching checkpoints, 14 steps, 210 agent-attributed lines skills: go-cli (1), tui (1) tools: fileOps (6) mcp: github (2) files: cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go, cmd/entire/cli/experts_tui.go - TUI polish - 1 checkpoints, 14 steps ``` Session names are **clickable links** (OSC 8) to `https://entire.io/gh/{owner}/{repo}/session/{id}` when running in a capable terminal. --- ## How it works (short) 1. ## Summary

Prevent turn-end capture from recreating a shadow branch for files an agent already committed mid-turn when the working copy uses CRLF and Git stores LF. This addresses the Windows Copilot failure in nightly install smoke [run 34583415795](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34583415795), `TestMultiSessionSequential/copilot-cli`.

The turn-end guard previously compared raw bytes against HEAD, so line-ending conversion made committed files appear uncommitted. #2341 exposed this by teaching Copilot's transcript analyzer to read `restrictedProperties.filePaths`.

## Why Copilot exposed this on Windows

Windows does not force every file to use CRLF. The agent's file-writing tool chooses the line endings. With `core.autocrlf=true`, `git add` normalizes the stored blob to LF without rewriting the working file:

| Agent writes | Working file after commit | Git blob | Previous raw comparison |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

issue.title: Run the strategy package on Windows, and fix what that found
issue.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1551
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes git hook install validation used by `entire enable` on Windows; the rest is test/CI and targeted `osroot` cache teardown with limited production surface beyond hook setup.
> 
> **Overview**
> Enables the full **`strategy`** package on Windows CI (longer timeout, unfiltered `go test`) after fixing the failures that blocked it.
> 
> **Production fix:** `InstallGitHook` no longer treats a missing parent under `core.hooksPath` as “hooks disabled” on Windows. It walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and only errors when that node is a non-directory, matching POSIX behavior for setups like Husky’s `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists.
> 
> **Test infrastructure:** Adds `osroot.ForgetUnder` to release cached `osroot.Shared` handles under a temp tree (parallel-safe vs `ResetShared`). `testutil.TempDir` / `ReleaseRootsOnCleanup` (via `InitRepo`) wire that into cleanup so Windows can delete temp repos. Strategy tests adopt these helpers, JSON-encode paths in transcript fixtures, normalize worktree path comparisons, set `USERPROFILE` for git author tests, and skip POSIX-only cases where needed.
> 
> **Docs:** `docs/development/testing.md` documents the Windows temp-dir / path-spelling expectations.
>

issue.title: Remove shadow branches and line attribution
issue.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1509
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Agent turns no longer write anything to git. Older versions committed a full working-tree snapshot to a per-worktree shadow branch (`entire/<commit>-<worktree>`) at every turn end. That was the source of runaway local storage, and cleaning those branches up at the wrong moment made uncondensed work unreachable. Turn ends now record pending work in session state only: the step count, the files the agent touched, and each touched file's git blob hash. A checkpoint is written only when you commit.

Line attribution is removed entirely, including the AI/Human/Mixed labels in `entire blame`, which now reports whether each line's commit is linked to a checkpoint. Checkpoint metadata no longer carries `initial_attribution` or `combined_attribution`; entire.io derives the experts counts from those and must be told they stop arriving.

Commits link to a session by file name: any committed path the session touched links it, except a new file at a path the agent deleted. Carry-forward after a partial commit compares the recorded hashes with the commit and the worktree, so a `git add -p` remainder, a pending deletion, or a session upgraded from the old state format keeps its uncommitted work. Gitignored files, submodule pointers, and paths inside a submodule or beneath a symlinked directory never enter the tracked files, so they can no longer keep a session pending forever; edits inside a submodule belong to the nested repository's own session. Whether a committed file still has uncommitted agent changes is asked of `git status`, so repositories with `text=auto` or `core.autocrlf` no longer keep fully committed files pending.

Lifecycle decisions (condensation, the zombie sweep, orphan cleanup, doctor) key on one predicate over session state instead of whether a shadow ref exists. Pending step rows, explain of temporary checkpoints, incremental task checkpoints and the Claude Code post-todo hook install are gone. `checkpoint list --pending` now previews what the next commit's checkpoint will contain.

Claude Code gains a transcript prompt extractor, so its prompts no longer depend on `prompt.txt` alone.

Addresses #2663, #2378, #2350, #1730, #1807 and #2653. Supersedes trail 1486 (`soph/fix-shadow-after-midturn-commit`), which patches code this PR deletes.

## Migrations

Turn ends no longer write shadow branches (entire/<commit>-<worktree>): pending work is tracked in session state and checkpoints are written only when you commit. comments.body: An ID-based retry is not necessarily unreferenced: `reserveDoctorCondensationAttempt` reuses `PendingCondensationID`, and `checkpointIDForSessions` can stamp that same ID on a later commit. If the initial salvage and that commit's post-commit write both fail, then the transcript disappears (for example, when the home worktree is removed), this unconditional requirement skips recovery despite the remaining file metadata. The skipped-result handler clears the reservation and marks the session fully condensed, leaving the commit's trailer unresolved and suppressing further automatic recovery. Distinguish fresh, unreferenced salvage from recovery of an already-stamped ID; preserve files/prompt-only recovery for the latter and cover this retry sequence in a regression test.

The new requirement checks only the raw transcript. If redaction then fails, `redactOrDrop` drops the transcript and `skipIfPostRedactionEmpty` still allows a checkpoint when pending files exist. Sweep/doctor consequently writes the paths-only checkpoint this change intends to prevent, resets the pending window, and releases the stored transcript copy instead of leaving the session available for retry. Set `failOnRedactionError` for this call so a redaction failure returns an error before that cleanup.

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

issues.title: Shadow branches re-store the whole transcript every turn: storage grows quadratically with session length (168 GB on one branch)
issues.body:
## What happened

On Entire CLI 0.11.3 (I also checked current `main` and the nightlies, which have no change here), one shadow branch `entire/<base>-<worktree>` reached **3,643 commits and 168 GB of loose objects** in about 12 days. That helped fill a 926 GB laptop disk to 0 bytes free.

Each shadow commit stores `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl`, the **whole** transcript so far. Two long-running sessions in one worktree (3,299 and 502 turns) never committed code in that worktree, so the branch was never condensed. Every turn re-stored a transcript of 50–320 MB uncompressed. Sampled blobs show the same session id again and again at growing sizes.

## Why nothing reclaims it

- Entire writes these as **loose** objects (go-git `SetEncodedObject`) and never packs.
- `docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` (ENT-241) tells users to set `gc.auto 0`, so `git gc --auto` never runs either.
- The branch is reachable, so `git prune` can't free it. Only a manual repack shrinks it. Successive snapshots of an append-only JSONL delta to almost nothing: a synthetic reproduction packed 243 MiB of loose snapshots into 16.9 MiB.

`checkpoint-scenarios.md` limitation #5 acknowledges that storage "grows linearly with session length × number of commits". Since the transcript itself grows with the session, the total is effectively **quadratic** for long sessions (orchestrator-style agents run for days).

## Suggestion

Make each turn's storage cost proportional to what the turn **added**. Possible ways:

1. **Chunk `full.jsonl` in shadow commits at fixed, line-aligned offsets.** Committed checkpoints already chunk at 50 MiB; smaller chunks, say 1–4 MiB, would work here. An append-only transcript's unchanged prefix chunks would then hash to the same blobs and be stored once. Only the tail chunk is new each turn.
2. Or write each turn's objects into a pack (or run a bounded `git repack -d` after condensation or cleanup), so Entire doesn't leave the reclaim to a gc it tells users to disable.
3. Consider surfacing very large or long-lived shadow branches in `entire status` / `entire doctor`. A session that never commits in its home worktree pins its branch indefinitely, and nothing tells the user.

I'm happy to share more measurements.

issues.title: Hook latency: remaining work after #2002
issues.body:
Follow-up to #2002, which fixed the *tail* of hook latency but not the median. Filing the
measured state so the remaining work is picked up from evidence rather than re-derived.

## What #2002 fixed

Profiling `createRedactedBlobFromFile` put redaction at **99.7%** of the checkpoint blob
write (git object writing was 174ms of a 66.7s pass on 70MB), and the CPU profile put
**82%** of that in betterleaks' regex ruleset. `full.jsonl` holds the full session and was
re-redacted from byte zero every checkpoint, so a session with N checkpoints re-redacted
O(N²) bytes — which is also what inflates the multi-GB packs.

Sharding plus prefix reuse took a 14-checkpoint session growing to 70MB from **~66s to
~2.0s** on the final Stop.

## What is still open

### 1. ~~The ~3s p50 floor is unexplained~~ — ANSWERED, see the re-measure below

It was substantially the redaction path, and #2002 fixed it: population p50 **2326ms →
1103ms**, with `write_temporary_checkpoint` and `redact_transcript` gone from slow traces
entirely. Evidence and method are in the re-measure section.

Kept for the ruling-out work, which stays useful if the floor ever returns: it was **not**
the transcript-flush `maxWait` (its warning appears **0** times in real logs), the
trail-enablement refresh (detached subprocess by design), git-refs vs git-branch backend,
`telemetry`, checkpoint history, authentication, or `local_dev`. Size was not the driver
either — `stop` was flat across a 235× range of pack size, and 8KB → 1.2MB of transcript
added only ~125ms. The original distribution was **bimodal** with a hard floor at ~3s and a
near-empty 2500-2999ms gap beneath it, which is what made a conditional timeout look more
likely than variable work.

### 2. `process_sessions` — post-commit condensation

Dominant step in **27 of 93** slow traces. Independently confirms
[`docs/architecture/commit-hook-perf-analysis.md`](docs/architecture/commit-hook-perf-analysis.md):
~73–103ms per accumulated session, N sessions per commit, PostCommit dominating. That doc
already lists concrete fixes (batch condensation into one commit, prune stale ENDED
sessions, skip the orphan check for sessions with `LastCheckpointID`). Nothing has been
done. **Probably the largest remaining win.**

### 2b. The compact transcript is generated twice per Stop

`writeCompactTranscript` has two call sites — `checkpoint/persistent.go:1092` (checkpoint
write) and `:2069` (Stop finalize rewrite) — and `compact.FullWithBoundary` compacts the
**whole** session each time. Measured at 457ms + 447ms = **904ms of a 2505ms Stop**, which
makes it the largest single item in a Stop now that redaction is fixed.

Same shape as the problem #2107 just solved, and possibly the same remedy. Found during the
2026-08-23 re-measure, not from first principles — it only became visible once redaction
stopped dominating.

### 3. The transcript-flush sentinel is dead code costing a fixed ~520ms per Stop

`waitForTranscriptFlush` waits for a `hook_progress` transcript entry containing
`"hooks claude-code stop"`. Claude Code no longer writes it — **0 occurrences across 40
real transcripts**. So it always falls through to settle-on-stability, which structurally
cannot return before `quietWindow` (500ms) + one 50ms poll.

There is nothing to revive: what Claude Code writes now is
`{"type":"system","subtype":"stop_hook_summary"}`, emitted *after* the hook returns (it
reports the hook's own `durationMs`), so waiting on it would deadlock. Measured separately:
the final assistant entry lands 33ms before the hook starts, so the transcript is already
complete when the wait begins.

Needs a decision, not more investigation — shortening the window trades against reading a
truncated transcript, which is why it exists. Suggested shape: return as soon as the size
is stable across two polls **and** the last line parses as complete JSON.

### 4. ~~Prefix reuse covers only the shadow write~~ — DONE in #2107

Condensation and the Stop finalize rewrite now reuse prefixes too, via
`checkpoint.RedactTranscriptCached`. Promoted ahead of the rest because it stopped being
latency and became breakage: a coworker on a 65MB Codex rollout hit Codex's **30s Stop-hook
timeout** (30.203s, process killed, finalize rewrite left incomplete).

Two things found while doing it, both worth knowing:

- **A git blob is not a free place to cache bytes.** The first cut stored the reused prefix
  as a blob, on the assumption git would dedup it. go-git deflates the whole payload before
  dotgit discovers the object exists — dedup saves the rename, not the compression — so it
  cost ~1-2s of zlib per checkpoint. Worse, the store chunks at `agent.MaxChunkSize` (50MB),
  so above that the whole-transcript blob matches no chunk, is never deduped, and lingers
  unreachable until `git gc` prunes it and silently reverts the cache to full redaction.
  The prefix is a plain file in the cache dir now.
- **The redaction test suite was most of the `checkpoint` package's runtime.** The 1MiB size
  gate forced every test to build and redact a megabyte of realistic content; 17 tests cost
  4m57s under `-race` and timed out CI at 10m. The gate is now test-overridable and the
  package runs in ~22s — faster than before this work started.

## Re-measured 2026-08-23

Corpus: 95 `.entire/logs/entire.log` files, 57,619 lines, **1,465** paired
turn-end→shadow-commit spans and **287** `perf` spans. Both comparison windows below sit
*after* #1999, so the deleted `entire-dev` launcher is not a confound between them.

### #2002 worked, and the ~3s floor is gone

Unbiased population metric (every turn, not just slow ones), non-CLI repos:

| window | n | p50 | p90 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| post-#1999, pre-#2002 (08-17..08-20) | 58 | 2326ms | 2747ms |

issues.title: git-refs writes can return success without durable push bookkeeping
issues.body:
### What happened?

On the git-refs checkpoint backend, an ordinary persistent write updates the
checkpoint ref and then records that ref in
`entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl`. If queue resolution, locking, opening, or
appending fails, `enqueueForPush` logs a warning but the write still returns
success.

I understand the documented intent: enqueue is best-effort so a locally
successful condensation is not failed, and a later write to the same checkpoint
can re-enqueue the ref. The residual problem is that the queue is also the sole
input to the normal git-refs unpushed count and publication path. If there is no
later write, the result is a durable false-success state:

- the checkpoint ref and object exist only in the originating clone;
- the write caller received success;
- the normal unpushed count reports `0`;
- the normal queue publisher pushes `0` refs;
- a fresh clone from the remote cannot recover the checkpoint ref or object.

The local ref remains readable and GC-protected, so this is not immediate local
deletion. It becomes unrecoverable through the normal remote path if that sole
clone is later lost or discarded.

### Expected behavior

A successfully acknowledged checkpoint should not become indefinitely invisible
to both normal pending diagnostics and normal publication. Keeping condensation
fail-soft is reasonable, but the system should retain or reconstruct durable
knowledge that the local ref still needs publication, or explicitly surface a
partial/local-only outcome.

### Actual behavior

The enqueue failure is warning-only. Once the transient obstruction clears,
queue-only status and publication see no pending checkpoint and perform no
reconciliation against local checkpoint refs.

### Steps to reproduce

I reproduced this using a disposable work repository, a local bare remote, and a
fresh recovery clone:

1. Configure `checkpoints.primary.type` as `git-refs`.
2. Create the queue pathname as a directory to deterministically make only the
   JSONL queue open fail.
3. Write a checkpoint through `checkpoint.Open(...).Persistent.Write(...)`.
4. Verify that the write returns `nil` and the checkpoint ref resolves locally.
5. Remove the synthetic obstruction and call
   `strategy.CountUnpushedCheckpoints(...)`; it returns `0`.
6. Call `strategy.PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(...)`; it returns `pushed=0` with
   pushing enabled.
7. Verify the bare remote lacks the checkpoint ref, clone that remote, and
   verify the clone has neither the ref nor the checkpoint commit object.

Observed output:

```text
WARN checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed ... open push queue: ... is a directory
write_success=true local_ref=refs/entire/checkpoints/f6/c1b2c3d4e5f6
count_unpushed=0 pushed=0 push_disabled=false
remote_ref_present=false recovery_ref_present=false recovery_object_present=false
```

The focused end-to-end regression passed while asserting this current behavior;
the control experiment also confirmed that the same write creates both the ref
and queue record when queue persistence is available.

### Entire CLI version

v0.10.6

### OS and architecture

Windows amd64

### Agent

Codex

### Terminal

PowerShell

### Logs / debug output

```bash
=== RUN   TestGitRefsQueueFailure_LosesRemoteRecoverability
WARN checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed ref=refs/entire/checkpoints/f6/c1b2c3d4e5f6 error="open push queue: openat entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl: is a directory"
write_success=true local_ref=refs/entire/checkpoints/f6/c1b2c3d4e5f6 checkpoint_commit=4589427309d230ba0e4bce32bbf4f17913fe7ac0
count_unpushed=0 pushed=0 push_disabled=false
remote_ref_present=false recovery_ref_present=false recovery_object_present=false
--- PASS: TestGitRefsQueueFailure_LosesRemoteRecoverability (1.99s)
```

### Additional context

This is a correctness and checkpoint-durability report, not a security report.
The failure was deterministically injected; real-world trigger frequency is
unknown. Plausible queue persistence failures include filesystem permission,
capacity, locking, or I/O failures, and there is also a structural interruption
window after ref update and before enqueue, but those natural triggers were not
claimed as reproduced here.

The source test ran at `5f09e04de77d627984ff118eb87bd2c16cce8fbd`
and was revalidated on current `main`
`174dca012af81d3d6ebefc2d7cc17f50a5eb37bb`. The ref-write, queue,
unpushed-count, publication, and architecture-document blobs are identical
between those revisions.

Related but distinct work:

- `#1925` fixes cancellation affecting post-ref bookkeeping.
- `#2008` / `#2012` cover removal of a newer same-ref enqueue during an
  in-flight push.
- `#1773` / `#1929` cover logged-out import and later synchronization.
- `#2327` adds explicit checkpoint migration/re-enqueue behavior.
- `#1917` / `#1926` cover a concurrent same-checkpoint ref-update race before
  queue publication.

Potential solution directions include a durable pre-acknowledgement outbox,
surfacing a partial/local-only result, or reconciling local checkpoint refs
against queued/published state before status and publication. I have not assumed
which trade-off is preferred.

issues.title: OPF writers still CAS checkpoint refs via go-git, racing #1926's native update-ref
issues.body:
#1926 routed persistent checkpoint ref updates through a cross-process flock plus native `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`, which closed #1917 for the checkpoint store's own writers.

Two writers in `strategy` still update those same refs outside that lock, using go-git's `CheckAndSetReference`:

- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go:815` - CAS on `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_opf_refs.go:169` - CAS on the per-checkpoint refs

Both compare-and-swap, so this is not the unconditional-update defect from #1917. The problem is that go-git's `CheckAndSetReference` does not interoperate with native git's `.lock` files - the reason documented at `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/shadow_ref.go:53`. So a pre-push OPF rewrite and a post-commit condensation can now race on the same ref through two mutually invisible CAS mechanisms.

The author of #1926 called this out in that PR's description as remaining scope.

Needs its own reproduction before a fix - #1917's does not cover it, since both sides here verify an expected old value.

issues.title: Checkpoint duplicated when a session-end hook is killed between the v1 write and the state save
issues.body:
A session-end hook killed part-way through can leave a checkpoint committed to `entire/checkpoints/v1` whose session bookkeeping never advanced, so PostCommit later writes a **second** checkpoint covering the same transcript range.

Found by an agent review on [trail #1001](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1001) (finding `01M0A84AHZ7F`) while reviewing #1940, and verified against the code. Filed as a follow-up because the durable fix changes the condensation path, which did not belong in a session-cleanup PR.

### The window

`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` runs the condense *inside* the `MutateSessionState` callback (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1350`), and `MutateSessionState` persists the state only after that callback returns (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go:563`). The checkpoint, however, is committed to v1 partway through the callback, at `manual_commit_condensation.go:434`.

Kill the process between those two points and:

- the checkpoint is durable on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, `LastCheckpointID`, `StepCount` and `FullyCondensed` are all unchanged on disk

so the next PostCommit mints a fresh checkpoint ID over a transcript range that already has one.

The other kill windows are fine, which is what makes this one worth fixing rather than absorbing: before `markSessionEnded` the exited-owner sweep reclaims the session, and before `store.Write` nothing durable happened so the existing fail-open retry is correct.

### Who can hit it

Any agent whose host kills the hook. Today that is Codex, which runs `SessionEnd` inside its shutdown under a hard 3s `SESSION_END_MAX_TIMEOUT_SEC` and terminates the hook's whole process tree on expiry. #1940 widened Entire's self-imposed budget to 2s and pinned ≥1s of headroom for wrapper and binary startup, which makes overrunning much less likely — but a budget only narrows the race, it cannot close it. A SIGKILL, a laptop suspend, or an OOM kill lands in the same window.

No data is lost in any case, and the flock is OS-advisory so a killed hook cannot wedge later sessions. The cost is duplication.

### Fix

Make the v1 write and the state save one recoverable unit, so a retry after a kill cannot duplicate. Roughly, either:

1. persist the advanced bookkeeping (at minimum `LastCheckpointID` and `CheckpointTranscriptStart`) before or atomically with the v1 write, so a retry recognises the range as already covered; or
2. make PostCommit idempotent against an existing checkpoint for the same transcript range, and reconcile rather than mint.

### Also worth answering

- **Do `tokens profile` / `checkpoint list` double-count an overlapping pair?** If they do, the user-visible symptom is inflated token totals, not just a redundant checkpoint.
- **Does Codex send SIGTERM or SIGKILL on expiry?** On SIGTERM, `cmd/entire/main.go:47` prints `Received termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.` to stderr, which would surface on the user's terminal during Codex's own shutdown. The cancellation itself is the graceful path; the message is the problem.

On the git-refs checkpoint backend, an ordinary persistent write updates the
checkpoint ref and then records that ref in
`entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl`. If queue resolution, locking, opening, or
appending fails, `enqueueForPush` logs a warning but the write still returns
success.

I understand the documented intent: enqueue is best-effort so a locally
successful condensation is not failed, and a later write to the same checkpoint
can re-enqueue the ref. The residual problem is that the queue is also the sole
input to the normal git-refs unpushed count and publication path. If there is no
later write, the result is a durable false-success state:

- the checkpoint ref and object exist only in the originating clone;
- the write caller received success;
- the normal unpushed count reports `0`;
- the normal queue publisher pushes `0` refs;
- a fresh clone from the remote cannot recover the checkpoint ref or object.

The local ref remains readable and GC-protected, so this is not immediate local
deletion. It becomes unrecoverable through the normal remote path if that sole
clone is later lost or discarded.

### Expected behavior

A successfully acknowledged checkpoint should not become indefinitely invisible
to both normal pending diagnostics and normal publication. Keeping condensation
fail-soft is reasonable, but the system should retain or reconstruct durable
knowledge that the local ref still needs publication, or explicitly surface a
partial/local-only outcome.

### Actual behavior

The enqueue failure is warning-only. Once the transient obstruction clears,
queue-only status and publication see no pending checkpoint and perform no
reconciliation against local checkpoint refs.

### Steps to reproduce

I reproduced this using a disposable work repository, a local bare remote, and a
fresh recovery clone:

1. Configure `checkpoints.primary.type` as `git-refs`.
2. Create the queue pathname as a directory to deterministically make only the
   JSONL queue open fail.
3. Write a checkpoint through `checkpoint.Open(...).Persistent.Write(...)`.
4. Verify that the write returns `nil` and the checkpoint ref resolves locally.
5. Remove the synthetic obstruction and call
   `strategy.CountUnpushedCheckpoints(...)`; it returns `0`.
6. Call `strategy.PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(...)`; it returns `pushed=0` with
   pushing enabled.
7. Verify the bare remote lacks the checkpoint ref, clone that remote, and
   verify the clone has neither the ref nor the checkpoint commit object.

Observed output:

```text
WARN checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed ... open push queue: ... is a directory
write_success=true local_ref=refs/entire/checkpoints/f6/c1b2c3d4e5f6
count_unpushed=0 pushed=0 push_disabled=false
remote_ref_present=false recovery_ref_present=false recovery_object_present=false
```

The focused end-to-end regression passed while asserting this current behavior;
the control experiment also confirmed that the same write creates both the ref
and queue record when queue persistence is available.

v0.10.6

### OS and architecture

Windows amd64

### Agent

Codex

### Terminal

PowerShell

```bash
=== RUN   TestGitRefsQueueFailure_LosesRemoteRecoverability
WARN checkpoint: enqueue checkpoint ref for push failed ref=refs/entire/checkpoints/f6/c1b2c3d4e5f6 error="open push queue: openat entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl: is a directory"
```

This is a correctness and checkpoint-durability report, not a security report.
The failure was deterministically injected; real-world trigger frequency is
unknown. Plausible queue persistence failures include filesystem permission,
capacity, locking, or I/O failures, and there is also a structural interruption
window after ref update and before enqueue, but those natural triggers were not
claimed as reproduced here.

The source test ran at `5f09e04de77d627984ff118eb87bd2c16cce8fbd`
and was revalidated on current `main`
`174dca012af81d3d6ebefc2d7cc17f50a5eb37bb`. The ref-write, queue,
unpushed-count, publication, and architecture-document blobs are identical
between those revisions.

Related but distinct work:

- `#1925` fixes cancellation affecting post-ref bookkeeping.
- `#2008` / `#2012` cover removal of a newer same-ref enqueue during an
  in-flight push.
- `#1773` / `#1929` cover logged-out import and later synchronization.
- `#2327` adds explicit checkpoint migration/re-enqueue behavior.
- `#1917` / `#1926` cover a concurrent same-checkpoint ref-update race before
  queue publication.

Potential solution directions include a durable pre-acknowledgement outbox,
surfacing a partial/local-only result, or reconciling local checkpoint refs

### The window

`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` runs the condense *inside* the `MutateSessionState` callback (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1350`), and `MutateSessionState` persists the state only after that callback returns (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go:563`). The checkpoint, however, is committed to v1 partway through the callback, at `manual_commit_condensation.go:434`.

Kill the process between those two points and:

- the checkpoint is durable on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, `LastCheckpointID`, `StepCount` and `FullyCondensed` are all unchanged on disk

so the next PostCommit mints a fresh checkpoint ID over a transcript range that already has one.

The other kill windows are fine, which is what makes this one worth fixing rather than absorbing: before `markSessionEnded` the exited-owner sweep reclaims the session, and before `store.Write` nothing durable happened so the existing fail-open retry is correct.

### Who can hit it

Any agent whose host kills the hook. Today that is Codex, which runs `SessionEnd` inside its shutdown under a hard 3s `SESSION_END_MAX_TIMEOUT_SEC` and terminates the hook's whole process tree on expiry. #1940 widened Entire's self-imposed budget to 2s and pinned ≥1s of headroom for wrapper and binary startup, which makes overrunning much less likely — but a budget only narrows the race, it cannot close it. A SIGKILL, a laptop suspend, or an OOM kill lands in the same window.

No data is lost in any case, and the flock is OS-advisory so a killed hook cannot wedge later sessions. The cost is duplication.

### Fix

Make the v1 write and the state save one recoverable unit, so a retry after a kill cannot duplicate. Roughly, either:

1. persist the advanced bookkeeping (at minimum `LastCheckpointID` and `CheckpointTranscriptStart`) before or atomically with the v1 write, so a retry recognises the range as already covered; or
2. make PostCommit idempotent against an existing checkpoint for the same transcript range, and reconcile rather than mint.

### Also worth answering

- **Do `tokens profile` / `checkpoint list` double-count an overlapping pair?** If they do, the user-visible symptom is inflated token totals, not just a redundant checkpoint.
- **Does Codex send SIGTERM or SIGKILL on expiry?** On SIGTERM, `cmd/entire/main.go:47` prints `Received termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.` to stderr, which would surface on the user's terminal during Codex's own shutdown. The cancellation itself is the graceful path; the message is the problem.

issues.title: Run the strategy package on Windows, and fix what that found
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1551
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

issues.title: Record a session's edits against the worktree they happen in
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1378
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Rebuilt on top of the shadow-branch removal (now on main). The earlier version of this PR moved sessions between worktrees on top of shadow branches; that no longer applies. This version records a session's edits against the worktree they happened in, so a commit in any worktree links the session's work there.

## Problem

A session has one home worktree: where its first hook ran. An agent launched there fires every hook there, even when it edits another worktree of the repository by absolute path, or is resumed in one. Without shadow branches visible from every worktree:

- edits in another worktree fell outside the hook's tree at turn end and were dropped, so the session recorded nothing and a later commit of those files there didn't link;
- a turn ending in another worktree marked the home's uncommitted untracked files as deleted, and moved the session's base and branch to that tree;
- the stored transcript and prompts were written to whichever worktree the hook ran in, splitting them, and readers in other worktrees missed them.

## Change

**Edits are recorded per worktree.** The home keeps its existing fields (`files_touched`, `touched_file_hashes`). Edits the transcript places in another registered worktree go into `other_worktrees[<worktree id>]` (files, hashes, path), hashed in that worktree. Only transcript-named paths count there, so other people's uncommitted changes in that worktree are never claimed. Entries are keyed by worktree ID (they survive `git worktree move`) and pruned when the worktree is removed. A subagent's edits don't create entries (main transcript only).

**A commit in worktree X matches and clears only X's record.** Prepare-commit-msg and post-commit read X's record in place of the home's: overlap and content checks, the checkpoint's `files_touched`, and clearing. A session with a record for X takes part in linking there, but must overlap X's files. The no-TTY fast path now requires that too, unless the session is identified as the committer by process ancestry or caller-session env, so an agent's own mid-turn commit still links and an unrelated process's commit doesn't. When work stays pending in another worktree, the commit carries the rest forward (as split commits do today), and the stored copy is released only when nothing is pending anywhere. Pending work, the stale sweep, doctor, session end and adopt count every worktree.

**The stored copy lives in the home worktree.** Turn-start and turn-end writes go through `OpenSessionEntireDir`; every reader goes through `storedSessionRoot`, under the existing registered-worktree gate.

**A turn ending outside the home records only its own work** there: no deletions of the home's files, no base or branch moves.

Reproduced with the real binary and installed git hooks (agent launched in the main checkout, editing a linked worktree by absolute path; "someone else" commits from a process outside the agent's tree):

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| A: agent edits the worktree; later the user commits it there | not linked | linked, `files_touched=[a.txt]` |
| D: work pending at home + worktree edit, each committed in its own tree | worktree commit not linked | both linked, each with only its own file |
| C: back at home | linked | linked |
| F: session ACTIVE with a worktree record; an unrelated process commits there (no TTY) | linked (wrong) | not linked |
| G: the agent's own mid-turn shell edit in the worktree, committed by it | linked | linked, `files_touched=[g.txt]` |
| H: session ended with only a worktree record; later commit there | not linked | linked |
| I: worktree moved before the commit | not linked | linked |

## Known limits

- Files written in another worktree only through shell commands aren't in the transcript, so they aren't recorded there (an agent's own commit of them still links by ancestry). Edits recorded mid-turn (PostToolUse) and subagent task files still go to the home record.
- When commits in two worktrees split a session's work, the second checkpoint shows the whole conversation (as split commits do); tokens are counted once via `token_transcript_start`.
- An older CLI that rewrites the session state drops `other_worktrees`.
- Removing the home worktree deletes its `.entire`, so an uncommitted stored copy is lost.
- `entire status` and the commit preview don't list other worktrees' files yet.

## Tests

Strategy, session and integration tests for: recording per worktree at turn end (including both trees in one turn, symlinked paths, pruning, adopt), linking and the fast path requiring X's files, carry-forward with work pending elsewhere, the stored copy in the home, guest turns, the transcript fallback ignoring already-checkpointed edits, and a commit in X whose record doesn't overlap falling back to the committed files. Each behavioral test fails with its change reverted; `mise run check` passes.
