issues.title: Remove shadow branches and line attribution
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1509
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Agent turns no longer write anything to git. Older versions committed a full working-tree snapshot to a per-worktree shadow branch (`entire/<commit>-<worktree>`) at every turn end. That was the source of runaway local storage, and cleaning those branches up at the wrong moment made uncondensed work unreachable. Turn ends now record pending work in session state only: the step count, the files the agent touched, and each touched file's git blob hash. A checkpoint is written only when you commit.

Line attribution is removed entirely, including the AI/Human/Mixed labels in `entire blame`, which now reports whether each line's commit is linked to a checkpoint. Checkpoint metadata no longer carries `initial_attribution` or `combined_attribution`; entire.io derives the experts counts from those and must be told they stop arriving.

Commits link to a session by file name: any committed path the session touched links it, except a new file at a path the agent deleted. Carry-forward after a partial commit compares the recorded hashes with the commit and the worktree, so a `git add -p` remainder, a pending deletion, or a session upgraded from the old state format keeps its uncommitted work. Gitignored files, submodule pointers, and paths inside a submodule or beneath a symlinked directory never enter the tracked files, so they can no longer keep a session pending forever; edits inside a submodule belong to the nested repository's own session. Whether a committed file still has uncommitted agent changes is asked of `git status`, so repositories with `text=auto` or `core.autocrlf` no longer keep fully committed files pending.

Lifecycle decisions (condensation, the zombie sweep, orphan cleanup, doctor) key on one predicate over session state instead of whether a shadow ref exists. Pending step rows, explain of temporary checkpoints, incremental task checkpoints and the Claude Code post-todo hook install are gone. `checkpoint list --pending` now previews what the next commit's checkpoint will contain.

Claude Code gains a transcript prompt extractor, so its prompts no longer depend on `prompt.txt` alone.

Addresses #2663, #2378, #2350, #1730, #1807 and #2653. Supersedes trail 1486 (`soph/fix-shadow-after-midturn-commit`), which patches code this PR deletes.

## Migrations

Turn ends no longer write shadow branches (entire/<commit>-<worktree>): pending work is tracked in session state and checkpoints are written only when you commit. Branches left by older versions are not removed automatically. `entire doctor` and `entire status` report them, and `entire doctor --force` or `entire disable --uninstall` deletes the `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` form without touching session state. The oldest bare `entire/<commit>` form is only ever listed, since a branch of your own named after a short SHA looks the same; `entire clean --all` removes it behind a confirmation. Do not use plain `entire clean` for this: it also clears pending session state. They hold full snapshots of your working tree, so run it once after upgrading. Deleting the branches frees no space by itself: a later `git gc` reclaims it once their objects are two weeks old. `git gc --prune=now` frees it immediately, but it drops every unreachable object in the repository (recently dropped stashes included) and must only run when no other git process is active.

`entire blame --json` reports a per-line `status` (`checkpoint`, `commit`, `uncommitted`) instead of `authorship` and `tag`. Its summary reports checkpoint-linked, commit and uncommitted line counts instead of AI/Human/Mixed counts.

New checkpoints no longer include `initial_attribution`, `combined_attribution` or `prompt_attributions`; checkpoints written by older versions keep theirs, and rewrites (explain `--generate`, attach) carry them through unchanged. Session state files written by older versions still load; their attribution and `last_checkpoint_commit_hash` keys are dropped on the next save.

The Claude Code post-todo hook is no longer installed, and any `entire enable` prunes it and says so. Its subcommand stays so older hook configs keep working. An older CLI run against the same tracked `.claude/settings.json` reports the hooks as out of date and re-adds it; this CLI removes it again on the next `entire enable`.

Commit pending agent work before downgrading to a previous release: the previous CLI deletes ended but uncondensed session state when its shadow branch is missing, and this release never writes one.

`entire session info --json` and `entire session current --json` report the number of turns not yet condensed into a checkpoint as `pending_turns`. The old `checkpoints` field is still emitted with the same value for this release only and will be removed in the next one; switch scripts to `pending_turns`. `entire status --json` adds `legacy_shadow_branches`.

## Follow-ups, not in this PR

Downgrade safety: the previous CLI deletes ended but uncondensed session state when its shadow branch is missing, and this release never writes one, so rolling back after pending work discards it. The migration note covers it; a patch on the previous release line whose orphan check also requires no pending work, named as the minimum safe downgrade target, is a release-management follow-up (trail finding 01M4DD0R83YC).

Worktree scoping, deferred to the #2531 work: scoping the zombie sweep and doctor to the current worktree, retiring the stored transcript copy with the growth check moving to the live transcript position, prompts and transcript for guest-linked commits, and capture following the event's cwd. #2531 itself must be reworked after this lands, since it pins sessions through shadow-branch steps; #2486 is expected to close in its favour.

Tracked on the priority list for go-git (#DM2KFD6): its worktree hashing lacks gitattributes, filter, and index-aware CRLF handling, which is why this PR asks `git status` instead of hashing; porting that logic into go-git would let the CLI drop the subprocess.

## Test plan

`mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit, integration, Vogon canary) and `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` on the final tree, with a cold lint cache, after merging main at `375819df95`. Every commit builds and vets on its own. A focused security review of the cross-worktree stored-transcript read (a path taken from on-disk session state, gated by `git worktree list` registration and the `.entire` anchor) found no findings. The only local failures are the known OpenCode seed-cache guard and the Claude config-probe timeout, which passes alone.

New unit, integration and command tests cover: recorded-hash carry-forward (partial commits, pending, committed and re-created deletions, upgraded sessions, an unreadable worktree); name-based linking; gitignored and submodule paths on every capture route; the doctor legacy-branch check; the `--pending` preview in text and JSON without a TTY; and the Claude prompt extractor against the real transcript fixture.

Real-agent E2E passed on `44ebccb136` for every leg (claude-code, codex, cursor-cli, copilot-cli, factoryai-droid, opencode, antigravity, roger-roger, and Windows): https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/37655720329. One changed expectation is `TestInteractiveNewFileLinksAfterUserRewrite`, which now expects a trailer after a user rewrites an agent-created file.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> This rewrites core session-to-checkpoint lifecycle, persistent metadata contracts, and labs blame JSON—high blast radius for upgrades, downstream consumers (e.g. entire.io attribution fields), and real-agent E2E behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Turn-end work stays out of git.** Agent stops no longer commit working-tree snapshots to `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` shadow branches; **SaveStep** only updates local session state (step count, files touched, content hashes, transcript copy). Permanent checkpoints are written at **`git commit`** onto metadata refs, matching the updated README/CLAUDE contract.
> 
> **Checkpoint storage and metadata slim down.** The ephemeral/shadow-branch store (`EphemeralStore`, `WriteTemporary`, task step writes, related benchmarks and tests) is removed. **`CheckpointAttribution`** and all **`Attribution`** fields (`initial_attribution`, `combined_attribution`, `prompt_attributions`, `EphemeralBranch`) drop out of `api/checkpoint` and git/fs backends.
> 
> **`entire blame` / `why` semantics change.** Per-line **AI/Human/Mixed** authorship is gone; JSON uses **`status`** (`checkpoint`, `commit`, `uncommitted`) and summaries count checkpoint-linked vs other commits. Help text states Entire does not attribute lines to AI vs humans—only whether the blame commit carries an **Entire-Checkpoint** trailer.
> 
> **Claude Code hooks and prompts.** The **post-todo** (`TaskCreate|TaskUpdate`) hook is no longer installed; **`entire enable`** prunes stale installs while keeping the subcommand registered. New **`prompts.go`** implements **`PromptExtractor`** / **`TranscriptPromptExtractor`** so user prompts come from transcript bytes with injected/meta lines filtered.
> 
> **Operator/docs touchpoints.** `checkpoint list --pending` documents **`is_next_checkpoint`** preview semantics; legacy shadow branches are called out for **`entire doctor`** / **`entire clean`**. E2E/debug skills swap “attribution” for **file tracking** language.
>

issues.title: Let review profiles carry each reviewer's own agent config
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1516
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A reviewer in a review profile can carry its own agent config, set with `entire review --edit` or `entire review --configure <profile> --set-config <reviewer>=<config.json|isolated|none>`. The branch's hooks, MCP servers and extensions are not loaded for that reviewer; it uses the profile's instead. This is the review-profile form of the `--agent-config` proposal discussed on trail 1493 (#2671).

| Agent | Branch config not loaded | Profile config applied | Still loaded from the branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `--setting-sources user`, `--strict-mcp-config` | `settings` (with Entire's tracking hooks added) and `mcp_servers`, as 0600 files | CLAUDE.md; `.claude/skills` and `.claude/commands` as the `project` plugin, copied from the committed tree (`/review` becomes `/project:review`); symlinks and submodules there are skipped |
| Codex | checkout and main repo marked untrusted for the run | `mcp_servers` via `-c` (`command`, `args`, `url`, `default_tools_approval_mode`; other fields, literal `env` values, and a server name the user's `~/.codex/config.toml` already defines are refused); Entire's tracking hooks via `-c` with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` | AGENTS.md, skills |
| Pi | `--no-extensions` | `extensions` (absolute paths), plus Entire's own | AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, skills, prompt templates, `.pi/settings.json` |

- **Where config comes from is enforced; what its commands do is not.** A reviewer config is honored and saved only in developer-owned layers: clone-local preferences (`review_agent_configs`, which overlay only the config so the rest of the profile keeps coming from its own file), or an untracked `.entire/settings.local.json`. A config in the committed file, the judge or the legacy `review` map is dropped with a note; a local file that can't be verified fails the review. The profile's own hooks and MCP servers are the user's code, like their own agent settings, and run in the checkout as configured. A value naming a path inside the checkout or `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` gets a warning.
- **Fail, don't fall back.** A field an agent can't apply is refused when saved and before the run.
- **Blocked tools are reported.** Reviewers run headless, so a tool their settings don't allow is denied. Claude's `permission_denials` and Codex's approval refusals are printed after the run with where to allow them (`settings.permissions.allow` for Claude, `default_tools_approval_mode` for Codex).
- **Codex tracking.** The untrusted checkout's `hooks.json`, Entire's own included, isn't loaded, so Entire's hooks are passed as session flags. `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` lets them run without persisted trust; it also runs the user's own not-yet-approved Codex hooks, and still never the checkout's.
- **Gate.** Reviewing someone else's code still needs approval because the branch's skills load. The warning and `--show-config` (`isolated_agents` in `--json`) name the reviewers using their own config and list only what still loads; each run prints which reviewers use their own config.

+2802/-78 in 32 files.

## Testing

- `mise run check` passes.
- Integration test: `entire review` against fake `claude` and `codex` launchers checks what each receives (profile settings and MCP servers, Entire's tracking hooks, Codex trust overrides and the hook-trust bypass, the blocked-tool notice) with the branch's MCP server left out.
- Unit tests: settings provenance and overlay order, structural validation and checkout-path warnings, per-agent argv and files, blocked-tool parsing for Claude and Codex, the gate inventory, and where configs are saved (`--set-config`, `none`, local-owned profiles, `--edit` re-saves).
- Real reviews with new binaries in a scratch repo, each tracked as an `agent_review` session:
  - Claude Code (haiku): the profile's MCP server started and its tool was called once allowed; the profile's `SessionStart`/`PreToolUse`/`Stop` hooks ran; the branch's hook and MCP server did not; the blocked-tool notice printed when the tool wasn't allowed.
  - Codex: the profile's MCP server started and its tool was called with `default_tools_approval_mode = "approve"`; the branch's MCP server and a planted branch hook did not run; the blocked-tool notice printed without it.
  - Pi (Gemini): the profile's extension loaded and the branch's did not. Pi runs needed #2759, a separate fix for Pi reviews reported as failed.

## Follow-ups

- Team-shared reviewer config (committed profile read from the default branch).
- Codex profile hooks (Entire's own run via session flags; user hooks per profile not yet).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes how review agents load hooks, MCP, and extensions from untrusted branches, with command validation and fail-closed behavior, but misconfiguration or gaps could still affect security-sensitive review runs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **per-reviewer agent config** on review profiles so a reviewer can run with your hooks/MCP/extensions instead of the reviewed checkout’s, while branch skills can still load where supported.
> 
> **Configuration & storage:** `ReviewConfig` gains optional `config` (`settings`, `mcp_servers`, `extensions`). Set via `entire review --edit` or `--configure --set-config reviewer=<file|isolated|none>`. Config is **never** written to shared `.entire/settings.json`; it lives in clone-local preferences or untracked `.entire/settings.local.json`, with the same trust rules as reviewer prompts. Unverifiable local config **blocks** the review rather than falling back to checkout config.
> 
> **Runtime:** `ReviewerTemplate` adds a `Prepare` step that validates commands (absolute paths outside checkouts, no `npx`/relative/`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, per-agent field support) and writes ephemeral 0600 files under the user cache. **Claude Code** uses user-only settings plus profile MCP, copies committed skills/commands as the `project` plugin, and rewrites `/skill` → `/project:skill`. **Codex** marks checkout and main repo untrusted and applies profile MCP via `-c`. **Pi** uses `--no-extensions` plus Entire’s extension and profile extensions.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"issues":[{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2779","title":"Count a turn's step and tokens once when its Stop repeats","issue_number":2779,"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1576
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Bug

A Stop for a file-changing turn can reach Entire more than once: a retried hook, a duplicate delivery, or two hook processes racing. Each repeat runs SaveStep again. It adds the turn's tokens to `TokenUsage` and `CheckpointTokenUsage` again, and increments `StepCount` again.

Measured with the real hooks before this fix:

| Agent | Session total | Pending window | `StepCount` | Committed checkpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code (turn 100/10) | 200/20 | 200/20 | 2 | 100/10 (correct) |
| Cursor (turn 200/50) | 400/100 | 400/100 | 2 | 400/100 |

- **Claude Code:** the committed checkpoint is right because condensation recounts it from the transcript. The session total stays doubled.
- **Cursor:** the hook tokens double end to end, including the committed checkpoint.
- **Git:** no extra commit is written, because SaveStep writes no git objects.

## Fix

SaveStep records which turn its last step came from, in the same locked mutation that adds the tokens and the step:

- **A repeat** is a Stop that read a transcript of the same byte size as the recorded step. A new turn grows the transcript. This covers a repeat whose pre-prompt state an earlier Stop already removed, and a turn that never had a TurnStart.
- **A Stop whose pre-prompt nonce** (`PrePromptState.TurnNonce`) **differs from the recorded one** is always a new turn.
  - TurnStart writes the nonce before it takes any session lock, so a TurnStart that times out on the lock still gets a fresh one. Such a TurnStart never rotates `TurnID`, which is why this is not keyed on `TurnID`.
  - A matching nonce alone is not enough: a Stop that ran late can read the next turn's nonce from the per-session pre-prompt file.
- **A repeat** still merges its files, but adds no tokens and no step.
  - Exception: if a commit condensed the window in between, the repeat counts one step, because its files are new pending work.

## Legitimate paths preserved

- **Normal Stop after TurnStart:** counts once.
- **First Stop after a mid-session enable, and turns with no TurnStart** (Droid exec mode, a turn the agent starts on its own): each grows the transcript, so each still counts.
- **A TurnStart that hit the session-lock timeout:** gets a new nonce, so its turn counts.
- **Antigravity's suppressed mid-turn TurnStart, mid-turn commits, and Ctrl-C recovery:** unchanged.
- **Compaction, Droid Workers and attach:** do not go through SaveStep.

## Overlap with #2722

#2722 applies a turn's tokens at the turn-end transition when the turn changes no files, gated on the ACTIVE phase. This PR covers the file-changing path, so the two do not overlap in behaviour. They do conflict textually: this PR wraps SaveStep's token block, which #2722 extracts into `applyTurnTokenUsage`. Whichever merges second resolves that.

Follow-up after both land: #2722's no-change path should record the same marker. Otherwise a no-change Stop followed by a file-changing repeat counts the turn twice.

Remaining gaps, unchanged from main:
- A Stop-hook continuation in the same turn still counts its tokens from transcript line 0.
- A late duplicate that reads the next turn's pre-prompt state is not caught.

## Tests

- **Integration, with real hooks:**
  - Claude Code: a repeated Stop, concurrent Stops, a next turn after the repeat, Stops without TurnStart (plus a repeat of one), and an unprompted turn after a prompted one.
  - Cursor: a repeated Stop and concurrent Stops, both checked through to the committed checkpoint.
- **Unit (SaveStep):**
  - a repeated nonce;
  - a matching nonce over a grown transcript (a late Stop holding the next turn's nonce) still counts;
  - a new nonce while `TurnID` stays unrotated;
  - matching on transcript size when there is no nonce;
  - turn identity unknown;
  - a repeat after condensation counts a step but no tokens, and keeps `TranscriptIdentifierAtStart`.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #2588. Fixes #2928 (same issue, reported on OpenCode 2.1.4; checked live on 2.1.4). Fixes #2810 (OpenCode 2 support): #2843 fixed the third OpenCode 2 break, text generation.

On OpenCode 2, Entire captured nothing:
- OpenCode 2 refuses to load the plugin; it only accepts `export default {id, setup}`.
- `opencode export` no longer exists. It prints help and exits 0, so there is no transcript.

This adds OpenCode 2 support with the same coverage as 1.x, and keeps OpenCode 1 working. Together with #2843 (merged), which fixed text generation (`opencode run --dir`), that completes #2810.

## What changes

**Plugin (`entire_plugin.ts`).** One file serves every version through its only export. The two loaders can't share a shape:
- OpenCode 1 before v1.3 calls every export as a function, so an object export makes OpenCode fail to start.
- OpenCode 2 requires the default export to be an `{id, setup}` object.

So the default export is chosen when the module loads. OpenCode 1 sets `OPENCODE=1` in its own environment and gets the existing 1.x plugin function, unchanged. Anything else gets `{id, server, setup}`, where `setup` is new.

**Plugin location: `.opencode/plugin/entire.ts`** (was `.opencode/plugins/`). OpenCode 0.15.x and 1.0.0 refuse to start when `.opencode/plugins` exists ("Use \"plugin\" instead"), so on main `entire enable` breaks OpenCode there. Every version loads `.opencode/plugin`.

Installing removes an Entire plugin an earlier CLI left in `.opencode/plugins`, because 1.0.224+ and 2.x load both directories and would run it twice. It also removes the directory when that empties it; the user's own plugins stay. `entire status`/`doctor` report a leftover as outdated, and an earlier CLI's install still counts as installed. The repo's own copy moves too. With mixed CLI versions, a teammate on an older CLI can re-create the old file. On OpenCode 1 the new plugin then stands down, so hooks still fire once (checked live on 1.18.33); OpenCode 2 can't load the old copy at all.

How `setup` works:
- **Shared service.** OpenCode 2 runs plugins in a background service shared by every repository. Hooks are per repo, but events are process-wide and execution events carry no location. The plugin only acts on sessions its own prompt hook saw, and asks OpenCode (`ctx.session.get`) whether each one is top-level or a subagent child. It never blocks the service: hooks that must finish first are awaited async spawns with a timeout, and events are handled in a queue per top-level session, so one session's slow hook never delays another session's turn end. Spawned hooks run without the service's `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`.
- **Turns.** A turn is one OpenCode execution:
  - turn-start comes from the prompt hook, and turn-end fires when the execution ends;
  - compaction comes from `session.compaction.ended`, and session-end from `location.shutdown`;
  - a prompt sent mid-turn joins the running execution.
- **Subagents, foreground and background.** The `subagent` tool maps onto the existing subagent-start and subagent-stop payloads, and every stop waits for its start. A background call is announced when it launches, and its stop is held until the child's own execution ends. The result delivered back to the parent is a turn with no prompt, the same as on 1.x.
- **Exit.** `opencode run --standalone` kills plugin cleanup about 3s after the turn. So turn-end, session-end, compaction and held subagent stops run detached. Each waits (by PID, bounded) for the session's earlier detached hooks, and the next turn-start waits for them, so a session's hooks land in the same order as on 1.x. Without this, session-end overtook turn-end and the commit got no checkpoint. Every subagent stop also waits for its subagent-start.

**Export (Go).**
- `opencode --version` is probed once per process, reusing #2843's parser. Only a readable 0.x/1.x version keeps `opencode export <id>`; anything else uses `opencode session export --standalone <id>`. A failed probe is not cached.
- A 2.x export is converted to the 1.x shape at capture (`normalizeOpenCodeExport`), so prompts, files, tokens, subagent slicing, stored checkpoints and entire.io's transcript view are unchanged:
  - tool names map back (`subagent`→`task`, `patch`→`apply_patch`, `shell`→`bash`);
  - paths become absolute;
  - synthetic and compaction messages become their 1.x equivalents.

  The conversion is deterministic, because transcript offsets are message indices. Sessions OpenCode 2 migrated from a 1.x database keep 1.x tool names and are accepted too.
- Chunking now carries raw JSON, so fields the typed structs don't model survive it.

**Resume.** On 1.x, resuming in a fresh clone imports the checkpoint back into OpenCode. 2.x now does the same:
- Each converted message keeps the OpenCode 2 messages it came from under `info.opencode2`. Resume imports exactly those with `opencode session import --standalone`, run from the worktree.
- Session info is restored from an allowlist only. `permissions`, `agent` and `metadata` come from checkpoint data, so restoring them would let anyone who can push checkpoints change tool approval in the resuming user's OpenCode.
- Attachments that redaction changed are dropped, because OpenCode rejects the whole import otherwise.
- A session OpenCode still has is never deleted or replaced.
- On OpenCode 1, resume no longer imports the stored session's permission rules. Until now it restored them as is, which let anyone who can push checkpoints change tool approval in the resuming user's OpenCode.
- A checkpoint captured from 1.x (or by an older Entire) has no 2.x messages, and resuming it on 2.x reports that.

**e2e.**
- The `opencode` runner detects OpenCode 2. It drives `run` and the TUI with `--standalone`, takes the TUI model from `opencode.json`, skips the 1.x plugin-dependency pre-build, and recognizes the 2.x TUI's turn footer.
- CI gets a new `opencode-2` leg on main pushes, pinned to `@opencode/cli@2.1.1` and outside the reliable tier for now. The nightly smoke runs the latest 2.x from its own npm prefix, so an upstream release that breaks the plugin shows up within a day.
- The 1.x leg's floating installer now fails if it ever installs OpenCode 2.

## Verification

Live runs used the real OpenCode 2.1.1 and 1.18.33 binaries, with isolated XDG directories and this branch's binary. Unless noted, the model was a scripted mock (free).

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| 2.x write/edit/shell, patch (gpt model id), compaction, three runs on one session | checkpoints with files, tokens, prompt and model; hooks in order |
| 2.x foreground and background subagents | task records with child transcripts; background stop when the child finishes; wake-up turn |
| Two repos on one shared service at once | each repo saw only its own session |
| 2.x interactive TUI (tmux) | 2 turns plus a subagent; checkpoint with task record |
| 1.x session continued on 2.x (DB migration) | old and new turns both captured |
| Real Gemini sessions pushed to a scratch repo on entire.com | 3 checkpoints incl. a real subagent call, checked through Entire's API |
| Fresh clone with an empty OpenCode store → `entire session resume` → `opencode run -s` | session restored; Gemini recalled the earlier turn |
| Version matrix: same capture scenario (edits, shell, subagent, commit) | checkpoint with all files plus the task record on 1.0.224, 1.1.65, 1.2.27, 1.3.0, 1.3.3, 1.4.17, 1.14.51, 1.17.20, 1.18.33, 1.19.3, 2.0.0, 2.0.16, 2.0.32, 2.1.1 and 2.1.2. With the new directory, 0.15.31 and 1.0.0 start, load the plugin and fire its hooks. Both then crash in OpenCode's own cost calculation on today's provider responses (`DecimalError`), with or without Entire, so neither finishes a turn |
| Upgrade from main's install (`.opencode/plugins`) | `entire status` reports it out of date; `entire enable` moves the plugin and removes the empty old directory |
| 1.x hook-order flakiness | session-start/turn-start occasionally missing or out of order on 1.x, as on main: 2 of 6 runs on main, 0 of 6 here |
| **e2e suite on 2.1.1** (`gemini-2.5-flash`, paid) | 50/53 pass; the other 3 are other agents' tests and skip |

`mise run lint` and the canary pass. `mise run check` passes apart from `TestProbeConfigDir_AsksClaude`, a Claude Code test that times out under heavy machine load and passes when re-run on its own.

New tests:
- the converter and import round trip on real 2.1.1 exports in `testdata/opencode2` (repo path scrubbed), including byte-identical messages after the round trip;
- import hardening: the real redactor's output, and the session-info allowlist;
- version selection;
- a Node-driven harness for the OpenCode 2 plugin covering lifecycle, shutdown, mid-turn prompts, other repos, foreground and background subagents, start-before-stop, held stops before session-end, interrupted launchers, and 1.x calling `setup`, a slow hook in one session while another session's turn ends, and a held stop still waiting for its start at shutdown. Both of those fail on the previous version of the plugin.

## Trade-offs and follow-ups
- **Storage:** keeping the OpenCode 2 originals for exact resume roughly doubles an OpenCode 2 transcript in checkpoints. A slimmer variant would store only the fields the conversion loses.
- **Quitting the 2.x TUI** leaves the session idle rather than ended: the shared service keeps running, so OpenCode never reports the location shutting down. session-end fires when the service stops. Commits still link the session.
- **Back-to-back `opencode run`s:** if a run's final turn-end takes longer than cleanup's ~2.5s, the next run's turn-start can arrive before it finishes.
- **Background subagents** still running when `opencode run --standalone` exits are killed with it, the same as 1.x `run`.
- **Not verified live on 2.x:** OpenCode Desktop and Windows.

https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2631/changes/cli/1703
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

fixes #2902. part of [COR-2277](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-2277/validate-the-checkpoint-detail-slow-host-breaker-and-fix-the-cli) (item 2, the cli fix; the entire-brain items stay open).

## problem

on a fresh clone, `entire checkpoint explain` fetches the whole checkpoint archive from the checkpoint remote, bounded by a fixed 2-minute deadline (`checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout`). when the archive takes longer than that, git is killed, the partial pack is thrown away, the ref never lands, and the next explain starts the same fetch from zero. it never finishes. on entireio/cli (5.1 GB) every explain took 120s and returned nothing, which made `entire-brain setup` look hung for ~2.7h.

i found the same pattern in my own clone: 8 abandoned `tmp_pack_*` files of 187-518 MB each, written about 2 minutes apart on 15 oct, 2.9 GB thrown away in ten minutes.

the deadline went from 30s to 2 minutes in d46dfcc68b for the same failure. any fixed number breaks again once the archive outgrows it, so this replaces the deadline rather than raising it.

## what changes

- **foreground fetches (explain, resume, enable, checkpoint delete) have no fixed per-fetch deadline.** they run within one overall budget of 30 minutes that covers the lock wait and the transfer; `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_FETCH_TIMEOUT` (a go duration like `45m`) overrides it, and an invalid value falls back to 30m with a warning. a watchdog also kills git once it has written nothing to stdout or stderr for 10 minutes, on any transport (http, ssh, `entire://`); a stalled fetch fails with `fetch stalled`. the push hot path keeps its 30s budget.
- **`--progress` on those fetches**, so git reports objects as they arrive. it only redraws when an object completes, so a single large object arrives in silence: through a 1 MB/s throttle, a fetch of one 40 MB object printed nothing for 49s, while 300 small objects never went more than 0.5s without output. the 10 minute window is sized for that. fetch error details keep only the final text of each redrawn progress line.
- **parallel foreground fetches in one repo wait on a lock** in the git common dir (existing `internal/flock`). the waiter's fetch then negotiates against the objects that just landed and transfers almost nothing. the lock is held through promotion of the shared tmp ref, since otherwise one caller's cleanup can delete the ref under the next caller's fetch. a waiter prints that it is waiting, and ctrl-c or the budget running out stops the wait with an error. a waiter never falls back to its own transfer, which would move the archive once per waiter. if the lock can't be taken for any other reason, the fetch runs unserialized with a warning.
- **after a fetch stalls or runs out of budget, the next ones fail fast.** the fetch records the failure (redacted url, ref, reason, time) next to the fetch lock, and for 2 minutes foreground fetches of the same ref from the same remote fail with `checkpoint remote failed recently` without contacting it. without this, commands queued on the lock behind a stalled fetch each paid the 10 minute window in turn, and so did every new process: at entire-brain's fan-out of 4, roughly 40h for the issue's 319 checkpoints against ~2.7h on main (estimated from the design, not measured). only stalls and budget exhaustion are recorded, so a fast failure like bad credentials can be retried right after the fix, and a successful fetch clears the record.
- **`entire enable` keeps the local orphan when the empty-orphan heal can't fetch**, including when its lock wait fails, and the heal checks again for checkpoint data once it holds the lock, since one can land while it waits.
- **the push path uses its own tmp ref**, so a push-time fetch can't delete the ref a foreground fetch is about to promote.
- **`GIT_SSH` is shell-quoted** when copied into `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` for batch-mode ssh, so a windows path like `C:\Program Files\...\ssh.exe` survives `sh`.
- one `[entire] Fetching checkpoints from <url>` status line on stderr, only when it's a terminal. it clears the spinner line first so the two don't overlap.

## evidence

measured locally against a real `git http-backend` behind a throttling proxy at 150 KB/s, serving a 26 MB checkpoint archive (one real checkpoint plus incompressible history). same workload for both binaries, machine kept awake:

- explain, run 1: main took 121s, returned `checkpoint not found`, and threw away ~17 MB. this branch took 187s, returned the checkpoint, and the ref landed.
- explain, run 2: main took 120s and failed the same way. this branch took 0s and transferred no pack.
- 3 explains in parallel: all returned the checkpoint. the server sent the 26.9 MB pack once; the others got 82-179 byte responses.
- lock can't be taken: the fetch still succeeded and logged a warning.

the stall row from the earlier run (aborted after 71s) was measured with the http low-speed abort this branch replaced. the watchdog is covered by the tests below and was not re-measured over http.

caveat: this is a synthetic archive (few large objects, local throttle), not the real 5.1 GB one on github. the issue reporter measured the real one: the full fetch takes 677s when it isn't killed, and explain then drops from 120.1s to 1.05s.

## tests

no git-over-http in the test suite; everything uses local-path remotes or a fake ssh.

- `TestBoundFetch`: foreground mode has no deadline and enables the stall abort; the hot path keeps its 30s deadline.
- `TestFetch_AbortStalledKillsSilentFetch` and `TestFetch_AbortStalledLetsProgressingFetchRun`: a fake ssh that goes silent is killed; one that keeps printing for longer than the idle limit is not.
- `TestFetch_AbortStalledRequestsProgress`: fails if `--progress` is removed.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_WaitsForConcurrentFetch`, `TestFetchMetadataBranch_CancelWhileWaitingForFetchLock`, `TestFetchMetadataBranch_ProceedsWhenFetchLockUnavailable`.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_BudgetExpiresWhileWaitingForFetchLock`: a waiter out of budget fails with an error naming the env var and does not fetch.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_BudgetBoundsTheFetch`: a real git fetch to a server that accepts and never answers is killed at the budget.
- `TestParseForegroundFetchBudget`.
- `TestFetchBranchIfMissing_LeavesForegroundTmpRefAlone`.
- `TestFetch_BatchModeRunsGITSSHPathWithBackslash` and a quoting case in `TestWithBatchModeSSH`.
- `TestErrWithGitOutput_DropsOverwrittenProgress`.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_FailsFastAfterSlowFailure`: after a fetch hits its budget against a silent server, the next fetch fails fast and opens no new connection.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_WaiterFailsFastWhenHolderStalls`: a waiter on the lock fails as soon as the holder records a stall, without contacting the remote.
- `TestFetchMetadataBranch_SlowFailureScope`: another remote still fetches, an expired record is retried and then cleared, and a fast failure is not recorded.
- `TestEnsurePrimaryRef_HealLockWaitFailureKeepsOrphan` and `TestEnsurePrimaryRef_HealKeepsCheckpointWrittenWhileWaitingForLock`.

not covered: a real stalled http or `entire://` transfer, windows beyond ci, and the lock-through-promotion ordering (the lock test can't tell it apart from lock-through-fetch).

## known gaps / follow-ups

- the read-remote path (`fetchMetadataFromReadRemotes`) still caps full fetches from named remotes at 2 minutes per candidate and 3 minutes total, and the blob-hydration fallback (`fetchBlobsByHash`) runs under the same 3-minute `ReadChainBudget`. not changed here.
- on a git-branch primary, an archive too large for 30s is re-attempted on every `git push` (`fetchMetadataBranchIfMissing`).
- explain still reports `checkpoint not found` when the real cause was a failed fetch.
- abandoned `tmp_pack_*` cleanup and fetching once per invocation, both suggested in the issue, aren't done. the negative cache above only covers slow failures, for 2 minutes.
- on a healthy remote, a waiter still runs its own fetch after the holder lands the ref. it only negotiates, since the pack is already local, and checkpoint delete needs the fresh remote tip anyway.
- stall detection reads git's output, so it can't fail faster than 10 minutes without killing healthy single-object transfers. watching bytes land in `tmp_pack` would allow a 1-2 minute window and a live progress line.
- explain still downloads the whole archive to read one checkpoint; a partial or lazy fetch is the real fix for agent callers with short tool timeouts.
- the `GIT_SSH` quoting above fixes a separate bug on main: `withBatchModeSSH` sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, which git runs through `sh`, so a `GIT_SSH` path with spaces or backslashes broke the batch-mode ssh paths. it's small and covered by `git_test.go`, so it stays in this change.

","state":null,"user":null,"assignees":null,"labels":null,"milestone":null,"state_reason":null,"comments":null,"created_at":null,"updated_at":null,"closed_at":null,"display_url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2920","display_title":"fix(checkpoint): let foreground checkpoint fetches finish instead of restarting them"},{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2589","title":"feat(opencode): support OpenCode 2 with V1 fallback","issue_number":2589,"body":"## Summary

Makes the OpenCode integration work on OpenCode 2 while keeping OpenCode 1 working from the same generated plugin. Fixes #2588.

OpenCode 2 is a hard break in two places:

1. It loads a default plugin definition with `id` + `setup`/`effect`, and rejects V1 hook-map plugins with `PluginModule.LoadError: Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function`.
2. It moved export/import under `opencode session`; the V1 `opencode export` prints a help page and exits 0.

This builds on the approach in #2397 (thanks @aryasaatvik) but keeps OpenCode 1 plugin support instead of dropping it.

## Changes

**Plugin** (`entire_plugin.ts` + committed dogfood copy)
- Default export `{ id: "entire", setup(ctx) }` for OpenCode 2: `session.hook("prompt")` drives turn-start, `session.hook("context")` applies the turn-start context injection and tracks the model, and `ctx.event.subscribe()` handles `session.created`, `session.idle`/`session.status`/`session.execution.*`, `session.compacted`, `session.deleted`, `global.disposed`, `location.shutdown`.
- Keeps the named `EntirePlugin` export (older V1) and adds a `server()` factory on the default export (V1 ≥ 1.18.29).
- No runtime dependency on either SDK package (the V1 type import was removed), so the file loads under Bun and Node with no project `node_modules`.

**Commands** (`cli_commands.go`)
- Try `opencode session export` / `session import` first, fall back to the V1 top-level commands.
- Validate export output, so an exit-0 help page is not treated as a transcript, and preserve a classified V2 error across the fallback.

**Schema** (`types.go`, `transcript.go`, `transcript/compact/opencode.go`)
- Normalize OpenCode 2's flattened messages (`type` + `content`, message-level `text`) to the v1 model for reads, while keeping the raw transcript byte-preserving so `opencode session import` can resume the session.

**e2e**
- Accept `opencode v2.x` version output and skip V1 plugin-dependency seeding on major ≥ 2.

**Docs** — agent guide updated for both plugin APIs and both export commands.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/... ./e2e/agents/...` clean.
- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/... ./cmd/entire/cli/transcript/...` pass, including the new `opencode_v2_test.go` schema/export tests and a Node canary that drives the V2 `setup` path (session-start, turn-start, turn-end) alongside the existing V1 canary.
- Loaded the generated plugin against real **OpenCode 2.0.16**: the server logs `loading plugin` with no subsequent `failed to load plugin`.
- Confirmed the command split on 2.0.16: `opencode session export <id>` returns session JSON; `opencode export <id>` prints `DESCRIPTION`/`USAGE` and exits 0.

## Notes

- The V2 event subscription guards turn-end with a `turnActive` flag, because OpenCode 2 can report a turn ending via more than one event.
- OpenCode 1 remains fully supported; no config migration is required.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

E2E run [38724857355](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/38724857355/job/116388096213) failed `TestExplainCheckpoint` (claude-code). Haiku committed `docs/feature.md` itself, then ran `git reset HEAD~1`, and the test's own commit came out with two checkpoint trailers: the inherited `3afa00e9bfa6` (correct, via the redo inheritance from 6170bc1612) and a fresh `93418f0f011f`.

The fresh one was wrong. The reset put the file back in the worktree, the next turn end recorded it as touched again, and session matching saw transcript growth plus an overlapping staged file. The new checkpoint's transcript slice held only the agent's commit and reset, which the turn-end finalize had already folded into `3afa00e9bfa6`.

## Fix

- The redo step (`inheritReplacedCommitsTrailers`) now also reports which staged paths the inherited checkpoints already hold. A path counts only when the newest dropped commit that changed it carries a checkpoint that is not deleted and exists in this clone's store (`capturedCheckpoints`), and the staged content and mode both match what that commit left. Inheriting the trailer stays permissive: a trailer whose capture failed still links, but holds nothing, so the session's work gets a fresh checkpoint. Content, mode and deletions come from one rename-free read of the commit index git is preparing (`parseStagedRaw` now also keeps the staged mode, building on #2330), so `git commit -a` and path-limited commits compare what they commit.
- `PrepareCommitMsg` returns right after inheriting when every staged path is held, so a pure redo gets no fresh trailer, whatever the session phase.
- Otherwise the staged-files overlap check in `filterSessionsWithNewContent` sees only the redo's other staged paths, from the same rename-free view, so only other session work earns a fresh checkpoint. (A rename-detecting list would hide a staged deletion paired with a held file.)
- Prepare records the held paths in the inherited-trailers marker. After a redo that stamps no fresh trailer (pure, or partial with no session's other work), which condenses nothing, post-commit (`reconcileRedoneFiles`) drops them from this worktree's sessions' touched files when the commit holds the recorded content, as carry-forward would. Only held files go through that check; other touched files, steps and transcript growth stay pending untouched.
- `openRepositoryTimed` is extracted to keep `PrepareCommitMsg` under the `maintidx` limit; the `open_repository` span no longer includes the redo lookup.
- The deleted-checkpoint list is loaded once per commit, each dropped commit's diff is computed once, and store lookups are memoized.
- Documented in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md` and `docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md`.

## Deliberately not changed

Whenever a fresh trailer is stamped, a redundant checkpoint is preferred to a lost or dangling link:

- On a partial redo (redone files staged together with other files), the mid-turn agent fast path still stamps a fresh trailer. Transcripts miss edits made through shell commands (`sed -i`, formatters, codegen), so it cannot rule out new work.
- Post-commit judges overlap without the redo, so a session that only redid work may fold into another session's fresh checkpoint. An earlier commit on this branch excluded redone paths there, but that left a fresh trailer with no checkpoint behind it when a stale ACTIVE session tracked only redone files, or when a read-only ACTIVE session was gated out by a redo-only claimant.

## Real-agy quirks (all hardened in code + tests)

- **`invocationNum` is 0-indexed**; PreInvocation fires per *model invocation*. `invocationNum > 0` emits a conditional TurnStart (`Event.SuppressIfSessionActive`) the dispatcher drops only when a turn is genuinely mid-flight — so resumes (`agy --conversation`) are tracked and follow-up invocations don't clobber the pre-prompt baseline.
- **agy writes its transcript AFTER `Stop`.** `PrepareTranscript` briefly waits then materializes a placeholder; condensation degrades to a files/prompt-only checkpoint (agy-scoped) and prompts are re-extracted late (`resolvePromptsFromLateFlushedTranscript`).
- **Tokens have exactly one surface** — the title/statusline JSON. The global `title` slot is claimed by `entire hooks antigravity title-tee` (wrap-preserving, doctor-checked); TurnStart snapshots a baseline, TurnEnd computes the delta (`OutOfBandTokenSource`).
- **Tool args are double-encoded**; `decodeAgyString`/`decodeAgyBool` tolerate both shapes. macOS `/tmp` symlinks resolved.
- **No SessionStart hook surface** → silent tracking (same as Cursor/OpenCode/Copilot/Pi). agy's PostToolUse/PostInvocation hooks are deliberately **not installed** — no lifecycle mapping, and they'd spawn a no-op subprocess per tool call.

### Problem

Previously, checkpoints used a 1:N model — one checkpoint ID could span multiple commits. When an agent made several commits during a single turn, they all shared the same checkpoint ID. This made it impossible to tie a specific commit to a specific snapshot of session context, and the `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase added
 complexity to the state machine.

### Approach

Every user commit now gets its own unique checkpoint ID. The core challenge is that mid-turn commits happen before the agent is done — the transcript is incomplete. We solve this with a **provisional-then-finalize** pattern:

1. **At commit time (PostCommit hook):** Condense whatever transcript exists so far to `entire/checkpoints/v1` with a fresh checkpoint ID. This is *provisional* — the transcript is partial. Then carry forward any remaining uncommitted files to a new shadow branch so the next commit gets its own checkpoint.

2. **At turn end (Stop hook):** `HandleTurnEnd` iterates over all checkpoint IDs recorded during the turn (`TurnCheckpointIDs` on session state) and replaces each provisional transcript with the complete one via `UpdateCommitted`.

This means every checkpoint on `entire/checkpoints/v1` ends up with the full prompt-to-stop transcript, while each commit still gets its own unique ID for precise linking.

### Key changes

**New: `UpdateCommitted` on checkpoint store**
- Replace semantics (not append) — swaps transcript, prompts, and context blobs for a checkpoint's session folder
- Chunks large transcripts (matching `WriteCommitted` behavior)
- Redacts secrets before writing (matching `WriteCommitted` behavior)

**New: `TurnCheckpointIDs` on session state**
- Tracks checkpoint IDs condensed during the current agent turn
- Populated in PostCommit for ACTIVE sessions after successful condensation
- Consumed in `HandleTurnEnd` to finalize all checkpoints
- Cleared on new prompt (both strategies)

**New: `HandleTurnEnd` finalization**
- `TurnEndHandler` interface simplified — no longer takes `[]session.Action` parameter since work items come from state, not the action list
- Called unconditionally when strategy implements the interface (removed dead `if len(remaining) > 0` guard)

**Phase simplification**
- Removed `ACTIVE_COMMITTED` phase — the state machine is now 3 phases: ACTIVE, IDLE, ENDED
- `active_committed` in persisted state normalizes to ACTIVE (not IDLE) so pending finalization isn't lost on upgrade

**PostCommit carry-forward**
- After condensation, uncommitted files are carried forward to a new shadow branch
- Ensures the next commit gets its own checkpoint ID instead of accumulating into the previous one

## Problem
OpenCode emits a user `message.updated` event before the `message.part.updated` event containing the prompt text. The plugin starts the turn from that metadata event with an empty prompt so a fast agent commit still sees an ACTIVE session. Because the message was then marked as seen, the later text part was ignored and checkpoints lost the user prompt.

The first version of this PR kept a marker for those promptless starts and fired `turn-start` again when the text arrived. That recovered the prompt, but `turn-start` is not a prompt setter. It captures pre-prompt Git state, creates a new `TurnID`, recalculates prompt attribution, and clears `LastCheckpointID` and `TurnCheckpointIDs`.

The timing this fallback exists for makes that destructive. A checkpoint may already have been created between the empty metadata event and the text event.

The new integration regression exercises exactly that order:

```
message.updated
  → turn-start with empty prompt
  → agent commit and checkpoint
  → message.part.updated with prompt text
```

Against the second-`turn-start` implementation, the prompt was recorded, but the original turn ID changed, the pre-prompt snapshot was replaced, attribution was recalculated, and both checkpoint fields were cleared.

## Fix
Keep the early empty `turn-start`, but repair the missing text through a new internal `PromptUpdate` lifecycle event.

`PromptUpdate` writes the late text to `prompt.txt` and updates session `LastPrompt`. It does not call `CapturePrePromptState` or `InitializeSession`, so it cannot start another logical turn or reset checkpoint bookkeeping.
The file and state updates run inside `MutateSessionState`. Checkpoint condensation clears `prompt.txt` while holding the same session lock, so either ordering is safe:

- If repair gets the lock first, condensation sees and checkpoints the prompt before clearing the file.
- If condensation gets the lock first, repair writes the prompt after condensation finishes, leaving it available for turn-end finalization.
The OpenCode plugin keeps a `promptlessTurnStarts` marker per message. Empty text updates leave the marker pending; the first non-empty part sends one synchronous `prompt-update`; later duplicates do nothing. Multiple pending messages are tracked independently. The set is cleared on session switches, session deletion, and server disposal.

The generated plugin template and the checked-in dogfood plugin remain byte-identical.

## Cost
The plugin does expected `O(1)` set work per event and keeps `O(P)` additional state for `P` promptless messages awaiting text.
A late repair starts one synchronous hook subprocess, reads and rewrites `prompt.txt` in `O(Q + L)` time for existing prompt data `Q` and incoming prompt length `L`, and performs `O(S)` session-state I/O for state size `S`.

It performs no worktree scan. The earlier second-`turn-start` path repeated work proportional to worktree size `F`, including both status walks used by turn initialization.

In the real OpenCode run, the empty `turn-start` took 74 ms and the subsequent `prompt-update` took 5 ms in the same repository.

## Verification

- [x] Regression test fails before the fix by capturing only the empty fallback prompt.
- [x] Regression test passes after the fix with `turn-start("")` followed by `prompt-update("preserve this prompt")`.
- [x] Duplicate text-part updates do not trigger additional hooks.
- [x] OpenCode package tests pass.
- [x] `mise run check` passes, including lint, race-enabled unit and integration tests, and E2E canary tests.
- [x] The generated plugin template matches the repository’s installed OpenCode plugin.
- [x] A real `opencode run` session produced a checkpoint containing the complete original prompt.
- [x] A checkpoint occurring between the metadata event and prompt-text event preserves the original turn and checkpoint bookkeeping.
- [x] Prompt repair avoids repeating the complete `turn-start` lifecycle.

## Scope
`PromptUpdate` is an internal lifecycle event used only by OpenCode in this change. There are no new CLI flags, settings, dependencies, or changes to other agent integrations.

## Summary

The root corruption is git's own bug, not Entire's, and cannot be prevented from a hook: git (and go-git v6, independently) treats a missing \`.git/index\` (ENOENT) as an empty in-core index, and \`git status\` renames a fresh index over the real one as a side effect — so any concurrent process running \`git status\` at the wrong moment can cause a commit to record an empty tree. The previously-merged mitigation (#2143) already scrubs Entire's own \`git status\` calls, but by the time any hook runs, git has already read the index — prevention was never available from here, only detection.

**A second, previously-unknown data-loss bug was found while investigating, and that one is Entire's, and is fixed here**: when an empty-tree commit happens, Entire's \`post-commit\` hook still ran condensation on it — consuming the session's pending checkpoint data. So even if a user notices and runs \`git reset --mixed HEAD~1\` to recover, the checkpoint data backing that work was already gone. \`post-commit\` now detects an empty-tree commit and skips condensation entirely; \`prepare-commit-msg\` warns before the commit lands, naming the recovery command and \`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0\`.

## Evidence
- Real repro against a binary built from \`origin/main\`: staged files silently committed as an empty tree, exit 0, files still on disk — confirmed with real git, not simulated.
- Same repro on this branch: both warnings fire, naming the exact recovery steps.
- New \`gitrepo.IndexRecordsNoEntries\` distinguishes "missing" from "genuinely empty" (only a positively-parsed zero-entry header counts), refuses non-regular files (stats before opening — a FIFO at the index path would otherwise block \`open(2)\` forever), and works on sha256 repos (verified against their different empty-tree hash).
- **Mutation-tested**: 9 deliberate mutations (removing the post-commit skip, removing the prepare-commit-msg wiring, removing the stat-before-open, etc.) each turn a passing test red, proving the tests aren't vacuous.
- Adversarial review pass found and fixed 5 issues before this PR (a coverage gap where deleting the hook wiring left everything green, the FIFO-blocking hazard, a dangling-trailer edge case documented as accepted, an errno-masking bug, and a factually-incorrect code comment) — see commit body for the full list.

## Test plan
- \`mise run fmt\` clean, \`mise run lint\` 0 issues, \`go vet\` clean under default/integration/e2e tags.
- \`mise run test\`: 10,719 passed, 9 skipped. \`mise run test:integration\`: 565 passed, 3 skipped. \`mise run test:e2e:canary\`: 56 vogon + 4 roger-roger passed (free).
- \`-race\` clean on \`gitrepo\`, \`cli\`, \`strategy\`.
- \`mise run check\`/\`test:ci\` intentionally not run here (executes real agents with live model calls) — everything else it covers was run individually.
- Perf cost measured: +0.1ms per hook invocation.

## Remaining risk (documented, not hidden)
- The corruption itself cannot be prevented from a hook — user-side mitigation is \`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0\`, now named in the warning message.
- One accepted false positive: \`git rm -r --cached .\` then commit warns twice and skips post-commit condensation; the next ordinary commit condenses normally (verified).
- A kept (not reset) empty-tree commit still carries an unclaimed checkpoint trailer — documented, not suppressed, since suppressing it would make the warning conditional on a hazard the user may choose to ignore.

## Side findings for a maintainer (out of scope here, not fixed in this PR)
- \`strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go\`'s \`getStagedFiles\` runs \`git diff --cached\` without \`gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides()\` inside prepare-commit-msg, violating the rule this repo adopted after #2143 (~15 call sites share the gap). Consequence is a wrong condensation decision, not data loss.
- go-git's ENOENT-as-empty-index behavior is now documented but not defended against in a few of Entire's own readers (\`content_overlap.go\`, \`settings/opf_command_trust.go\`, \`gitrepo.Status\`) — no destructive consumer currently, but \`IndexRecordsNoEntries\` is there to route them through if someone wants to close this fully.

@lcv-leo, thank you for the report. You traced the bug to the exact line in `resolveWorktreeCandidates`, and you'd already written and verified a patch, so this PR builds on your fix. Earlier today [I asked](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2979#issuecomment-6618856546) whether you planned to open a PR, and asked @peyton-alt to assign the issue to me if you weren't. I'm opening this now because I have the fix reproduced, with tests that fail on `main` and pass here. If you'd rather open your own PR, just say so and I'll close this one.

## What was wrong

If you commit from a worktree that has no Entire session, the CLI falls back to sessions from other worktrees of the same repo. `resolveWorktreeCandidates` only checks the 15-minute `recentSessionWindow` when those sessions come from more than one worktree. If they all come from one worktree, it links them without checking, no matter how long they've been idle. In the report, a Codex session that had been idle for over a day got linked to every commit made from another worktree. Each time, `post-commit` condensed its 5 GB transcript.

## The fix

`findSessionsForCommitLinking` now runs the fallback's matches through `withoutIdleSessions`. It drops a session whose last interaction is older than `recentSessionWindow`. These sessions are kept:

- a session with no recorded interaction, as before, because we don't know how long it's been idle;
- a session that's mid-turn (active phase, turn started within `activeSessionInteractionThreshold`), because `LastInteractionTime` only changes at turn boundaries;
- a session with a background subagent still running (`hasFreshLiveTaskRecord`), the same case `idleWithLiveTaskRecord` already trusts;
- a session that recorded edits in the committing worktree, which still joins through its worktree entry, limited to those edits.

Amend and post-rewrite use `findSessionsForWorktree` to keep existing links up to date, and they don't change. The multi-worktree path doesn't change either.

Here's how this differs from the patch in the issue. Review on my fork found that putting the check inside `resolveWorktreeCandidates` also hid idle sibling sessions from amend and post-rewrite. It also dropped sessions that were mid-turn or had a subagent running. So the check now runs only for commit linking, and it keeps those two cases. The drop is logged at Debug, without `idle_for`. I'm happy to switch to the Info line from your patch if you prefer it.

## Tests

New file `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/worktree_idle_fallback_test.go`:

- `TestCommitLinking_FallbackSkipsSiblingSessionsIdleBeyondTheWindow`: idle for a day, idle just past the window, recent, no recorded interaction, mid-turn past the window, left active for two days, idle with a subagent in flight, idle with a finished subagent, and stale next to recent and undated.
- `TestCommitLinking_IdleSiblingSessionThatEditedHereStillJoins`
- `TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession`

On `main` with only the test file added, 5 subtests fail. The last two tests pass there; they guard behaviour that must not change:

```
--- FAIL: TestCommitLinking_FallbackSkipsSiblingSessionsIdleBeyondTheWindow
    --- FAIL: .../idle_for_a_day
    --- FAIL: .../idle_just_past_the_window
    --- PASS: .../recent
    --- PASS: .../no_recorded_interaction
    --- PASS: .../mid-turn_past_the_window
    --- FAIL: .../left_active_for_two_days
    --- PASS: .../idle_with_a_subagent_in_flight
    --- FAIL: .../idle_with_a_finished_subagent
    --- FAIL: .../stale_beside_recent_and_undated
--- PASS: TestCommitLinking_IdleSiblingSessionThatEditedHereStillJoins
--- PASS: TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession
FAIL
```

On this branch, all 12 pass.

## What I ran

I ran these on this exact tree in a clean `env -i` with a throwaway HOME, Go 1.27.3 and git 2.56:

- `go vet`, then `go test -count=1` of `./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/` and `./cmd/entire/cli/`: pass.
- `go test -race` on `strategy`: pass. Windows `go vet` and a Windows test build of `strategy`: pass.
- `mise run lint`: 0 issues.
- Complexity gate, run the way CI runs it (`BASE_REF=711697ee5 mise run complexity:gate`): pass.
- A one-off check of the nested layout (`.worktrees/nested` under the main checkout): an idle session in the main checkout isn't linked, and a recent one is. That test isn't in this PR.

## Review on my fork

Before opening this, I had the review bots go over it on my fork. "Ran" means I reproduced the finding with a test before changing anything.

- Kilo, first commit: a sibling session mid-turn for over 15 minutes was dropped. Ran: confirmed, fixed, and covered by `mid-turn_past_the_window`.
- Kilo, first commit: the check also hid idle sibling sessions from amend and post-rewrite. Ran: confirmed with a post-rewrite test, fixed by moving the check to commit linking, and covered by `TestPostRewrite_StillRemapsAnIdleSiblingSession`.
- Kilo and Codex, second commit: an idle session with a background subagent still running was dropped. Ran: confirmed, fixed, and covered by `idle_with_a_subagent_in_flight`.
- Baz noted that a turn longer than 24h still drops out. Read-only: I didn't change it, because that's the same limit `activeSessionInteractionThreshold` sets everywhere else.
- On the final head: Codex, Kilo and Greptile reported no issues. Gitar and CodeRabbit didn't review because of plan limits on my fork.

The commit has no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

## Open questions, possible follow-ups

These came from the issue. I kept them out of this PR so it stays small:

1. **Sessions with no recorded interaction.** They're still linked, as on `main`. Should the fallback drop them too?
2. **Hint message.** A dropped idle session is only logged. The ambiguous multi-worktree case prints an `entire session adopt` hint. Do you want a one-line hint here too, given the concern in #1852 about losing links silently? It would show up on every terminal commit while an agent sits idle in another worktree.
3. **Nested `.worktrees/` case.** A worktree under the main checkout matches the parent checkout's sessions through `parentWorktreeMatches`, and this check applies there too. I checked that by hand but didn't add a test for it. Should that layout get the same treatment and its own test?

## Problem

Entire tracks Antigravity (agy) subagents as unrelated top-level sessions and counts agy's tokens from the wrong source. A live run on main (agy 1.4.2, one subagent):

| | Entire on main | agy's own per-call records |
|---|---|---|
| Parent session | 16,478 in / 134 out, 2 calls | 81,107 / 926, 10 calls |
| Subagent | 0 | 18,519 / 254, 3 calls |
| Plain session, 4 turns | 95 / 27 | 48,383 / 98 |

The causes:

- **Wrong token source.** Entire reads agy's tokens only from the title/statusline feed, which has three problems:
  - the snapshot carrying a turn's last call usually lands just after Stop, so single-call turns record nothing;
  - its `total_input_tokens` is how full the context is, not a running total;
  - it never fires for subagent conversations or `agy -p`.
- **Subagents aren't linked to their parent.** agy runs each `invoke_subagent` as a separate conversation with its own hooks, and Entire records it as a separate top-level session.
- **Parent turns restart mid-turn.** A parent waiting on a subagent is resumed by a new execution whose first PreInvocation has `invocationNum` 0. That fired an unconditional TurnStart, so everything before the last resume dropped out of the turn.
- **Parent turns can stay open forever.** If the parent's last Stop (`fullyIdle: false`) lands before the subagent finishes, agy sends the parent nothing further. Its turn never ends, and in `-p` mode the parent stays ACTIVE as a ghost.

## Change

1. **Tokens from the transcript.** Since 1.4, agy writes each model call's `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `cache_read_tokens` on its `PLANNER_RESPONSE` step in `transcript_full.jsonl`.
   - Antigravity now implements `TokenCalculator` over those steps, so `resolveTurnTokenUsage` reads them before the statusline.
   - `output_tokens` already includes reasoning: in print mode agy reports `thinking_tokens` 2310 inside `output_tokens` 2313.
   - Transcripts without these fields (older agy) return nil, so the statusline stays the fallback for them.
2. **Subagent support.** Antigravity implements `SubagentSessionResolver`, the interface Factory Droid Workers use.
   - The link needs two text formats agy writes, and both must be present:
     - the child transcript's first step is a `SYSTEM_MESSAGE` with `sender=<parent>`;
     - the parent's transcript has a "Created the following subagent" step naming the child.
   - The task's tool-use ID is the child's conversation ID, since agy tool calls have no IDs. Its type and description come from the call's `TypeName` and `Role`.
   - If agy changes either format, the child falls back to being a top-level session, as on main.
3. **Subagent sessions never act on their own** (shared code, so Droid Workers get this too).
   - Once its parent is known, a subagent's state carries `ParentSessionID`. Such a session never links a commit, never condenses on its own, and is never picked as "the calling session". Identity matching would otherwise tie it with the parent, because they share an agy process.
   - Its file changes go to the parent.
   - A live task record on the parent carries its transcript so far, so a commit made while the subagent runs goes to the parent's checkpoint as the parent's task.
   - Condensing a subagent session from doctor or the exited-owner sweep hands its files to the parent and marks it done.
   - Later hooks rebuild the link from the parent's task record instead of re-reading transcripts.
4. **A wake-up doesn't restart the parent's turn.** At PreInvocation, a new prompt's `USER_INPUT` step is already in the transcript, while a subagent's reply isn't yet. So `invocationNum` 0 starts a turn unconditionally only when the transcript ends with `USER_INPUT`, or doesn't exist yet. An Esc-interrupted turn fires no Stop at all, and the next prompt still starts its own turn.
5. **A paused parent is ended when its subagents finish.**
   - A `fullyIdle: false` Stop records the pause (`AwaitingSubagentsAt`), and a resume clears it.
   - The parent's turn is ended only once every subagent the turn involved (launched, messaged, or heard from, per the parent's transcript) has stopped, and every reply it sent (`send_message` to the parent) is in the parent's transcript. An unread reply will wake the parent, so its turn isn't over yet.
   - A subagent whose agent died counts as stopped. A subagent woken again is running.
   - "Done" comes from the subagents' own sessions, not task records, which track pending checkpoint work.
   - The subagent's turn end and the parent's Stop can land milliseconds apart in either order, so both check. The first to find the turn done claims it (`SubagentTurnEndClaimed`, cleared at the next turn start). A pause reported after the claim can't re-arm it.
   - New agent capability: `SubagentReplyCounter`.
6. **Marking at any tool call.** A subagent is marked at its first tool call of any kind, not only at file edits, because a shell command can edit and commit.

## Subagent tokens in the parent's total

Since #2824, an agy child's turns are credited to the parent's total once, on the same path as Factory Droid Workers: `entire status` and the checkpoint's `subagent_tokens` include them. `TestAntigravity_SubagentWorkBelongsToTheParent` checks it.

## Review fixes

- A Stop for a turn already ended for its subagents is dropped, so the parent's tokens and step are not counted twice (`TestAntigravity_LateStopAfterSubagentTurnEndCountsNothing`).
- A working subagent's hooks keep it live, so one running past `StuckActiveThreshold` still holds its parent's turn (`TestAntigravity_LongRunningSubagentKeepsItsParentWaiting`).
- Only children this parent created hold its turn (`TestTurnSubagents_OnlyChildrenThisParentCreated`). A created child with no session state here is still waited on.
- `entire doctor` sets a stuck ACTIVE subagent IDLE after handing its work to the parent; ENDED stays ENDED.
- A subagent whose first step is cut off by the 256 KiB head read (a very long prompt) is still linked.
- Planner steps without `step_index` are separate calls.
- A Droid commit made during a Worker's turn is covered by `TestFactoryDroidWorkerFileCommittedMidTurn` (passes on main and here).
- Known costs, deferred and documented in `agent/antigravity/AGENT.md`: one bounded transcript head read per tool call, and a whole-file read once per prompt or wake.

## Tests

- **Unit tests:**
  - the token calculator, on a trimmed real transcript;
  - the resolver, including its fail-closed cases: a top-level conversation, a sender that didn't create the child, no child transcript yet, a missing parent transcript, an invalid sender ID, a path outside the brain directory, and several calls in one step;
  - the PreInvocation wake-up rule;
  - the shared filters: commit linking, caller resolution, and condense handing work to the parent.
- **Integration tests** (simulated hooks, in the hook order captured from live agy):
  - tokens from transcript steps, with late and context-fill statusline snapshots present;
  - a subagent writing a file, with a commit while it runs: one checkpoint session plus `tasks/<child>/`, and the parent's turn kept whole across the wake-up;
  - the parent's turn ended in both race orders; kept open for an unread reply and for a subagent woken again;
  - a subagent marked at a shell-command tool call;
  - a condense that can't reach the parent leaves the subagent's files in place.

  Each fails without its change.
- **Live runs with this branch** (agy 1.4.2):

  | Run | Parent (Entire = agy) | Subagent's task (Entire = agy) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Subagent writes `notes.txt` | 22,120 / 292, 3 calls | 22,294 / 272, 3 calls |
  | Subagent writes `notes2.txt` | 22,054 / 293, 3 calls | 22,248 / 190, 3 calls |
  | Read-only subagent | 22,257 / 399, 3 calls | 18,704 / 343, 3 calls |
  | Read-only subagent | 22,005 / 334, 3 calls | 18,338 / 253, 3 calls |

  - The checkpoints after commits hold one session plus `tasks/<child>/`, with the child's transcript, files, type and description.
  - The race that point 5 handles happened in one of the four runs. That build predated point 5, so its parent stayed open with its session total missing the turn, while the checkpoint was still exact. Point 5 is covered by the integration test above.

## Known limits and follow-ups

- **A paused parent can be woken again after its turn was ended for it.** When a subagent keeps calling tools after its last reply, agy sends the parent a "Subagent … has gone idle" notice once the subagent stops. That wake starts a new turn. Live (this branch): parent 28,738 / 136 over 4 calls, exact, split 3 + 1 across two turns. Waiting for the notice would avoid the split, but agy doesn't always send one, and then the parent would stay open.

- **Format coupling.** The link depends on two agy text formats, as described above; a change to either fails closed to today's behaviour.
- **Cache semantics are unverified.** No local agy session has reported a cache read, so whether `input_tokens` includes `cache_read_tokens` is unknown. Both are mapped across as they are.
- **Overlap with #2782.** #2782 adds a cumulative agy token source over the same transcript fields. The two should share one parser once both land.
- **A repeated Stop double counts on main.** For every agent, a repeated Stop on a turn that changed files counts the turn twice in the session total. Reproduced on main with Claude Code; separate PR.

## Summary

Write-side fixes for the token data behind `session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens`, and `tokens profile`. This PR makes the numbers written into checkpoints correct and complete; the report redesign follows in a separate PR off main. **One visible change:** `entire status`' per-session token total is now the session total again (see review fix 2 below) — everything else is metadata only.

Five commits, each independently reviewable:

### 1. `fix(tokens)`: Gemini and OpenCode parsers
- **Gemini** counted `cached` twice (it is a subset of `input`) and dropped `thoughts` (reported outside `output`). Real committed checkpoints were inflated 58–89%, with output understated 34–47%. Fresh input is now `input − cached + tool`; output is `output + thoughts`.
- **OpenCode** ignored `reasoning`, which is outside `output` in some versions and inside in others (7,456 vs 2,991 assistant messages in this repo's history). `Tokens.BilledOutput()` uses the per-message `total` identity to count it exactly once.
- Verified against every committed Gemini (19/19) and OpenCode (116/116) transcript on `entire/checkpoints/v1`: the four classes now sum to the provider's own total on all of them.

### 2. `fix(strategy)`: checkpoint `token_usage` gets its own window
`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart` to 0 after a partial commit (deliberately, for a self-contained transcript). Checkpoint tokens were computed from the same offset, so every post-carry-forward checkpoint re-reported the **whole session's** tokens: 53% of non-first checkpoints in this repo's history, 65% of all cache-read tokens ever recorded are re-counts, and anything summing `token_usage` was inflated 2–3×. `SessionState.TokenTranscriptStart` now scopes tokens; `advanceTranscriptWindows` moves both offsets at every condensation site; carry-forward resets only the transcript one. Legacy state files migrate on load.

### 3. `feat(tokens)`: persist what the agents already record
- `types.TokenUsage` gains `thinking_tokens` (⊂ `output_tokens`) and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` (⊂ `cache_creation_tokens`), both `omitempty`, **read verbatim from agent fields, never inferred** — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini for thinking; Claude Code and Pi for the 1-hour cache TTL (priced 2× vs 1.25×; sessions are usually all-one-or-the-other). Plus `model` on subagent entries so cost can be weighted per model.
- `AddTokenUsage` / `SubtractTokenUsage` / `accumulateTokenUsage` carry the new fields at every nesting level; Claude's subagent aggregation goes through `AddTokenUsage` instead of a field-by-field loop.
- Root `metadata.json` stamps `token_usage_version: 2` once no pre-delta row is left in the checkpoint (see review fix 3). Absent = legacy checkpoint whose `token_usage` may be a session-cumulative total.

### 4. `feat(checkpoint)`: persist `token_transcript_start`
Each session's `metadata.json` now records where its token window began. Without it a reader attributing a checkpoint's tokens from the stored `full.jsonl` had nothing to slice at — `checkpoint_transcript_start` is reset to 0 by carry-forward, so slicing there would re-create the cumulative bug. Written by `token_usage_version ≥ 2` CLIs, but presence is not a version marker: `omitempty` drops it at offset 0, so a session's first checkpoint omits it too; absent decodes as 0, which is the correct start in exactly those cases.
