## Summary

Agents that Claude Code's `Workflow` tool launches, and agents that skills with `context: fork` run in, left no trace in the checkpoint: no `tasks/` entry, no stored transcript, no subagent tokens. Entire's launch hooks (`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`) match only the `Agent` tool, so neither kind of agent got an in-flight record, and each of its `SubagentStop` events was skipped as "no live in-flight marker".

### Workflow agents

Claude Code fires `SubagentStart` for every workflow agent with `agent_id` and `agent_type: "workflow-subagent"`. This PR:

- installs Claude Code's `SubagentStart` hook with matcher `workflow-subagent`, so direct `Agent` launches never invoke it (the parser also ignores any other agent type);
- records a live task record per workflow agent, keyed by its `agent_id` (a Workflow call's `tool_use_id` is shared by all its agents); a repeated start cannot reset a record still in session state;
- lets the existing `SubagentStop` correlation by `agent_id` complete it from `agent_transcript_path` under `subagents/workflows/<run>/`;
- makes the transcript fallbacks (a commit while an agent is still running, the SessionEnd sweep) also look in the run directory, through one shared resolver in `paths` that replaces two duplicates;
- counts workflow agents in the session's `subagent_tokens`, for the runs the parent transcript launched (the launch's structured `toolUseResult.runId`, with the result's `Run ID: wf_…` text as a fallback), so `entire import` puts their tokens on the launching turn; an agent found in more than one run counts once, from its newest transcript;
- logs `agent_id`/`agent_type` when a `SubagentStop` is skipped.

### Forked skills

A skill with `context: fork` runs in an agent of its own. Claude Code names that agent only in the `Skill` call's result (`status: "forked"`, `agentId`, `background`); its `SubagentStart` reports an ordinary type such as `general-purpose`, so no `SubagentStart` matcher can single it out. This PR:

- installs `PostToolUse[Skill]` → the existing `post-task` command. A forked result records the launch under the Skill call's `tool_use_id` with the agent's ID, and the agent's `SubagentStop` completes it. Inline skills produce no event; the hook exits after a JSON parse for them;
- treats a missing `background` flag as still running; a fork reported finished (`background: false`) completes at once with files from its transcript only, since no `PreToolUse` baseline exists for a Skill call (otherwise every uncommitted worktree change would be credited to it);
- reads the agent from the parent transcript's structured `toolUseResult`, so its tokens count in the session's `subagent_tokens` and its edits in turn-end file attribution;
- logs a re-woken agent's repeated `SubagentStop` at debug instead of warn: a background agent stops again each time a child it launched wakes it (this also applies to background `Agent` subagents with background children).

Existing installs get the new hooks with `entire enable`; until then `entire status` and `entire doctor` report the Claude hook config as outdated.

Part of #2685 (and the forked-skill case of #2215): this PR gives each workflow agent and each forked skill's agent a task record and counts them in the session's subagent tokens. Each record's own `token_usage` is still undercounted (see below), which is being fixed in a separate PR; #2685 should close once both are in.

## Verified

- Live, Claude Code 2.1.291, binary from this branch: a Workflow running three parallel agents (each writing its own file) produced `tasks/<agent_id>/` ×3 with `task.json`, the agent transcript and the right file; `checkpoint explain --json` lists 3 tasks. Session `subagent_tokens` equals the summed `message.usage` of the three agent transcripts before and after the commit, with no double counting in a later checkpoint. A direct `Agent` subagent in the same session still gets exactly one `toolu_…`-keyed record, and Entire's `subagent-start` did not run for it. No warnings in `entire.log`.
- Same reproduction on `main`: no `tasks/`, `"tasks": []`, no `subagent_tokens`, three skipped `SubagentStop`s.
- Live, forked skill (binary from this branch): one session running an inline fan-out skill, a `context: fork` skill whose agent launches two background `Agent` subagents, and two `run_in_background` `Agent` calls produced 7 task records with the right files and no duplicates, including `tasks/<skill tool_use_id>/` for the forked agent (`task_description` `/fanout-fork`, full transcript). Session `subagent_tokens` went from 8 API calls on `main` to 12, now including the forked agent's own calls. On `main` the forked agent had no record.
- `mise run check` passes. New tests (hook install/upgrade/uninstall/health, parse filter, repeated start, resolver layout, token discovery and dedup, import turn split, forked-skill parse/launch modes, integration tests including a commit while an agent is still running and a finished fork beside unrelated worktree changes) fail on `main`.

## Not in this PR

- Per-task `token_usage` undercounts: it is computed at `SubagentStop`, before Claude Code has written the agent's final message to its transcript, so a task record misses its last API call(s) while the stored transcript has them (live: `task.json` 1 call, stored transcript 2). The same race exists on `main` for direct `Agent` subagents. Session `subagent_tokens` is computed later and is correct. Fix in a separate PR off `main` (recompute each task's tokens from the transcript stored at checkpoint time).
- A forked skill's agent stops once per wake; the first stop completes its record, so the record's `files` and `token_usage` stop there (live: 2 of 4 calls). The stored transcript is complete, the parent's next turn end still attributes later edits, and the per-task token PR recomputes tokens from it.
- Agents launched inside a forked skill get task records but are not in the session's `subagent_tokens` (their IDs are in the forked agent's transcript, not the parent's), the same limit as other nested subagents. To be handled with the token PR.
- A task record's `files` come from the agent's transcript, so files an agent changes through Bash (`echo >>`) are not listed on its record; they still appear in the session's `files_touched`. Same as direct `Agent` subagents.
- #2685 also reports a fourth, late `SubagentStop` for three agents; two live runs here produced exactly three. The skip log now includes `agent_id` and `agent_type`, so a repeat can be identified.
- Line attribution of subagent edits to the human: #2653.
- `session adopt` does not yet accept a workflow agent's transcript path.
- The web task view still needs checking with task ids that are agent ids rather than parent `tool_use_id`s.

Part of #2255. First of five stacked PRs that replace #2253.

Part of ENT-3643.

### Problem

Every reader of a saved commit scanned the whole message for `Entire-Checkpoint:`, so a line anywhere linked the commit: in the body, indented, pasted, or a teammate's trailer reused with `git commit -C`. Prepare-commit-msg took any such ID as its own stamp and added none, and post-commit then condensed the session's work into it. That created a checkpoint under a teammate's ID, or changed another commit's checkpoint.

### What changes

- **Only the last paragraph links a saved commit.** The `Entire-Checkpoint:` lines that start a line in the last non-subject paragraph count. Trailing blank and comment lines are skipped, and other lines in the paragraph are ignored. This is deliberately lenient; git's own trailer grammar comes in a later PR.
- **One resolver, `strategy.LinkedCheckpoints`, for code that writes into a checkpoint:** post-commit, attach and `explain --generate`.
  - It reads `core.commentChar`, `core.commentString` and `commit.cleanup` in one `git config` call, skipped when the message has no `Entire-Checkpoint` text.
  - Under `core.commentChar=auto` or a cleanup mode that keeps comment lines (`whitespace`, `verbatim`, `scissors`), it falls back to the whole-message scan, so no commit main links through a real trailer becomes unlinked.
  - Attach resolves once while planning and reuses the result.
- **Read-only views read without git config:** `explain <commit>`, `explain --commit`, the branch listing, `explain --checkpoint` search, export and the review re-run guard.
  - They read with `#` and show the last ID of the last paragraph, which is the one attach joins and `--generate` writes, or else the first ID anywhere.
  - For a squash commit they now show the checkpoint it stamped rather than the first inherited one.
- **Stamp record.**
  - Prepare records each ID it stamps in `entire-stamped-trailers.json` in the per-worktree git dir before writing the trailer: a generated one, a session's reservation, or one an amend restores. If it cannot record the ID, it writes no trailer.
  - An ID already in the draft counts as stamped only if the record holds it; otherwise prepare stamps a fresh trailer after it.
  - Post-commit consumes the record and condenses into the last stamped ID. Without one, it uses only the last ID whose checkpoint exists, for the session that owns it. It never creates a checkpoint prepare did not stamp.
- **Squash and redo inheritance** count only unindented trailers as already present. An editor squash, whose seeded message indents the squashed commits' trailers, now gets the inherited trailers in its last paragraph.
- **`explain --generate`** on a commit whose only ID is outside the last paragraph names that ID in its error.

Other read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, other history listings) still scan the whole message.

### Known gaps

- In the fallback configurations, a body mention can still steer attach and `explain --generate`, and show in `explain`. A later PR applies git's real comment and cleanup rules and removes the fallback.
- `git commit -C`, `-c` and `--amend` keep a reused trailer and stamp none, so reusing a foreign one leaves the commit unlinked. `entire attach` can link it.
- The lenient reader accepts some last paragraphs git would not read as trailers, as main did. A later PR applies git's trailer grammar.
- When two commits race in one worktree, the first post-commit consumes the stamp record, so the second commit's trailer can end up without a checkpoint. The inherited-trailers marker has the same window.

### Tests

Each test was written first and seen failing before its fix.

- Trailer reader unit tests, resolver tests across git configurations, and stamp record and target selection unit tests.
- Attach and explain tests: body mentions do not select a checkpoint, and the listing and `--checkpoint` search agree with `explain <commit>`.
- Integration tests through the real hook binaries:
  - a body line naming an unknown checkpoint, and one naming an existing checkpoint;
  - an indented line;
  - an agent commit with a body line;
  - `git commit -C` of a commit naming an unfetched checkpoint;
  - a trailer replaced in the editor;
  - a last paragraph naming an unknown then an existing checkpoint.
- `TestTrailerAuthority_RealGitCommits` runs real `git commit` for `-m`, `-F`, editor, `--amend`, `--amend --no-edit`, `;` comments, `commit.cleanup` whitespace / verbatim / scissors, `core.commentChar=auto`, and `-F` of a message naming a foreign checkpoint. It asserts the commit stays linked and no foreign checkpoint is created.
- Post-commit fixtures that hand-write a trailer now record the stamp prepare would, or they return before the logic they pin.

An agent can use a custom storage path, and a user can run several instances with different paths—for example, separate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` values. Entire currently resolves storage from the invoking process’s environment. When that environment differs from the source session’s, `session adopt` can reject a valid transcript and `attach` can fail to find it.

Record the agent home alongside each session and remember independently resolved homes in a bounded per-user registry. Adoption validates the recorded home against locally trusted roots; `attach` searches previously used homes after the active store misses. This lets users continue sessions across repositories and find transcripts from another agent instance without recreating its environment.

Carry that root through capture, checkpoint finalization, review, token accounting, and subagent reads. Shared rooted readers enforce containment when opening files, including after adoption, so stored paths and later symlink changes cannot redirect reads outside the authorized home. Preserve compatibility with older sessions and explicit session-directory overrides.

Alternatives considered:

- Require users to export the original storage variables for every command. This leaves ordinary shell workflows dependent on the source agent’s environment.
- Trust the transcript path or home recorded in session metadata. Repository-controlled metadata cannot authorize filesystem access.
- Implement confinement separately in each agent. A shared contract keeps the same protections across agents and transcript consumers.

## Why

The hidden `entire checkpoint policy` command wrote a client-side ref, `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint`, and pushed it to the checkpoint sync remote. That namespace is reserved on the Entire side for server-managed policy data, and Entire's git mirroring rejects a push that carries a client-written ref under it. One rejected ref fails the whole push, so a repository whose upstream carried the policy ref could no longer be mirrored at all: every sync failed and retried, and none of its branches or tags landed until the ref was removed.

The policy never earned that cost. The CLI was the only writer of the ref, so every hook, condensation pass, and explicit checkpoint writer was reading a ref that only ever held the default policy, and the feature carried its own package, telemetry event, and a dedicated repository-open fallback. Removing the feature removes the writer.

## What changed

The checkpoint policy feature is removed end to end: the `checkpointpolicy` package, the hidden `entire checkpoint policy` command, the post-run upgrade warning, the `checkpoint_policy_blocked` telemetry event, and every gate that read the ref (git hooks, agent hooks, condensation, the Stop finalize pass, all three pre-push paths, and the `attach` / `import` / `explain --generate` write guards). `gitrepo.OpenCurrentOrCwd` goes with it, since the warning was its only caller, as does `versioncheck.UpdateCommandShell`, whose only two callers were the policy command and the policy warning. Net change is 136 insertions against 4034 deletions across 63 files.

The branch is split into self-contained commits, each compiling on its own, in dependency order: agent hooks, git hooks plus telemetry, the strategy, the checkpoint writers, the command and warning, the package itself with its docs, and then the seams the removal left — stale references (lint config, complexity feature map, test plan), the dead `UpdateCommandShell` API, the agent-help classification, and two things the removal exposed rather than caused (see below).

## Decisions made during development

- **`checkpoint explain` is classified task-driven, and the checkpoint group stays task-driven.** `policy` was the group's only task-driven child, so deleting it left `agentHelpAudienceNote` rendering the group's own audience over four read-only children — a listing that said "task-driven" above a drill-down that said "read-only" four times. Classifying `explain` is the fail-safe way to answer that: `--generate` writes a summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider, the audience axis has no flag granularity, and this table's stated direction is an agent declining to run something it could have rather than running something it should not have. The group therefore renders `read-only except: explain` — the same shape it had before, with a different command named. **This is a product judgment call and a reviewer should feel free to move it.**
- **What that classification costs is repaid on the agent channel, not hidden.** Demoting `explain` tells an agent to avoid the drill-down that `checkpoint list` and `checkpoint search` exist to feed, over a flag it was never going to pass. `agentHelpGuidance` now carries the distinction for agents ("reading is free; `--generate` is the exception"), and `explain`'s cobra `Long` carries the half a human wants too — which is where CLAUDE.md says each kind of text belongs.
- **A group whose audience contradicts its children now fails the build.** `agentHelpAudienceNote` falls back to the group's own audience whenever its classified children agree *with each other*, which its comment described as their agreeing with the *group*. Those are not the same thing, and the gap is exactly how the checkpoint group came to need a decision at all. The fallback itself is correct — the group's audience also covers hidden children the note never counts, and `checkpoint resume` switches branches — so `TestAgentHelpClassification_GroupAudienceMatchesUnanimousChildren` catches the disagreement instead and leaves the call to a human. Verified non-vacuous: flipping `explain` back to read-only fails it by name.
- **The v1 pre-push opens the repository only when OPF needs it, in its own span.** The repository handle was shared between the policy sync and the OPF rewrite; with the sync gone, the open moves inside the `OPFRun` branch so the common no-OPF path no longer opens the repo at all. It gets its own `open_repository` span rather than sitting inside `opf_pre_push_rewrite`, so that span keeps measuring what it measured in every trace recorded before — the open is not free on a reftable repo, where `gitrepo` routes reference reads back through the git CLI.
- **`OpenCurrentOrCwd` is deleted rather than kept for future use.** Its doc comment and the CLAUDE.md guidance both said the cwd fallback was acceptable only for a read-only advisory; no such caller remains, and keeping a footgun with no user contradicts the "OpenCurrent fails rather than guessing" rule.
- **The refs-migration doc now names what the removal makes silent.** `checkpoint_min_version` was the mechanism that turned "an old CLI cannot read refs checkpoints" into an explicit upgrade nudge, and `ref-checkpoint-backend.md` still justified skipping a dual-write on the grounds that the case "is a feature, not something to paper over". With the nudge gone it is a silent feature — an old CLI sees a partial history and is told nothing — so the doc says that rather than arguing from a mechanism that no longer exists.
- **Existing checkpoint refs on remotes are untouched.** Nothing deletes `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` where it already exists; the CLI simply stops reading or advancing it.

## Reviewer notes

- No repository is known to carry a non-default policy ref, and no CLI command clears one any more. If one turns up, `git update-ref -d refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` locally plus `git push <remote> :refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` removes it, and deleting it from the upstream is what restores mirroring for a repository that hit the sync failure above.
- The CHANGELOG entries that introduced the feature (#1508, #1509) are left as historical record; no changelog entry is added here, because the command was hidden and experimental and nothing depended on it.
- `TestExecuteAgentHookPostTodoFailsWhenPolicyUnsupported` was the only unit test driving `executeAgentHook` with `HookNamePostTodo`, and this branch rewrites that dispatch condition. It is deleted rather than adapted: without the policy assertion there is nothing left to assert, since a bare "returns no error" would pass even if the condition broke. Restoring real coverage means observing the PostTodo side effect, which is a separate piece of work; the integration suite covers the path today.

A native Git checkpoint writer and an OPF rewrite could both read the same ref value and then both report a successful update. The OPF paths used go-git's compare-and-swap, which does not participate in native Git's reference-locking protocol. A native transaction could therefore commit after the OPF rewrite and silently discard it.

## The fix

Introduce `gitrepo.CompareAndSwapRef`, a shared direct-ref compare-and-swap built on a native `git update-ref --stdin` transaction. The transaction prepares the update first, acquiring Git's ref lock, verifies that the ref is not symbolic while that lock is held, and then commits.

The native helper now backs:

- shadow-branch updates
- all persistent-ref writers using `updatePersistentRef`, including the Stop hook
- both OPF rewrite paths: the shared v1 ref and per-checkpoint refs

The OPF scan remains outside the ref transaction. Its final CAS uses the value observed before the scan, so a concurrent update is rejected instead of overwritten.

`CASPersistentRef` deliberately does not acquire Entire's persistent-writer flock. Its expected value predates the call, and native Git is the correctness boundary. Avoiding the flock also prevents deadline-free pre-push operations from waiting indefinitely. Transient native lock contention is retried with a bounded budget; a genuine stale-value conflict is terminal.

## Transaction and failure behavior

The separate `git symbolic-ref` invocation is deliberate. Git does not allow `symref-verify` and an update of the same ref in one transaction because it treats them as multiple updates to that ref. Preparing the native update first keeps the ref locked while the symbolic-ref probe runs, closing the conversion race.

CAS error classification recognizes only Git's exact stale-value diagnostics. Corrupt refs, unreadable refs, namespace conflicts, and other permanent failures retain their underlying diagnosis rather than being mislabeled and retried. The v1 rewrite reports `V1RefMovedError` only after a successful reread confirms that the ref actually changed.

Cancellation closes the transaction's stdin so Git can abort cleanly. A three-second `WaitDelay` bounds shutdown if a hook or inherited pipe prevents the process from exiting.

## Performance

Routing the shared write path through the transaction increases a measured ref update from 13.4 ms to 22.0 ms—an 8.6 ms cost per update. That is under 1% of the roughly 3-second p50 Stop-hook latency.

The extra symbolic-ref process is required for the direct-ref guarantee described above; it is not an accidental round trip.

## Verification

Regression tests use real native Git transactions and cover both files and reftable repositories. They exercise:

- both OPF lost-update races
- symbolic-ref rejection and concurrent symbolic conversion
- native lock contention and bounded retry behavior
- cancellation and lock release
- malformed, corrupt, unreadable, and namespace-conflicting refs
- preservation of the original failure when a v1 ref cannot be reread

The focused race tests passed ten consecutive runs.

`mise run check` passed after the review fixes, including formatting, lint, race-enabled unit and integration tests, and the Vogon and Roger-Roger canary suites.

Follow-up to #2727 and #2731. The `strategy` package had never run on Windows in CI (`test-windows` only selected tests named `*Windows*`/`*MSYS*`). On a `windows-latest` runner it failed 542 tests and timed out at 20 minutes. This makes it pass and adds it to `test-windows`.

## One real bug

`entire enable` refused a `core.hooksPath` whose parent directory did not exist yet, such as Husky's `.husky/_` before `.husky` exists. The guard treated stat's `ENOTDIR` as "a path component is a file", but on Windows `syscall.ENOTDIR` is `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`, which a plain missing parent also returns. It now walks up to the nearest existing ancestor and refuses only if that is a non-directory, which gives the same answer on every platform.

That walk-up alone would have broken the "disable hooks globally" setting `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on Windows. `filepath.IsAbs("/dev/null")` is false there, so `getHooksDirInPath` joined it onto the repository as `<repo>\dev\null`. The old check refused that only by accident (its missing parent also returned `ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND`). With the walk-up, it was created and hooks were installed. A Windows runner confirmed this before the fix. Rooted paths are no longer joined onto the repository, the guard refuses `/dev/null` and anything beneath it by name, and the `/dev/null` tests now use the literal value on Windows too.

## Temp-directory locks (502 of the 542)

`osroot.Shared` keeps every root it opens for the life of the process, and Windows cannot delete a directory with an open handle, so `t.TempDir` cleanup failed. The leaked handles were also why the package was so slow: about 6 minutes once they are released, against more than 20 before.

- `osroot.ForgetUnder(dir)` closes the cached roots at or beneath one directory, under its given and its resolved spelling. Unlike `ResetShared` it leaves other tests' roots alone, so it is safe with `t.Parallel`.
- `testutil.InitRepo` registers it at cleanup, which covers most tests without touching them. `testutil.TempDir(t)` covers directories made another way (clones, linked worktrees, bare hooks or `.entire` dirs). It is used only at the 31 call sites where an instrumented run showed a root actually being released.

## Test portability

- Transcript fixtures spliced Windows paths into JSON unescaped, so the paths never parsed. They now go through `jsonQuote`.
- Session fixtures recorded worktrees as `C:\...`, but production records git's `C:/...` and matches by exact string. The fixture now uses production's spelling.
- The global git-author test now sets `USERPROFILE` as well as `HOME`.
- Tests that need Unix permission bits, a shell-script fake agent, `proclive` process introspection, or an `ENOTDIR` distinct from a missing parent now skip on Windows, like the existing skips. The last one is a real behavior difference: on Windows a transcript path whose parent is a file reads as absent, so that session counts as having no content.

## Not changed

`paths.WorktreeRoot` still returns git's forward-slash spelling on Windows. Every production writer of `SessionState.WorktreePath` uses it, so matching is consistent. Normalizing it would split in-flight session state files between two spellings.

Rebuilt on top of the shadow-branch removal (now on main). The earlier version of this PR moved sessions between worktrees on top of shadow branches; that no longer applies. This version records a session's edits against the worktree they happened in, so a commit in any worktree links the session's work there.

## Problem

A session has one home worktree: where its first hook ran. An agent launched there fires every hook there, even when it edits another worktree of the repository by absolute path, or is resumed in one. Without shadow branches visible from every worktree:

- edits in another worktree fell outside the hook's tree at turn end and were dropped, so the session recorded nothing and a later commit of those files there didn't link;
- a turn ending in another worktree marked the home's uncommitted untracked files as deleted, and moved the session's base and branch to that tree;
- the stored transcript and prompts were written to whichever worktree the hook ran in, splitting them, and readers in other worktrees missed them.

## Change

**Edits are recorded per worktree.** The home keeps its existing fields (`files_touched`, `touched_file_hashes`). Edits the transcript places in another registered worktree go into `other_worktrees[<worktree id>]` (files, hashes, path), hashed in that worktree. Only transcript-named paths count there, so other people's uncommitted changes in that worktree are never claimed. Entries are keyed by worktree ID (they survive `git worktree move`) and pruned when the worktree is removed. A subagent's edits don't create entries (main transcript only).

**A commit in worktree X matches and clears only X's record.** Prepare-commit-msg and post-commit read X's record in place of the home's: overlap and content checks, the checkpoint's `files_touched`, and clearing. A session with a record for X takes part in linking there, but must overlap X's files. The no-TTY fast path now requires that too, unless the session is identified as the committer by process ancestry or caller-session env, so an agent's own mid-turn commit still links and an unrelated process's commit doesn't. When work stays pending in another worktree, the commit carries the rest forward (as split commits do today), and the stored copy is released only when nothing is pending anywhere. Pending work, the stale sweep, doctor, session end and adopt count every worktree.

**The stored copy lives in the home worktree.** Turn-start and turn-end writes go through `OpenSessionEntireDir`; every reader goes through `storedSessionRoot`, under the existing registered-worktree gate.

**A turn ending outside the home records only its own work** there: no deletions of the home's files, no base or branch moves.

Reproduced with the real binary and installed git hooks (agent launched in the main checkout, editing a linked worktree by absolute path; "someone else" commits from a process outside the agent's tree):

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| A: agent edits the worktree; later the user commits it there | not linked | linked, `files_touched=[a.txt]` |
| D: work pending at home + worktree edit, each committed in its own tree | worktree commit not linked | both linked, each with only its own file |
| C: back at home | linked | linked |
| F: session ACTIVE with a worktree record; an unrelated process commits there (no TTY) | linked (wrong) | not linked |
| G: the agent's own mid-turn shell edit in the worktree, committed by it | linked | linked, `files_touched=[g.txt]` |
| H: session ended with only a worktree record; later commit there | not linked | linked |
| I: worktree moved before the commit | not linked | linked |

## Known limits

- Files written in another worktree only through shell commands aren't in the transcript, so they aren't recorded there (an agent's own commit of them still links by ancestry). Edits recorded mid-turn (PostToolUse) and subagent task files still go to the home record.
- When commits in two worktrees split a session's work, the second checkpoint shows the whole conversation (as split commits do); tokens are counted once via `token_transcript_start`.
- An older CLI that rewrites the session state drops `other_worktrees`.
- Removing the home worktree deletes its `.entire`, so an uncommitted stored copy is lost.
- `entire status` and the commit preview don't list other worktrees' files yet.

## Tests

Strategy, session and integration tests for: recording per worktree at turn end (including both trees in one turn, symlinked paths, pruning, adopt), linking and the fast path requiring X's files, carry-forward with work pending elsewhere, the stored copy in the home, guest turns, the transcript fallback ignoring already-checkpointed edits, and a commit in X whose record doesn't overlap falling back to the committed files. Each behavioral test fails with its change reverted; `mise run check` passes.

## Summary

Agent turns no longer write anything to git. Older versions committed a full working-tree snapshot to a per-worktree shadow branch (`entire/<commit>-<worktree>`) at every turn end. That was the source of runaway local storage, and cleaning those branches up at the wrong moment made uncondensed work unreachable. Turn ends now record pending work in session state only: the step count, the files the agent touched, and each touched file's git blob hash. A checkpoint is written only when you commit.

Line attribution is removed entirely, including the AI/Human/Mixed labels in `entire blame`, which now reports whether each line's commit is linked to a checkpoint. Checkpoint metadata no longer carries `initial_attribution` or `combined_attribution`; entire.io derives the experts counts from those and must be told they stop arriving.

Commits link to a session by file name: any committed path the session touched links it, except a new file at a path the agent deleted. Carry-forward after a partial commit compares the recorded hashes with the commit and the worktree, so a `git add -p` remainder, a pending deletion, or a session upgraded from the old state format keeps its uncommitted work. Gitignored files, submodule pointers, and paths inside a submodule or beneath a symlinked directory never enter the tracked files, so they can no longer keep a session pending forever; edits inside a submodule belong to the nested repository's own session. Whether a committed file still has uncommitted agent changes is asked of `git status`, so repositories with `text=auto` or `core.autocrlf` no longer keep fully committed files pending.

Lifecycle decisions (condensation, the zombie sweep, orphan cleanup, doctor) key on one predicate over session state instead of whether a shadow ref exists. Pending step rows, explain of temporary checkpoints, incremental task checkpoints and the Claude Code post-todo hook install are gone. `checkpoint list --pending` now previews what the next commit's checkpoint will contain.

Claude Code gains a transcript prompt extractor, so its prompts no longer depend on `prompt.txt` alone.

Addresses #2663, #2378, #2350, #1730, #1807 and #2653. Supersedes trail 1486 (`soph/fix-shadow-after-midturn-commit`), which patches code this PR deletes.

## Migrations

Turn ends no longer write shadow branches (entire/<commit>-<worktree>): pending work is tracked in session state and checkpoints are written only when you commit. Branches left by older versions are not removed automatically. `entire doctor` and `entire status` report them, and `entire doctor --force` or `entire disable --uninstall` deletes the `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` form without touching session state. The oldest bare `entire/<commit>` form is only ever listed, since a branch of your own named after a short SHA looks the same; `entire clean --all` removes it behind a confirmation. Do not use plain `entire clean` for this: it also clears pending session state. They hold full snapshots of your working tree, so run it once after upgrading. Deleting the branches frees no space by itself: a later `git gc` reclaims it once their objects are two weeks old. `git gc --prune=now` frees it immediately, but it drops every unreachable object in the repository (recently dropped stashes included) and must only run when no other git process is active.

`entire blame --json` reports a per-line `status` (`checkpoint`, `commit`, `uncommitted`) instead of `authorship` and `tag`. Its summary reports checkpoint-linked, commit and uncommitted line counts instead of AI/Human/Mixed counts.

New checkpoints no longer include `initial_attribution`, `combined_attribution` or `prompt_attributions`; checkpoints written by older versions keep theirs, and rewrites (explain `--generate`, attach) carry them through unchanged. Session state files written by older versions still load; their attribution and `last_checkpoint_commit_hash` keys are dropped on the next save.

The Claude Code post-todo hook is no longer installed, and any `entire enable` prunes it and says so. Its subcommand stays so older hook configs keep working. An older CLI run against the same tracked `.claude/settings.json` reports the hooks as out of date and re-adds it; this CLI removes it again on the next `entire enable`.

Commit pending agent work before downgrading to a previous release: the previous CLI deletes ended but uncondensed session state when its shadow branch is missing, and this release never writes one.

`entire session info --json` and `entire session current --json` report the number of turns not yet condensed into a checkpoint as `pending_turns`. The old `checkpoints` field is still emitted with the same value for this release only and will be removed in the next one; switch scripts to `pen…51763 tokens truncated…s the one attach joins and `--generate` writes, or else the first ID anywhere.
  - For a squash commit they now show the checkpoint it stamped rather than the first inherited one.
- **Stamp record.**
  - Prepare records each ID it stamps in `entire-stamped-trailers.json` in the per-worktree git dir before writing the trailer: a generated one, a session's reservation, or one an amend restores. If it cannot record the ID, it writes no trailer.
  - An ID already in the draft counts as stamped only if the record holds it; otherwise prepare stamps a fresh trailer after it.
  - Post-commit consumes the record and condenses into the last stamped ID. Without one, it uses only the last ID whose checkpoint exists, for the session that owns it. It never creates a checkpoint prepare did not stamp.
- **Squash and redo inheritance** count only unindented trailers as already present. An editor squash, whose seeded message indents the squashed commits' trailers, now gets the inherited trailers in its last paragraph.
- **`explain --generate`** on a commit whose only ID is outside the last paragraph names that ID in its error.

Other read-only lookups (resume, status, attribution, other history listings) still scan the whole message.

### Known gaps

- In the fallback configurations, a body mention can still steer attach and `explain --generate`, and show in `explain`. A later PR applies git's real comment and cleanup rules and removes the fallback.
- `git commit -C`, `-c` and `--amend` keep a reused trailer and stamp none, so reusing a foreign one leaves the commit unlinked. `entire attach` can link it.
- The lenient reader accepts some last paragraphs git would not read as trailers, as main did. A later PR applies git's trailer grammar.
- When two commits race in one worktree, the first post-commit consumes the stamp record, so the second commit's trailer can end up without a checkpoint. The inherited-trailers marker has the same window.

### Tests

Each test was written first and seen failing before its fix.

- Trailer reader unit tests, resolver tests across git configurations, and stamp record and target selection unit tests.
- Attach and explain tests: body mentions do not select a checkpoint, and the listing and `--checkpoint` search agree with `explain <commit>`.
- Integration tests through the real hook binaries:
  - a body line naming an unknown checkpoint, and one naming an existing checkpoint;

"},{"n":2636,"title":"Support multiple agent homes across session workflows","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1462
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

An agent can use a custom storage path, and a user can run several instances with different paths—for example, separate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `CODEX_HOME` values. Entire currently resolves storage from the invoking process’s environment. When that environment differs from the source session’s, `session adopt` can reject a valid transcript and `attach` can fail to find it.

Record the agent home alongside each session and remember independently resolved homes in a bounded per-user registry. Adoption validates the recorded home against locally trusted roots; `attach` searches previously used homes after the active store misses. This lets users continue sessions across repositories and find transcripts from another agent instance without recreating its environment.

Carry that root through capture, checkpoint finalization, review, token accounting, and subagent reads. Shared rooted readers enforce containment when opening files, including after adoption, so stored paths and later symlink changes cannot redirect reads outside the authorized home. Preserve compatibility with older sessions and explicit session-directory overrides.

Alternatives considered:

- Require users to export the original storage variables for every command. This leaves ordinary shell workflows dependent on the source agent’s environment.
- Trust the transcript path or home recorded in session metadata. Repository-controlled metadata cannot authorize filesystem access.
- Implement confinement separately in each agent. A shared contract keeps the same protections across agents and transcript consumers.
"},{"n":2508,"title":"Remove the checkpoint policy feature","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1355
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Why

The hidden `entire checkpoint policy` command wrote a client-side ref, `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint`, and pushed it to the checkpoint sync remote. That namespace is reserved on the Entire side for server-managed policy data, and Entire's git mirroring rejects a push that carries a client-written ref under it. One rejected ref fails the whole push, so a repository whose upstream carried the policy ref could no longer be mirrored at all: every sync failed and retried, and none of its branches or tags landed until the ref was removed.

The policy never earned that cost. The CLI was the only writer of the ref, so every hook, condensation pass, and explicit checkpoint writer was reading a ref that only ever held the default policy, and the feature carried its own package, telemetry event, and a dedicated repository-open fallback. Removing the feature removes the writer.

## What changed

The checkpoint policy feature is removed end to end: the `checkpointpolicy` package, the hidden `entire checkpoint policy` command, the post-run upgrade warning, the `checkpoint_policy_blocked` telemetry event, and every gate that read the ref (git hooks, agent hooks, condensation, the Stop finalize pass, all three pre-push paths, and the `attach` / `import` / `explain --generate` write guards). `gitrepo.OpenCurrentOrCwd` goes with it, since the warning was its only caller, as does `versioncheck.UpdateCommandShell`, whose only two callers were the policy command and the policy warning. Net change is 136 insertions against 4034 deletions across 63 files.

The branch is split into self-contained commits, each compiling on its own, in dependency order: agent hooks, git hooks plus telemetry, the strategy, the checkpoint writers, the command and warning, the package itself with its docs, and then the seams the removal left — stale references (lint config, complexity feature map, test plan), the dead `UpdateCommandShell` API, the agent-help classification, and two things the removal exposed rather than caused (see below).

## Decisions made during development

- **`checkpoint explain` is classified task-driven, and the checkpoint group stays task-driven.** `policy` was the group's only task-driven child, so deleting it left `agentHelpAudienceNote` rendering the group's own audience over four read-only children — a listing that said "task-driven" above a drill-down that said "read-only" four times. Classifying `explain` is the fail-safe way to answer that: `--generate` writes a summary onto the checkpoint and spends tokens with the summary provider, the audience axis has no flag granularity, and this table's stated direction is an agent declining to run something it could have rather than running something it should not have. The group therefore renders `read-only except: explain` — the same shape it had before, with a different command named. **This is a product judgment call and a reviewer should feel free to move it.**
- **What that classification costs is repaid on the agent channel, not hidden.** Demoting `explain` tells an agent to avoid the drill-down that `checkpoint list` and `checkpoint search` exist to feed, over a flag it was never going to pass. `agentHelpGuidance` now carries the distinction for agents ("reading is free; `--generate` is the exception"), and `explain`'s cobra `Long` carries the half a human wants too — which is where CLAUDE.md says each kind of text belongs.
- **A group whose audience contradicts its children now fails the build.** `agentHelpAudienceNote` falls back to the group's own audience whenever its classified children agree *with each other*, which its comment described as their agreeing with the *group*. Those are not the same thing, and the gap is exactly how the checkpoint group came to need a decision at all. The fallback itself is correct — the group's audience also covers hidden children the note never counts, and `checkpoint resume` switches branches — so `TestAgentHelpClassification_GroupAudienceMatchesUnanimousChildren` catches the disagreement instead and leaves the call to a human. Verified non-vacuous: flipping `explain` back to read-only fails it by name.
- **The v1 pre-push opens the repository only when OPF needs it, in its own span.** The repository handle was shared between the policy sync and the OPF rewrite; with the sync gone, the open moves inside the `OPFRun` branch so the common no-OPF path no longer opens the repo at all. It gets its own `open_repository` span rather than sitting inside `opf_pre_push_rewrite`, so that span keeps measuring what it measured in every trace recorded before — the open is not free on a reftable repo, where `gitrepo` routes reference reads back through the git CLI.
- **`OpenCurrentOrCwd` is deleted rather than kept for future use.** Its doc comment and the CLAUDE.md guidance both said the cwd fallback was acceptable only for a read-only advisory; no such caller remains, and keeping a footgun with no user contradicts the "OpenCurrent fails rather than guessing" rule.
- **The refs-migration doc now names what the removal makes silent.** `checkpoint_min_version` was the mechanism that turned "an old CLI cannot read refs checkpoints" into an explicit upgrade nudge, and `ref-checkpoint-backend.md` still justified skipping a dual-write on the grounds that the case "is a feature, not something to paper over". With the nudge gone it is a silent feature — an old CLI sees a partial history and is told nothing — so the doc says that rather than arguing from a mechanism that no longer exists.
- **Existing checkpoint refs on remotes are untouched.** Nothing deletes `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` where it already exists; the CLI simply stops reading or advancing it.

## Reviewer notes

- No repository is known to carry a non-default policy ref, and no CLI command clears one any more. If one turns up, `git update-ref -d refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` locally plus `git push <remote> :refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` removes it, and deleting it from the upstream is what restores mirroring for a repository that hit the sync failure above.
- The CHANGELOG entries that introduced the feature (#1508, #1509) are left as historical record; no changelog entry is added here, because the command was hidden and experimental and nothing depended on it.
- `TestExecuteAgentHookPostTodoFailsWhenPolicyUnsupported` was the only unit test driving `executeAgentHook` with `HookNamePostTodo`, and this branch rewrites that dispatch condition. It is deleted rather than adapted: without the policy assertion there is nothing left to assert, since a bare "returns no error" would pass even if the condition broke. Restoring real coverage means observing the PostTodo side effect, which is a separate piece of work; the integration suite covers the path today.
- Merging main brought two conflicts, both resolved in `852757b5c4` with the reasoning in its message. `checkpointpolicy/remote.go` was a modify/delete — `7693ebb5ca` fixed `checkpointpolicy.Push`'s error formatting, entirely inside the package this branch deletes, so the deletion stands and nothing needs porting. `CLAUDE.md` was the larger one: `d16dce053f` slimmed it from 2143 lines to 199 and moved the detail into `docs/development/`, so this branch's three CLAUDE.md edits are re-applied at their new homes (`cli-conventions.md`, `git-safety.md`, `checkpoint-implementation.md`) rather than lost by taking main's file wholesale.
- Two integration tests in `external_command_signal_unix_test.go` failed once under `-race` during the full suite with "plugin never reached ready state", then passed in isolation and on a full rerun of the package. They are unrelated to this change.

"},{"n":2211,"title":"fix(checkpoint): serialize OPF ref updates","body":"Fixes #2204

A native Git checkpoint writer and an OPF rewrite could both read the same ref value and then both report a successful update. The OPF paths used go-git's compare-and-swap, which does not participate in native Git's reference-locking protocol. A native transaction could therefore commit after the OPF rewrite and silently discard it.

## The fix

Introduce `gitrepo.CompareAndSwapRef`, a shared direct-ref compare-and-swap built on a native `git update-ref --stdin` transaction. The transaction prepares the update first, acquiring Git's ref lock, verifies that the ref is not symbolic while that lock is held, and then commits.

The native helper now backs:

- shadow-branch updates
- all persistent-ref writers using `updatePersistentRef`, including the Stop hook
- both OPF rewrite paths: the shared v1 ref and per-checkpoint refs

The OPF scan remains outside the ref transaction. Its final CAS uses the value observed before the scan, so a concurrent update is rejected instead of overwritten.

`CASPersistentRef` deliberately does not acquire Entire's persistent-writer flock. Its expected value predates the call, and native Git is the correctness boundary. Avoiding the flock also prevents deadline-free pre-push operations from waiting indefinitely. Transient native lock contention is retried with a bounded budget; a genuine stale-value conflict is terminal.

## Transaction and failure behavior

The separate `git symbolic-ref` invocation is deliberate. Git does not allow `symref-verify` and an update of the same ref in one transaction because it treats them as multiple updates to that ref. Preparing the native update first keeps the ref locked while the symbolic-ref probe runs, closing the conversion race.

CAS error classification recognizes only Git's exact stale-value diagnostics. Corrupt refs, unreadable refs, namespace conflicts, and other permanent failures retain their underlying diagnosis rather than being mislabeled and retried. The v1 rewrite reports `V1RefMovedError` only after a successful reread confirms that the ref actually changed.

Cancellation closes the transaction's stdin so Git can abort cleanly. A three-second `WaitDelay` bounds shutdown if a hook or inherited pipe prevents the process from exiting.

## Performance

Routing the shared write path through the transaction increases a measured ref update from 13.4 ms to 22.0 ms—an 8.6 ms cost per update. That is under 1% of the roughly 3-second p50 Stop-hook latency.

The extra symbolic-ref process is required for the direct-ref guarantee described above; it is not an accidental round trip.

## Verification

Regression tests use real native Git transactions and cover both files and reftable repositories. They exercise:

- both OPF lost-update races
- symbolic-ref rejection and concurrent symbolic conversion
- native lock contention and bounded retry behavior
- cancellation and lock release
- malformed, corrupt, unreadable, and namespace-conflicting refs
- preservation of the original failure when a v1 ref cannot be reread

The focused race tests passed ten consecutive runs.

`mise run check` passed after the review fixes, including formatting, lint, race-enabled unit and integration tests, and the Vogon and Roger-Roger canary suites.
"},{"n":2232,"title":"fix: serialize session-state clear against concurrent MutateSessionState","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1214
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary
- `clearSessionState` (and its exported wrapper `ClearSessionState`, used by `entire doctor`) deleted a session's state file with no lock at all, while every other mutation of the same file goes through `MutateSessionState`'s per-session gate.
- A concurrent, properly-locked write (e.g. a PostToolUse hook for the same session) landing in the gap between a caller's "safe to clear" decision and the actual delete was silently destroyed — the file the write just produced gets deleted out from under it, with nothing surfacing the loss.
- `initializeSession` documents and fixes the identical hazard class elsewhere in this file ("take the gate, then re-check under lock"); this closes the same gap for the clear path.
- `clearSessionState` now acquires `sessionID`'s gate before clearing.
- `CondenseSessionByID`'s `clearAfter` path — the concrete, routine-traffic instance of this race (no shadow branch, condensation decides to clear state only) — now clears via a new `clearSessionStateLocked` helper from inside its own already-locked mutation closure, so the decision and the delete are atomic with respect to other writers rather than racing across an unlocked gap.
- `Reset`/`ResetSession`/doctor's `ClearSessionState` all call the same hardened `clearSessionState`, so they're covered with no additional changes.

## Verification
- Real-goroutine concurrency reproduction (`TestClearSessionState_SerializesAgainstConcurrentMutation`): a writer holds the real gate via `MutateSessionState` and blocks mid-mutation; `clearSessionState` must block until it releases, not run concurrently.
- **Mutation-verified**: temporarily reverted `clearSessionState` to skip gate acquisition (matching the exact pre-fix code path), confirmed the test genuinely fails (clear returns immediately while the writer is still mid-flight), then restored the fix and confirmed the full `strategy` package test suite passes with no regressions.
- `go build` passes. Full `mise run check` deferred to a follow-up pass to keep local CI load down.

## Test plan
- [x] New concurrency reproduction test added and passing
- [x] Verified test fails without the fix (mutation check)
- [x] Full `strategy` package test suite green, no regressions
- [ ] Full `mise run check` (deferred, will run before merge)"}]}

### Rehome keeps stale attribution snapshots **Medium Severity** `rehomeSessionAfterOwnCommit` moves `BaseCommit` and realigns the attribution base after a guest condensation, but leaves `PendingPromptAttribution` and `PromptAttributions` in place. Turn-start always records that snapshot against the old home, and guest condensation already includes it when attributing the commit. The home condensation path clears both fields after a base move because those values have been consumed; without the same reset, the next SaveStep or condensation on the new home reapplies old-home user-line counts.
Additional Locations (1) - [`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L1615-L1619`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/deeab2b71b413332e1f8a72ab01b63f0f704fabb/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L1615-L1619)

cd /Users/puneetpalsingh/Documents/Code/dev/Shadowbox/shadowbox-039-run-admission-truth && gh pr edit 391 --body $'## Objective

Implement LLD 039.6: durable, canonical Brain run admission that distinguishes blocked capacity from provider failures.

## Architecture decision

- The Run Admission Durable Object is the single persisted owner of rate counters and concurrency leases.
- Admission policy requires canonical user, workspace, thread, and run-attempt identities; no client-fingerprint fallback remains.
- The exact run-attempt owns its idempotent lease. `RUN_ADMISSION_BLOCKED` carries typed admission metadata rather than provider semantics.
- Policy, transport, and orchestration are focused runtime collaborators.

## Changed / deleted paths

Changed: controller integration, `RunAdmissionLimiter`, admission policy/client/service collaborators, focused runtime tests, and policy inventory.

Deleted: legacy service-layer admission implementation/tests and fingerprint scope helper/tests.

## Review repair

Added direct Durable Object contract coverage for concurrent different-thread admission, deterministic constrained-workspace blocking, and exact-lease-only release. This closes the prior gap where only mocked policy/client paths were tested.

## Lifecycle-first evidence

### User-visible symptom

Capacity-blocked work could be admitted inconsistently or appear as a provider failure.

### Full affected lifecycle

Chat request -> canonical identity validation -> persisted rate admission -> persisted concurrency lease -> Brain/RunEngine dispatch -> runtime terminal settlement -> exact lease release.

### Canonical owner

The Run Admission Durable Object owns persisted rate counters and leases; Brain runtime helpers only compute policy and transport typed decisions.

### Violated invariant

A blocked run must not acquire partial ownership or use provider-failure semantics; a terminal run attempt must settle only its own lease.

### Architectural root cause

The prior service was a disabled no-op with client-fingerprint fallback, and its limiter contract did not expose run-attempt-owned capacity decisions.

### Duplicate authority or fallback removed

Removed the no-op admission path, old service-layer owner, and client-fingerprint fallback. No legacy path is retained.

### Boundary regression test

Focused Durable Object tests prove two threads can acquire within workspace policy, a constrained sibling is deterministically blocked, and releasing a non-owner does not free the occupying lease.

### Lifecycle/conformance regression test

Brain focused admission tests (8), Brain lint/typecheck, import-boundary, and rebuild-governance gates pass locally. Terminal-event lease-release integration is revalidated after the required 039.3 runtime settlement dependency lands.

## Proof

- Brain focused admission tests: 8 passed
- Brain lint and typecheck passed
- `pnpm check:boundaries` passed
- `pnpm gate:rebuild-governance` passed (24 migration-safety and 13 governance tests)
- `git diff --check` passed

## Merge independence

This PR is otherwise independent of 039.4/039.5 secure API and of Web slices; it does not modify ExecutionService, secure API, or Web.

## Remaining integration

Hard dependency: PR #392 (039.3 runtime interrupt and terminal settlement) must merge first. This PR must then be refreshed against `dev` without rewriting history, and terminal-event lease-release integration revalidated. Do not merge while #392 is open.

## Temporary mechanism deletion criteria

None. No fallback, compatibility lane, or temporary admission mechanism is retained.

## Risks / rollback

Forward-only: missing canonical identities now fail explicitly. Revert the two PR commits only if emergency rollback is required; doing so restores the unsafe no-op/fallback behavior.

## Red-flag evidence

This reduces the admission portion of RF-032: capacity is persisted and typed instead of being mislabelled as a provider failure. It does not close RF-032, RF-008, RF-017, or RF-027; secure-run isolation, control-plane separation, contextual action routing, and broader policy consolidation remain owned by their respective slices.'

Implement LLD 039.6: durable, canonical Brain run admission that distinguishes blocked capacity from provider failures.

## Architecture decision

- The Run Admission Durable Object is the single persisted owner of rate counters and concurrency leases.
- Admission policy requires canonical user, workspace, thread, and run-attempt identities; no client-fingerprint fallback remains.
- The exact run-attempt owns its idempotent lease. `RUN_ADMISSION_BLOCKED` carries typed admission metadata rather than provider semantics.
- Policy, transport, and orchestration are focused runtime collaborators.

## Changed / deleted paths

Changed: controller integration, `RunAdmissionLimiter`, admission policy/client/service collaborators, focused runtime tests, and policy inventory.

Deleted: legacy service-layer admission implementation/tests and fingerprint scope helper/tests.

## Review repair

Added direct Durable Object contract coverage for concurrent different-thread admission, deterministic constrained-workspace blocking, and exact-lease-only release. This closes the prior gap where only mocked policy/client paths were tested.

## Lifecycle-first evidence

### User-visible symptom

Capacity-blocked work could be admitted inconsistently or appear as a provider failure.

### Full affected lifecycle

Chat request -> canonical identity validation -> persisted rate admission -> persisted concurrency lease -> Brain/RunEngine dispatch -> runtime terminal settlement -> exact lease release.

### Canonical owner

The Run Admission Durable Object owns persisted rate counters and leases; Brain runtime helpers only compute policy and transport typed decisions.

### Violated invariant

A blocked run must not acquire partial ownership or use provider-failure semantics; a terminal run attempt must settle only its own lease.

### Architectural root cause

The prior service was a disabled no-op with client-fingerprint fallback, and its limiter contract did not expose run-attempt-owned capacity decisions.

### Duplicate authority or fallback removed

Removed the no-op admission path, old service-layer owner, and client-fingerprint fallback. No legacy path is retained.

### Boundary regression test

Focused Durable Object tests prove two threads can acquire within workspace policy, a constrained sibling is deterministically blocked, and releasing a non-owner does not free the occupying lease.

### Lifecycle/conformance regression test

Brain focused admission tests (8), Brain lint/typecheck, import-boundary, and rebuild-governance gates pass locally. Terminal-event lease-release integration is revalidated after the required 039.3 runtime settlement dependency lands.

## Proof

- Brain focused admission tests: 8 passed
- Brain lint and typecheck passed
- `pnpm check:boundaries` passed
- `pnpm gate:rebuild-governance` passed (24 migration-safety and 13 governance tests)
- `git diff --check` passed

## Merge independence

This PR is otherwise independent of 039.4/039.5 secure API and of Web slices; it does not modify ExecutionService, secure API, or Web.

## Remaining integration

Hard dependency: PR #392 (039.3 runtime interrupt and terminal settlement) must merge first. This PR must then be refreshed against `dev` without rewriting history, and terminal-event lease-release integration revalidated. Do not merge while #392 is open.

## Temporary mechanism deletion criteria

None. No fallback, compatibility lane, or temporary admission mechanism is retained.

## Risks / rollback

Forward-only: missing canonical identities now fail explicitly. Revert the two PR commits only if emergency rollback is required; doing so restores the unsafe no-op/fallback behavior.

## Red-flag evidence

This reduces the admission portion of RF-032: capacity is persisted and typed instead of being mislabelled as a provider failure. It does not close RF-032, RF-008, RF-017, or RF-027; secure-run isolation, control-plane separation, contextual action routing, and broader policy consolidation remain owned by their respective slices.'

- One runtime/plugin registry is held per workspace/run-attempt; distinct workspaces never share mutable plugin state.
- Serialized leases share a workspace mutation queue; explicit read-only leases may run concurrently.
- Active entries and cancellation use `(leaseId, taskId)` only.
- `sandbox_unavailable` is a typed execution status. Exit 137 releases the matching lease; the API emits 503 and persists exactly one replacement lease.
- Readiness is awaited before task execution. A 15-minute bounded lease matches Cloudflare Sandbox ephemeral lifecycle guidance; replacements are capped at one generation.

Capacity-blocked work could be admitted inconsistently or appear as a provider failure.

Chat request -> canonical identity validation -> persisted rate admission -> persisted concurrency lease -> Brain/RunEngine dispatch -> runtime terminal settlement -> exact lease release.

The Run Admission Durable Object owns persisted rate counters and leases; Brain runtime helpers only compute policy and transport typed decisions.

### Violated invariant

A blocked run must not acquire partial ownership or use provider-failure semantics; a terminal run attempt must settle only its own lease.

The prior service was a disabled no-op with client-fingerprint fallback, and its limiter contract did not expose run-attempt-owned capacity decisions.

Focused Durable Object tests prove two threads can acquire within workspace policy, a constrained sibling is deterministically blocked, and releasing a non-owner does not free the occupying lease.

# Entire CLI — repository instructions

Go CLI built with Cobra and Charmbracelet Huh. `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this
file. Keep this entry point short: repo-wide rules and pointers, not command
catalogs, implementation histories, or subsystem specifications.

## Project map

- `cmd/entire/`: entry point and external-command dispatch.
- `cmd/entire/cli/`: Cobra commands, group roots, and CLI helpers. Group/verb files
  use `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`: built-in agent integrations and external-agent protocol.
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/`: manual-commit strategy and lifecycle/git hooks.
- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`: persistent checkpoint storage (written at commit).
- `cmd/entire/cli/session/`: session state shared across worktrees.
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`: simulated-hook integration tests.
- `e2e/`: real-agent tests and deterministic Vogon canary.
- `internal/entireclient/`: API clients, authentication, and user directories.

Use the Go version pinned by `go.mod` and tools configured in `mise.toml`.
For installed CLI usage, run `entire agent-help`, then
`entire agent-help <command>` for current flags; do not guess from a static list.

## Read when relevant

Read the applicable reference **before changing that area**, not every reference
at session start. Follow its related links when the task crosses those boundaries.

| Area being changed | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Commands, help, experimental visibility, repo refs, prompts | [CLI conventions](docs/development/cli-conventions.md) |
| Test harnesses, isolation, TTY behavior, source guards | [Testing](docs/development/testing.md) |
| Filesystem I/O, `.entire`, symlinks, hook configs, root anchors | [Filesystem safety](docs/development/filesystem-safety.md) |
| Git operations, executable lookup, subprocesses, Windows launching | [Git and subprocess safety](docs/development/git-safety.md) |
| Caller identification or session current/tokens/adopt | [Caller-session resolution](docs/development/caller-session-resolution.md) |
| Control-plane auth or data-plane routing | [API routing](docs/development/api-routing.md) |
| Checkpoint writes, lifecycle, sync, settings trust, redaction | [Implementation contracts](docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md), [domain model](docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md), [scenarios](docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md) |
| Ref-based checkpoint backend | [Ref backend](docs/architecture/ref-checkpoint-backend.md) |
| Agent integrations | [Agent guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md), [integration checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) |
| External commands or agents | [External commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md), [agent protocol](docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) |
| Security, privacy, scanners | [Security and privacy](docs/security-and-privacy.md), [implementation contracts](docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md) |
| Review command | [Review architecture](docs/architecture/review-command.md) |
| Release artifacts, install scripts, version-check origins | [Release origins](docs/architecture/release-origins.md) |
| E2E tests | [E2E guide](e2e/README.md) |
| Complexity/coverage measurement and the CI complexity gate | [Complexity tooling](tools/complexity/README.md) |

## Verification

| Task | Command / requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Unit tests | `mise run test` |
| Integration tests | `mise run test:integration`; required when changing integration test code |
| Deterministic E2E canary | `mise run test:e2e:canary`; safe without API calls |
| All CI tests | `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + canary) |
| Format and lint | `mise run fmt && mise run lint` |
| Before every commit | **`mise run check`** (format, lint, all CI tests) |
| Before any push or remote code update | **`mise run lint` on the current tree**, after the latest formatting pass |
| After every push to an open PR | **check the trail's findings** (`entire trail finding list cli/<n> --freshness any`; `<n>` is the PR branch's cli trail number, not the PR number); fix real ones, resolve with `-m`, and re-check after the fix lands. Not done until findings are clear |
| Duplication checks | `mise run dup` or `mise run dup:staged`; normal lint also checks duplication |
| Complexity gate | `mise run complexity:gate`; CI fails a PR on functions over cognitive complexity 30 that are new or worsened against the merge base. The threshold is a gate flag (`COGNIT_WARN`), not a `.golangci.yaml` setting |
| Windows installer | `mise run test:ps1`; see testing reference for prerequisites |

**Do not run real-agent E2E tests unless the user explicitly requests them.** They
make paid API calls. Vogon is the exception: its canary is deterministic and free.
When changing E2E prompt wording, run the canary and update Vogon's regex parsing
if needed. Formatting can rewrite files; an earlier lint pass is not sufficient.

Before implementing Go code, search nearby packages and helpers for reusable
patterns. Use `/go:discover-related` when available, otherwise `rg` and related
implementations/tests. Check `.golangci.yaml`; handle errors and avoid duplication.

## Test safety

- Every top-level test and subtest calls `t.Parallel()` unless it changes
  process-global state (`t.Chdir`, `t.Setenv`, or their `os` equivalents).
- Git tests use isolated temporary repositories, preferably
  `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` plus its file/add/commit helpers. Redirect CWD before
  calling CWD-based handlers. Never mutate the real checkout's git/session state.
- Tests must not access the developer's real config, cache, or keychain.
  In-process fallbacks are shared per process; use per-test overrides and
  `tokenstore.UseFileBackendForTesting` when isolation between tests is needed.
  Tests that can reach the OS keyring need `keyring.MockInit()` in `TestMain`.
- Spawned binaries do not inherit Go's test detection. Harnesses must isolate
  `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`,
  `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, and `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE`.
- Prefer `execx.NonInteractive` for real CLI/git test subprocesses so a developer's
  terminal cannot make them prompt or hang.
- Caller-resolution tests clear every variable from `agent.CallerSessionEnvVars()`;
  never hand-maintain a partial list or inherit the developer's agent identity.
- Source-scanning guards discover files through testutil's guard helpers
  (`GitGrepGuard`, `GuardGoFiles`), restrict pathspecs to Go files, and fail on
  zero matches. Do not weaken guard ledgers to silence failures.

## Filesystem and settings safety

**Use the existing anchor for each tree; never assemble a path and perform bare
I/O beneath it.** Read the filesystem reference before adding or changing I/O.

| Tree | Canonical owner |
| --- | --- |
| `.entire` | `entiredir` |
| Git common directory | `gitdir` |
| Working tree | `worktreedir` |
| Agent hook configuration | `agent.HookConfigFile` |
| Agent session store | `agent.SessionStore` |
| Active git hooks directory | `strategy.hooksRootForInstall` / `ForRemoval` |
| Per-user config/cache | `userdirs.ConfigRoot` / `CacheRoot` |
| Managed plugins | `pluginRoot` |

- Root bases come from trusted resolvers, **not `filepath.Dir(target)`**. Confining
  a file to its own derived parent proves nothing. Prefer an existing anchor.
- Roots share the `osroot.Shared` registry. Open child roots with
  `osroot.SharedChild` / `OpenChild`, not bare `parent.OpenRoot`.
- Use `osroot` operations and `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn` / `CreateTempIn`.
  Directories use `MkdirAllNoSymlink`; rooted read-only operations must also
  enforce symlink policy. Atomic writes replace leaf links rather than follow them.
- `.entire` must be a real directory; validate through
  `paths.ValidateEntireDirAt` / `RequireEntireDir`. Do not treat an unresolved
  repository as absent. Settings reads must also refuse symlinks themselves.
- Do not broaden symlink exceptions. Developer-vouched agent config directories
  are scoped, locally trusted exceptions; `.entire` and git hooks are not vouchable.
- `entiredir.OpenForRead` must not create directories. Reset cached roots before
  deleting/recreating their directories. Use `entiredir.Name` / `MustName` to
  bridge repo-relative constants and root-relative I/O names.
- All settings access goes through `settings`; never read or parse settings JSON
  ad hoc. Per-user config/cache resolution belongs only to `userdirs`.
- Repository-controlled settings must not authorize executable discovery, custom
  executables, or instructions for permission-bypassed agents. Preserve the
  existing local-provenance gates and their rejection reporting.
- Existing exceptions (explicit user paths, global git config, transcript-read
  protocol gaps) are documented in the references; do not generalize them.

## Git and subprocess safety

- Open repositories only through `gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)` or
  `gitrepo.OpenPath(root)`, never direct go-git opens. This preserves alternates
  and reftable support. Do not fall back to CWD after failed repo resolution.
- Use `gitrepo.Status`, never `worktree.Status()`. Agent-hook capture paths use
  `StatusWithBudget` and preserve degraded-capture reporting on budget exhaustion.
- Every `git status` subprocess passes **`--no-optional-locks`**. This does not
  protect worktree-comparing `git diff` from refreshing the index; use the
  hook-safe alternatives in the git reference.
- Use the git CLI, not go-git v5, for checkout and hard reset; go-git can delete
  ignored/untracked directories. This is an implementation rule, not permission
  to run destructive git commands.
- Git-relative paths resolve against `paths.WorktreeRoot`, never process CWD.
- A git subprocess targeting a repository independently of the current hook must
  use `gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides()`; `Dir` or `-C` alone does not override
  inherited selectors. Queries inspecting the commit Git is preparing must retain
  the hook environment, including its temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. Hook queries
  reading only the hook's own refs or reflog may strip selectors and resolve from
  `paths.WorktreeRoot`. User-invoked CWD commands also honor intentionally
  exported repo selectors.
- PATH scanners use `execx.PathScanDirs()`; external-agent execution requires
  absolute binary paths. User-directory overrides use the checked `userdirs`
  resolvers before any I/O.
- When Entire owns execution, pass arguments separately; never interpolate
  dynamic values into `cmd.exe`. Agent-owned shell execution uses the shared
  escaping helper. See the reference for the literal-only Unix updater exception.

## CLI behavior and output

- Load settings through the `settings` package, not new helpers in CLI consumers.
- Operational/debug messages use `logging.Debug/Info/Warn/Error`; user output uses
  `cmd.OutOrStdout()` / `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. Never log prompts, file contents, or
  commit messages; log operational metadata only.
- Cobra suppresses errors globally; `main.go` prints returned errors. Return
  `NewSilentError(err)` only after printing a custom error yourself.
- Every read-only workflow must work without a TUI: provide complete text/JSON,
  stable IDs and detail commands, or direct selection flags. Test that path.
- Use `uiform.New` (or `NewAccessibleForm` in `cli`) for Huh forms; these wire
  accessibility and theming centrally. Do not hand-roll `WithAccessible`.
- Separately opened prompt terminals use `interactive.OpenPromptTTY()` and
  `PromptTTY.Close()`, not a bare file close (Windows pending reads can hang).
- Register experimental commands with `experimental.Register`. Classify new
  commands in `agentHelpClassification`; default to unlisted/user-owned and
  flag the product choice for review. Agent guidance belongs in `agentHelpGuidance`,
  not Cobra `Short`/`Long` or first-turn injection.

## Session, checkpoint, and API contracts

- `*strategy.ManualCommitStrategy` is the only strategy; there is no interface or
  worktree restore path. Turn ends write session state only; checkpoints are
  metadata refs written at commit, never working-branch commits. Log resume is distinct from restoring worktree files.
- Caller identity comes from `strategy.ResolveCallerSession`, not newest state.
  Preserve resolution provenance; do not narrate worktree fallback or ambiguous
  matches as identified callers. `IsCaller()` excludes those guesses; consult
  the caller-resolution reference for current enforcement gaps.
- Preserve sanitize → image externalization → redact ordering where all apply,
  fail-closed scanner behavior, and checkpoint-scoped token accounting. Read the
  implementation contracts before modifying any transcript/storage pipeline.
- Control-plane precedence belongs to `coreapi`; display `client.CoreOrigin()`
  rather than independently resolving a possibly different target.
- Repo-scoped data-plane requests resolve the repo's cell and fail on resolution
  failure. `/me` uses the home cell; repo-set queries use shared fanout helpers.
  Multi-cell operations share one `auth.CellClientFactory` per operation.

## Maintaining these instructions

Update the relevant reference when subsystem behavior changes. Update this file
only for repository-wide development rules or routing links. Preserve safety
contracts in references and regression tests rather than accumulating incident
narratives here. Prefer existing docs over a second account of the same behavior.

The root-file budget is **20 KiB**, enforced alongside local documentation links
by `go test ./docs/development`. Extract specialized material instead of expanding
that budget. Do not require every linked document
to be loaded on every task. Keep `AGENTS.md` as the symlink to this file.

## Status and evidence rules

- **OURS / PR OPEN**: we implemented it and have a public PR. This does not mean merged or accepted.
- **REPRODUCED**: a focused failing safety-contract test exists at the recorded revision. Test-only work is not an implemented fix.
- **BENCHMARKED**: current cost was measured; no optimized implementation or speedup is implied.
- **SOURCE CHECKED**: affected source was inspected; no fresh runtime reproduction is claimed for that date.
- **TAKEN**: an explicit claim, prototype or PR exists. An issue does not become available merely because GitHub shows no linked PR.
- **COORDINATE**: related work or a reporter-led proposal exists; it is not proof someone fixed the exact defect.
- **DESIGN / UNCONFIRMED**: a proposal or disputed hypothesis, not a confirmed bug.
- **SKIP / DROPPED / OBSOLETE**: retain the reason; do not rediscover and recommend it as new.

“No exact public match found” is limited to the searches documented in the evidence reports. It is not a reservation, assignment, maintainer approval or proof of no private work. Public GitHub association is not employment verification. Local IDs are stable tracker IDs, not GitHub issue numbers.
